herb/agnikarna.to: - Prasava-janana (labor induction): used in classical practice as a uterine stimulant to induce labor. This use is dangerous. Colchicine is a known uterine stimulant, and use is strictly contraindicated without medical supervision.

herb/agnikarna.from: - Anthelmintic (Krimighna) - supported by in vitro studies showing antiparasitic activity
herb/agnikarna.to: - Krimighna (anthelmintic): traditionally used against worms. In vitro studies have reported antiparasitic activity.

herb/ahiphena.from: - **[Analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) and pain management.** Morphine remains the gold standard analgesic in modern medicine. WHO Essential Medicines List includes morphine for moderate to severe pain. Multiple systematic reviews confirm efficacy for cancer pain, post-surgical pain, and chronic pain management.
herb/ahiphena.to: - **[Analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) use.** Traditionally used for pain. Morphine, derived from opium, is used as an analgesic in modern medicine. The WHO Essential Medicines List includes morphine for moderate to severe pain. Systematic reviews have reported analgesic activity of morphine in cancer pain, post-surgical pain, and chronic pain.

herb/ahiphena.from: - **Anti-diarrheal (Atisara/Pravahika).** Codeine and morphine's constipating effect via mu-receptor-mediated GI motility reduction is well-established. Loperamide (Imodium), a synthetic opioid derivative, is the standard OTC anti-diarrheal, validating the traditional use of opium for dysentery and diarrhea in Ayurveda.
herb/ahiphena.to: - **Anti-diarrheal (Atisara/Pravahika).** Traditionally used in Ayurveda for dysentery and diarrhea. Codeine and morphine are known to cause constipation by reducing gut motility through mu-receptors. Loperamide (Imodium), a synthetic opioid derivative, is a common OTC anti-diarrheal.

herb/ahiphena.from: - **Antitussive (cough suppressant - Kasa).** Codeine remains widely prescribed as an antitussive. Noscapine (narcotine) from opium is a non-addictive cough suppressant available OTC in many countries. WHO acknowledges codeine as effective antitussive.
herb/ahiphena.to: - **Antitussive (cough suppressant - Kasa).** Traditionally used for Kasa (cough). Codeine is widely prescribed as an antitussive. Noscapine (narcotine) from opium is a non-addictive cough suppressant sold OTC in many countries. WHO recognizes codeine as an antitussive.

herb/amlaparni.from: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) and hypoglycemic activity validated through in vivo studies confirming traditional Ayurvedic use of Amlaparni for managing blood sugar levels
herb/amlaparni.to: - Amlaparni is traditionally used in Ayurveda in relation to blood sugar levels. In vivo studies have reported [antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) and hypoglycemic activity.

herb/amlaparni.from: - Wound healing properties confirmed in preclinical models consistent with traditional topical application for skin conditions and wound management in folk medicine
herb/amlaparni.to: - Traditionally applied topically in folk medicine for skin conditions and wounds. Preclinical studies have reported wound healing activity.

herb/amlaparni.from: - [Hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) effects demonstrated in animal models supporting traditional use for liver disorders
herb/amlaparni.to: - Traditionally used for liver disorders. Animal studies have reported [hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) effects.

herb/akika-pishti.from: - Pitta disorders (heat, inflammation, irritability): The cooling mineral composition of silica-based agate provides mechanistic rationale for Pitta-pacifying claims, though rigorous clinical validation is lacking
herb/akika-pishti.to: - Pitta disorders (heat, inflammation, irritability): traditionally used to pacify Pitta. Agate is a silica-based mineral described as cooling. Rigorous clinical studies are lacking.

herb/akika-pishti.from: - Cardiac conditions and bleeding disorders: Trace mineral content (iron, magnesium, calcium) provides partial mechanistic support, but no controlled clinical trials specifically validate these indications
herb/akika-pishti.to: - Cardiac conditions and bleeding disorders: traditionally used for these conditions. Agate contains trace minerals such as iron, magnesium and calcium. No controlled clinical trials have looked at these uses specifically.

herb/aivana.from: - Cognitive enhancement and memory improvement validated through placebo-controlled clinical trials showing improved immediate and delayed recall in elderly subjects
herb/aivana.to: - Placebo-controlled clinical studies in elderly subjects have reported improved immediate and delayed recall.

herb/aivana.from: - Antimicrobial activity against oral pathogens and skin infections confirmed through in vitro studies supporting traditional use for throat infections and wound healing
herb/aivana.to: - Traditionally used for throat infections and wounds. In vitro studies have reported antimicrobial activity against oral pathogens and pathogens linked to skin infections.

herb/aivana.from: - Hypoglycemic effects validated in preclinical models supporting traditional Ayurvedic/European use for metabolic disorders
herb/aivana.to: - Traditionally used in Ayurvedic and European practice for metabolic disorders. Preclinical studies have reported hypoglycemic effects.

herb/akarakarabha.from: - Aphrodisiac and male fertility enhancer ([Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana)) - validated through studies showing increased testosterone and sperm parameters in animal models
herb/akarakarabha.to: - [Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana): traditionally used as an aphrodisiac and for male fertility. Animal studies have reported increased testosterone and improved sperm parameters.

herb/akarakarabha.from: - Oral health and toothache remedy (Dantavedanashaka) - confirmed analgesic properties of pellitorine on nerve endings
herb/akarakarabha.to: - Dantavedanashaka: traditionally used for oral health and toothache. Studies have reported analgesic activity of pellitorine on nerve endings.

herb/akarakarabha.from: - Cognitive enhancer and nervine tonic (Medhya) - supported by neuropharmacological studies showing memory enhancement
herb/akarakarabha.to: - Medhya: traditionally used as a cognitive and nervine tonic. Neuropharmacological studies have reported memory enhancement.

herb/akarakarabha.from: - Anti-inflammatory and anti-rheumatic - validated by in vivo anti-inflammatory studies
herb/akarakarabha.to: - Inflammatory and rheumatic conditions: traditionally used for inflammation and rheumatic complaints. In vivo studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/ajwain.from: - Carminative and anti-flatulence activity - validated through multiple pharmacological studies showing [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) effects on gastrointestinal smooth muscle
herb/ajwain.to: - Traditionally used as a carminative and for flatulence. Pharmacological studies have reported [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) effects on gastrointestinal smooth muscle.

herb/ajwain.from: - Treatment of dyspepsia and digestive disorders - confirmed by modern research demonstrating enhanced digestive enzyme secretion
herb/ajwain.to: - Traditionally used for dyspepsia and digestive disorders. Studies have reported increased digestive enzyme secretion.

herb/ajwain.from: - Bronchodilatory and antitussive use for respiratory conditions - validated by studies showing tracheal smooth muscle relaxation
herb/ajwain.to: - Traditionally used for respiratory conditions as a bronchodilator and for cough. Studies have reported relaxation of tracheal smooth muscle.

herb/ajwain.from: - Antimicrobial use for intestinal parasites and infections - confirmed by in vitro studies against multiple pathogens
herb/ajwain.to: - Traditionally used for intestinal parasites and infections. In vitro studies have reported antimicrobial activity against multiple pathogens.

herb/ajwain.from: - Use as [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) for abdominal and dental pain - supported by antinociceptive studies in animal models
herb/ajwain.to: - Traditionally used as an [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) for abdominal and dental pain. Animal studies have reported antinociceptive effects.

herb/akhuparni.from: - Epilepsy and seizure management (Apasmara) - partially validated through anticonvulsant studies; leaf powder traditionally used as snuff during seizures
herb/akhuparni.to: - Epilepsy and seizures (Apasmara): traditionally used for epilepsy and seizures, with the leaf powder used as snuff during seizures. Studies have reported anticonvulsant activity.

herb/akhuparni.from: - [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) and kidney remedy (Mutrala) - supported by diuretic and nephroprotective pharmacological data
herb/akhuparni.to: - [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) and kidney remedy (Mutrala): traditionally used as a diuretic and kidney remedy. Pharmacological studies have reported diuretic and nephroprotective activity.

herb/akhuparni.from: - Fever reduction (Jvarahara) - confirmed [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity in preclinical models
herb/akhuparni.to: - Fever reduction (Jvarahara): traditionally used to reduce fever. Preclinical studies have reported [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity.

herb/akhuparni.from: - [Hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) (Yakrit Roga) - validated through studies showing liver protection against chemical toxins
herb/akhuparni.to: - [Hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) (Yakrit Roga): traditionally used for liver conditions. Studies have reported liver protection against chemical toxins.

herb/alabu.from: - Cardiotonic and heart-protective (Hridya) - validated through preclinical studies showing cholesterol and triglyceride reduction
herb/alabu.to: - Cardiotonic and heart-protective (Hridya): traditionally used to support the heart. Preclinical studies have reported reductions in cholesterol and triglycerides.

herb/alabu.from: - Cooling and [diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) (Sheetala, Mutrala) - confirmed diuretic properties in pharmacological studies
herb/alabu.to: - Cooling and [diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) (Sheetala, Mutrala): traditionally used as a cooling and diuretic herb. Pharmacological studies have reported diuretic activity.

herb/alabu.from: - Hepatoprotective (Yakrit-shodhana) - validated against drug-induced liver toxicity in animal models
herb/alabu.to: - Hepatoprotective (Yakrit-shodhana): traditionally used to protect the liver. Animal studies have reported protection against drug-induced liver toxicity.

herb/alabu.from: - Anti-obesity and weight management - confirmed antihyperlipidemic and anti-obesity effects in multiple studies
herb/alabu.to: - Obesity: traditionally used for weight reduction. Several studies have reported antihyperlipidemic and anti-obesity effects.

herb/aja-dugdha-goat-milk.from: - Rajayakshma (tuberculosis/wasting diseases): Validated by modern evidence showing [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) peptides and easily absorbable nutrients support recovery in debilitated patients
herb/aja-dugdha-goat-milk.to: - Rajayakshma (tuberculosis/wasting diseases): traditionally used in debilitated patients with wasting conditions. Studies have reported [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) peptides and easily absorbable nutrients in goat milk.

herb/aja-dugdha-goat-milk.from: - Raktapitta (bleeding disorders): Cooling potency and [hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic) properties confirmed through traditional clinical observation; modern studies support its role in reducing Pitta-related inflammation
herb/aja-dugdha-goat-milk.to: - Raktapitta (bleeding disorders): traditionally used for its cooling potency and [hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic) properties. Studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/aja-dugdha-goat-milk.from: - Pediatric nutrition and cow milk allergy: A2 beta-casein and lower allergenicity scientifically validated as a suitable alternative for children with cow milk protein intolerance
herb/aja-dugdha-goat-milk.to: - Pediatric nutrition and cow milk allergy: used as an alternative milk for children with cow milk protein intolerance. Studies have reported A2 beta-casein and lower allergenicity.

herb/akshotaka.from: - Ellagic acid and gallic acid [polyphenols](/glossary/compounds-o-q/#polyphenols) inhibit NF-kB signaling and reduce COX-2/LOX expression, providing anti-inflammatory effects validated in multiple in vivo models
herb/akshotaka.to: - Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory effects of the [polyphenols](/glossary/compounds-o-q/#polyphenols) ellagic acid and gallic acid. These studies reported inhibition of NF-kB signaling and reduced COX-2/LOX expression.

herb/akshotaka.from: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) effects validated through clinical and preclinical studies showing improved glycemic control consistent with traditional Ayurvedic use of Akshotaka for Prameha (diabetes)
herb/akshotaka.to: - Akshotaka is traditionally used in Ayurveda for Prameha (diabetes). Clinical and preclinical studies have reported [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) effects, including improved glycemic control.

herb/akshotaka.from: - Anti-inflammatory and wound healing properties confirmed through in vitro and in vivo studies supporting traditional topical application of walnut bark and leaf preparations
herb/akshotaka.to: - Walnut bark and leaf preparations are traditionally applied to the skin. In vitro and animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory and wound healing activity.

herb/akshotaka.from: - [Neuroprotective](/reference/neuroprotective/) and cognitive benefits validated through clinical studies showing walnut consumption improves memory and cognitive function in elderly populations
herb/akshotaka.to: - Clinical studies have reported [Neuroprotective](/reference/neuroprotective/) and cognitive benefits. They linked walnut consumption to improved memory and cognitive function in elderly people.

herb/ambasthaki.from: - Antimalarial and [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) (Jvara-nashaka) - strongly validated through identification of active antiplasmodial [alkaloids](/glossary/compounds-1-a/#alkaloids)
herb/ambasthaki.to: - Antimalarial and [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) (Jvara-nashaka): traditionally used for fevers. Phytochemical studies have reported [alkaloids](/glossary/compounds-1-a/#alkaloids) with antiplasmodial activity.

herb/ambasthaki.from: - Menstrual regulation and uterine tonic (Artava-janana) - partially validated through smooth muscle studies
herb/ambasthaki.to: - Menstrual regulation and uterine tonic (Artava-janana): traditionally used to regulate menstruation and as a uterine tonic.

herb/ambasthaki.from: - Anti-inflammatory and antiarthritic (Shotha-hara) - confirmed through in vivo anti-inflammatory models
herb/ambasthaki.to: - Anti-inflammatory and antiarthritic (Shotha-hara): traditionally used for inflammation and arthritic conditions. Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/ambasthaki.from: - Snakebite antidote (Visha-nashaka) - partially validated through antivenom studies in folk medicine
herb/ambasthaki.to: - Snakebite antidote (Visha-nashaka): traditionally used in folk medicine as an antidote for snakebite.

herb/ambasthaki.from: Identified and quantified specific isoquinoline alkaloids responsible for the potent antiplasmodial (antimalarial) activity of the plant, validating traditional use against fevers.
herb/ambasthaki.to: A phytochemical study identified and quantified isoquinoline alkaloids in the plant and reported antiplasmodial (antimalarial) activity. The plant is traditionally used against fevers.

herb/ambasthaki.from: Comprehensive review documenting 54 phytomolecules isolated from the plant, primarily isoquinoline alkaloids, with validated antimalarial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer pharmacological activities.
herb/ambasthaki.to: A review documented phytomolecules isolated from the plant, mainly isoquinoline alkaloids. It summarized reported antimalarial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities from pharmacological studies.

herb/apamarga.from: - Kshara (alkaline preparation) for urinary calculi validated by in vitro lithotriptic activity and renal stone dissolution studies
herb/apamarga.to: - Kshara (alkaline preparation): traditionally used for urinary calculi. In vitro studies have reported lithotriptic activity and renal stone dissolution.

herb/apamarga.from: - Anti-hemorrhoidal use confirmed by wound healing and anti-inflammatory effects in rectal tissue models
herb/apamarga.to: - Traditionally used for hemorrhoids. Studies in rectal tissue models have reported wound repair and anti-inflammatory effects.

herb/apamarga.from: - Diuretic action (Mutrala) validated through increased urine output and sodium excretion in animal studies
herb/apamarga.to: - Mutrala (diuretic): traditionally used to increase urine flow. Animal studies have reported increased urine output and sodium excretion.

herb/asthishrinkhala.from: - Bone fracture healing acceleration validated through human clinical trials and meta-analysis showing significant improvement in bone biomarkers, confirming premier Ayurvedic use as Asthi Sandhanaka (bone setter)
herb/asthishrinkhala.to: - Traditionally used as Asthi Sandhanaka (bone setter) for bone fractures. Clinical studies and a meta-analysis reported improvement in bone biomarkers.

herb/asthishrinkhala.from: - Anti-obesity and metabolic benefits validated through clinical studies showing weight and body fat reduction with CQR-300 extract supplementation
herb/asthishrinkhala.to: - Clinical studies have reported weight and body fat reduction with supplementation of an extract of the herb.

herb/asthishrinkhala.from: - Analgesic and anti-inflammatory properties validated through in vivo studies, confirming traditional use in pain management and musculoskeletal conditions
herb/asthishrinkhala.to: - Traditionally used for pain and musculoskeletal conditions. In vivo studies have reported analgesic and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/ankola.from: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) activity validated through in vivo studies showing significant blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) reduction consistent with traditional Ayurvedic use for Prameha (diabetes)
herb/ankola.to: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) activity: traditionally used for Prameha (diabetes) in Ayurveda. Animal studies have reported reductions in blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose).

herb/ankola.from: - Antiarthritic and anti-inflammatory properties confirmed in preclinical models supporting traditional use for joint pain and rheumatism (Amavata) in Ayurveda
herb/ankola.to: - Traditionally used in Ayurveda for joint pain and rheumatism (Amavata). Preclinical studies have reported antiarthritic and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/ankola.from: - Antivenomous properties (traditional use as snakebite remedy) partially validated through in vitro studies showing neutralization of venom phospholipase activity
herb/ankola.to: - Traditionally used as a snakebite remedy. In vitro studies have reported antivenom activity, including neutralization of venom phospholipase activity.

herb/asana.from: - Antidiabetic (Prameha) use validated through multiple preclinical studies and preliminary clinical trial confirming significant blood glucose reduction
herb/asana.to: - Prameha: traditionally used for diabetes. Preclinical studies and a preliminary clinical trial have reported lower blood glucose.

herb/asana.from: - Beta-cell regeneration by (-)-epicatechin validated in vitro and in STZ-induced diabetic models
herb/asana.to: - An in vitro study and STZ-induced diabetic animal models have reported beta-cell regeneration with (-)-epicatechin.

herb/asana.from: - Anti-inflammatory use confirmed through COX-2 selective inhibition studies
herb/asana.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation. Studies have reported selective COX-2 inhibition.

herb/asana.from: - Wound healing and anti-hemorrhagic use (kino gum) validated through astringent and [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) property studies
herb/asana.to: - Kino gum: traditionally used for wounds and bleeding. Studies have reported astringent and [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) properties.

herb/aragwadha.from: - Mild laxative (Mridu Virechana) validated by clinical trial showing comparable efficacy to lactulose in geriatric constipation
herb/aragwadha.to: - Mridu Virechana (mild laxative): traditionally used as a mild laxative. A clinical study in older adults with constipation reported results comparable to lactulose.

herb/aragwadha.from: - Skin disease treatment confirmed by [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and antifungal activity of leaf and bark extracts against dermatophytes
herb/aragwadha.to: - Traditionally used for skin diseases. Laboratory studies have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and antifungal activity of leaf and bark extracts against dermatophytes.

herb/aragwadha.from: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) use (Jwaraghna) supported by significant fever reduction in Brewer's yeast-induced pyrexia model
herb/aragwadha.to: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) use (Jwaraghna): traditionally used for fever. Animal studies have reported reduced fever in a Brewer's yeast-induced fever model.

herb/amra.from: - Antidiabetic use of bark and leaf decoctions validated through multiple preclinical studies and preliminary clinical observations
herb/amra.to: - Bark and leaf decoctions are traditionally used for diabetes. Preclinical studies and preliminary clinical observations have reported antidiabetic activity.

herb/amra.from: - Anti-diarrheal and dysentery treatment validated through [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity and astringent tannin effects in animal models
herb/amra.to: - Traditionally used for diarrhea and dysentery. Animal studies have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity and astringent effects of tannins.

herb/amra.from: - Oral health use (bark decoction as mouthwash) validated through antimicrobial activity against oral pathogens
herb/amra.to: - Bark decoction is traditionally used as a mouthwash for oral health. Studies have reported antimicrobial activity against oral pathogens.

herb/amra.from: - Anemia management supported by iron content in leaves and fruits and confirmed hematopoietic effects in deficient models
herb/amra.to: - Traditionally used for anemia. The leaves and fruits are reported to contain iron. Studies in deficient models have reported hematopoietic effects.

herb/amlavetasa.from: - Digestive stimulant and carminative (Deepana-Pachana) - validated through studies showing enhanced digestive enzyme activity
herb/amlavetasa.to: - Deepana-Pachana (digestive stimulant and carminative): traditionally used to stimulate digestion and as a carminative. Studies have reported increased digestive enzyme activity.

herb/amlavetasa.from: - Anti-obesity and lipid management (Medohara) - HCA-mediated lipogenesis inhibition confirmed in clinical studies on related Garcinia species
herb/amlavetasa.to: - Medohara (anti-obesity): traditionally used to reduce excess fat. Clinical studies on related Garcinia species have reported that HCA inhibits lipogenesis.

herb/amlavetasa.from: - Hepatoprotective (Yakrit-shodhana) - validated through preclinical studies demonstrating liver protection from chemical toxins
herb/amlavetasa.to: - Yakrit-shodhana (liver): traditionally used for the liver. Preclinical studies have reported protection of the liver from chemical toxins.

herb/amlavetasa.from: - Laxative (Bhedana) - confirmed for Rheum emodi through anthraquinone-mediated mechanisms
herb/amlavetasa.to: - Bhedana (laxative): traditionally used as a laxative. Research on Rheum emodi has reported laxative action linked to anthraquinones.

herb/ashwattha.from: answer: "Ashwattha (Ficus religiosa L.) is a plant drug, also called Asvatthah, Pippala and Pippalah, from the Moraceae family. coli, and Candida albicans validated via disc diffusion and MIC assays Listed in WHO Traditional Medicine Strategy as a plant used in traditional medicine systems; included in the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India."
herb/ashwattha.to: answer: "Ashwattha (Ficus religiosa L.) is a plant drug, also called Asvatthah, Pippala and Pippalah, from the Moraceae family. In vitro studies using disc diffusion and MIC assays have reported activity against E. coli and Candida albicans. Listed in WHO Traditional Medicine Strategy as a plant used in traditional medicine systems; included in the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India."

herb/ashwattha.from: - Antidiabetic activity confirmed in multiple in vivo studies showing significant blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) reduction in alloxan-induced diabetic models
herb/ashwattha.to: - Animal studies have reported lower blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) in alloxan-induced diabetic models.

herb/ashwattha.from: - Wound healing properties validated through preclinical studies demonstrating accelerated epithelialization and increased tensile strength
herb/ashwattha.to: - Preclinical studies have reported faster epithelialization and increased tensile strength in wound models.

herb/ashwattha.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects confirmed in carrageenan-induced paw edema and acetic acid-induced writhing models
herb/ashwattha.to: - Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects in carrageenan-induced paw edema and acetic acid-induced writhing models.

herb/ashwattha.from: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity against Staphylococcus aureus, E. coli, and Candida albicans validated via disc diffusion and MIC assays
herb/ashwattha.to: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity against Staphylococcus aureus, E. coli, and Candida albicans has been reported in in vitro studies using disc diffusion and MIC assays.

herb/ashoka.from: - Menorrhagia and metrorrhagia control (validated by clinical studies showing [hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic) and uterotonic effects)
herb/ashoka.to: - Menorrhagia and metrorrhagia: traditionally used for these conditions. Clinical studies have reported [hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic) and uterotonic effects.

herb/ashoka.from: - PCOS management (validated by 2023-2024 studies showing hormonal modulation and aromatase inhibition)
herb/ashoka.to: - PCOS: traditionally used in this context. Studies have reported hormonal modulation and aromatase inhibition.

herb/ashoka.from: - Antioxidant and skin health (validated by flavonoid-mediated free radical scavenging studies)
herb/ashoka.to: - Antioxidant and skin health: traditionally used for skin health. Studies have reported flavonoid-mediated free radical scavenging.

herb/ashoka.from: - Antipyretic action (validated by preclinical seed extract studies)
herb/ashoka.to: - Antipyretic action: traditionally used for fever. Preclinical studies of seed extract have reported antipyretic activity.

herb/ashoka.from: - Anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects (validated by COX-2 inhibition and cytokine modulation studies)
herb/ashoka.to: - Anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects: traditionally used for inflammation and pain. Studies have reported COX-2 inhibition and cytokine modulation.

herb/aparajita.from: - Memory enhancer and nootropic (Medhya [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)) - validated through multiple studies showing improved memory and learning in animal models via cholinergic mechanism
herb/aparajita.to: - Memory enhancer and nootropic (Medhya [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)): traditionally used to support memory and learning. Animal studies have reported improved memory and learning, with a cholinergic mechanism proposed.

herb/aparajita.from: - Anxiolytic and antidepressant (Unmada-nashaka) - confirmed anxiolytic and antidepressant effects comparable to standard drugs in preclinical studies
herb/aparajita.to: - Anxiolytic and antidepressant (Unmada-nashaka): traditionally used for anxious and low mood states. Preclinical studies have reported anxiolytic and antidepressant-like effects.

herb/aparajita.from: - Anti-diabetic (Pramehaghna) - validated through in vivo studies showing blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) reduction and improved insulin sensitivity
herb/aparajita.to: - Anti-diabetic (Pramehaghna): traditionally used for Prameha. In vivo studies have reported lower blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) and improved insulin sensitivity.

herb/aparajita.from: - Complexion enhancer and eye health (Varnya, [Chakshushya](/herb/chakshushya/)) - partially validated through antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms
herb/aparajita.to: - Complexion enhancer and eye health (Varnya, [Chakshushya](/herb/chakshushya/)): traditionally used for complexion and eye health.

herb/bhringraj.from: Network pharmacology and experimental validation confirmed Eclipta extract modulates the p53/Fas pathway, promoting hair matrix cell proliferation by inhibiting TGF-beta1 expression.
herb/bhringraj.to: A network pharmacology and experimental study reported that Eclipta extract modulated the p53/Fas pathway. It reported that the extract promoted hair matrix cell proliferation by inhibiting TGF-beta1 expression.

herb/bhadra.from: - Anti-urolithiasis (kidney stone dissolution) activity validated through in vivo and in vitro studies confirming traditional Ayurvedic use of [Pashanabheda](/herb/pashanabheda/) for Ashmari (urinary calculi)
herb/bhadra.to: - Traditionally used in Ayurveda, as with [Pashanabheda](/herb/pashanabheda/), for Ashmari (urinary calculi). In vivo and in vitro studies have reported anti-urolithiasis (kidney stone dissolution) activity.

herb/bhadra.from: - [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) activity confirmed through pharmacological studies supporting traditional use for strangury and urinary disorders in Ayurveda
herb/bhadra.to: - Traditionally used in Ayurveda for strangury and urinary disorders. [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) activity has been reported in pharmacological studies.

herb/bhadra.from: - Anti-asthmatic and bronchodilatory effects validated in preclinical models consistent with traditional use for respiratory conditions
herb/bhadra.to: - Traditionally used for respiratory conditions. Preclinical studies have reported anti-asthmatic and bronchodilatory effects.

herb/babbula.from: - Dental and oral hygiene use validated through antimicrobial activity against oral pathogens and gingival health studies (babool datun)
herb/babbula.to: - Traditionally used for dental and oral hygiene (babool datun). Studies have reported antimicrobial activity against oral pathogens.

herb/babbula.from: - Anti-diarrheal use confirmed through castor oil-induced diarrhea models and tannin-mediated astringent action
herb/babbula.to: - Traditionally used for diarrhea. Animal studies using castor oil-induced diarrhea models have reported anti-diarrheal activity, attributed to the astringent action of tannins.

herb/babbula.from: - Wound healing validated through antimicrobial, astringent and collagen synthesis promotion studies
herb/babbula.to: - Traditionally used for wounds. Studies have reported antimicrobial and astringent activity and promotion of collagen synthesis.

herb/babbula.from: - Antidiabetic use supported by alpha-amylase inhibition and hypoglycemic effects in preclinical studies
herb/babbula.to: - Traditionally used for diabetes. Preclinical studies have reported alpha-amylase inhibition and hypoglycemic effects.

herb/bharangi.from: - Anti-asthmatic use (Shwasa-Kasahara) validated through ovalbumin-induced asthma model showing reduction in bronchial inflammation and IgE
herb/bharangi.to: - Shwasa-Kasahara: traditionally used for asthma. Animal studies using an ovalbumin-induced asthma model have reported reduced bronchial inflammation and IgE.

herb/bharangi.from: - Anti-inflammatory use for joint disorders confirmed by significant inhibition of carrageenan-induced edema

herb/danti.to: - Anti-dropsy and edema (Shotha-hara): traditionally used for dropsy and edema. Studies have reported [diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/dadima-twak.from: - Pelletierine and isopelletierine [alkaloids](/glossary/compounds-1-a/#alkaloids) exhibit anthelmintic activity by paralyzing tapeworm musculature through nicotinic receptor agonism, validated since antiquity
herb/dadima-twak.to: - Pelletierine and isopelletierine [alkaloids](/glossary/compounds-1-a/#alkaloids) have been reported to have anthelmintic activity, paralyzing tapeworm musculature through nicotinic receptor agonism.

herb/dadima-twak.from: - Anthelmintic activity (against tapeworms) validated through identification of pelletierine alkaloids in rind, confirming traditional Ayurvedic use of [Dadima](/herb/dadima/) Twak for Krimi (intestinal parasites)
herb/dadima-twak.to: - [Dadima](/herb/dadima/) Twak is traditionally used in Ayurveda for Krimi (intestinal parasites), including tapeworms. Pelletierine alkaloids have been identified in the rind.

herb/dadima-twak.from: - Antidiarrhoeal properties validated through tannin-mediated astringent effects on intestinal mucosa, supporting traditional use for Atisara (diarrhea) and Pravahika (dysentery)
herb/dadima-twak.to: - Traditionally used for Atisara (diarrhea) and Pravahika (dysentery). Its tannins have been reported to have an astringent effect on the intestinal mucosa.

herb/dadima-twak.from: - Antimicrobial activity against oral pathogens and gastrointestinal bacteria confirmed, supporting traditional use of pomegranate rind decoction for Mukha Roga (oral diseases)
herb/dadima-twak.to: - Pomegranate rind decoction is traditionally used for Mukha Roga (oral diseases). Antimicrobial activity against oral pathogens and gastrointestinal bacteria has been reported.

herb/dhamasa.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) properties validated through COX inhibition studies and in vivo models, confirming traditional use in pain and inflammatory conditions
herb/dhamasa.to: - Traditionally used for pain and inflammatory conditions. COX inhibition studies and animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) activity.

herb/dhamasa.from: - [Anticancer](/reference/anticancer/)/cytotoxic activity validated against multiple cancer cell lines, supporting its extensive folk use as an anticancer remedy (particularly in Pakistan and India)
herb/dhamasa.to: - Traditionally used in folk practice as an anticancer remedy, particularly in Pakistan and India. In vitro studies have reported [Anticancer](/reference/anticancer/) and cytotoxic activity against multiple cancer cell lines.

herb/dhamasa.from: - Antithrombotic properties experimentally confirmed, supporting traditional use in blood-related disorders
herb/dhamasa.to: - Traditionally used for blood-related disorders. Experimental studies have reported antithrombotic activity.

herb/daruharidra.from: - Skin diseases and acne (Kushtha/Yauvanpidika): Validated by RCTs showing berberine-containing extracts effective against acne-causing pathogens (P. acnes, S. epidermidis) and inflammatory acne
herb/daruharidra.to: - Skin diseases and acne (Kushtha/Yauvanpidika): traditionally used for skin diseases and acne. Clinical studies have reported that berberine-containing extracts showed activity against acne-associated bacteria (P. acnes, S. epidermidis) and improvement in inflammatory acne.

herb/daruharidra.from: - Skin lightening and exfoliation (Varnya): Traditional scrub preparations validated by tyrosinase inhibition studies showing competitive enzyme inhibition
herb/daruharidra.to: - Skin lightening and exfoliation (Varnya): traditionally used in scrub preparations for skin lightening and exfoliation. In vitro studies have reported competitive inhibition of the enzyme tyrosinase.

herb/daruharidra.from: - Eye diseases with skin manifestation (Netra Roga): Traditional use supported by berberine's demonstrated broad [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and anti-inflammatory activity
herb/daruharidra.to: - Eye diseases with skin manifestation (Netra Roga): traditionally used for eye diseases with skin manifestation. Studies have reported broad [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and anti-inflammatory activity for berberine.

herb/daruharidra.from: - Wound healing (Vrana): Supported by berberine's anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial mechanisms promoting tissue repair
herb/daruharidra.to: - Wound healing (Vrana): traditionally used for wound healing. Studies have reported anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial activity for berberine.

herb/daruharidra.from: Berberis root extract combined with spearmint oil demonstrated significant clinical improvement in acne vulgaris patients in a randomized controlled trial, validating the anti-acne potential of berberine-containing plants.
herb/daruharidra.to: A randomized controlled trial reported significant clinical improvement in acne vulgaris patients given Berberis root extract combined with spearmint oil.

herb/dadhi.from: - Grahani (malabsorption/IBS): Probiotic restoration of gut flora and enhanced digestion scientifically validated as therapeutic for IBS, malabsorption, and chronic diarrhea
herb/dadhi.to: - Grahani (malabsorption/IBS): traditionally used for malabsorption, IBS-like complaints, and chronic diarrhea.

herb/dadhi.from: - Deepana-Pachana (appetizer and digestant): Lactic acid-mediated stimulation of gastric secretions and enzyme activity confirms traditional classification as a digestive stimulant
herb/dadhi.to: - Deepana-Pachana (appetizer and digestant): traditionally classified as a digestive stimulant.

herb/dadhi.from: - Aruchi (anorexia/loss of appetite): Sour taste stimulates salivary and gastric secretion reflex; probiotic metabolites improve gut-brain signaling for appetite regulation
herb/dadhi.to: - Aruchi (anorexia/loss of appetite): traditionally used for loss of appetite. Its sour taste is traditionally linked to stimulating appetite.

herb/dadhi.from: - Ayurvedic restriction against nighttime consumption validated: heavy, sour, and hot properties may exacerbate acid reflux and disturb sleep; increases Kapha when consumed at night
herb/dadhi.to: - Ayurvedic restriction against nighttime consumption: classical practice advises against eating it at night. Its heavy, sour, and hot properties are said to increase Kapha at night, and are described as possibly aggravating acid reflux and disturbing sleep.

herb/eranda-paka.from: - Laxative and purgative (Virechana) activity thoroughly validated through pharmacological studies confirming ricinoleic acid-mediated stimulation of intestinal motility, supporting core Ayurvedic indication
herb/eranda-paka.to: - Virechana (laxative and purgative): traditionally used as a laxative and purgative. Pharmacological studies have reported stimulation of intestinal motility linked to ricinoleic acid.

herb/eranda-paka.from: - Anti-arthritic and anti-rheumatic effects validated in preclinical models showing reduction of joint inflammation and pain, supporting traditional use for Amavata (rheumatoid conditions)
herb/eranda-paka.to: - Amavata (rheumatoid conditions): traditionally used for joint and rheumatic complaints. Preclinical studies have reported reduced joint inflammation and pain.

herb/eranda-paka.from: - Digestive stimulant (Deepana) activity confirmed through studies showing enhanced gastric motility and secretion when processed with jaggery
herb/eranda-paka.to: - Deepana (digestive stimulant): traditionally used to stimulate digestion. Studies have reported increased gastric motility and secretion when the herb was processed with jaggery.

herb/dhatri-loha.from: - Iron deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga) - validated in multiple clinical trials showing significant hemoglobin improvement (1.5-2 g/dL rise over 8 weeks)
herb/dhatri-loha.to: - Pandu Roga (iron deficiency anemia): traditionally used for this condition. Clinical studies have reported improvement in hemoglobin levels.

herb/dhatri-loha.from: - Digestive disorders with acid peptic symptoms - traditional use supported by the gastroprotective action of Amalaki and [Yashtimadhu](/herb/yashtimadhu/) components
herb/dhatri-loha.to: - Digestive disorders with acid peptic symptoms: traditionally used for these complaints. The formulation includes Amalaki and [Yashtimadhu](/herb/yashtimadhu/) as components.

herb/eranda.from: - Purgative (Virechana) activity validated by clinical use and EP3 receptor-mediated mechanism in intestinal smooth muscle
herb/eranda.to: - Virechana (purgation): traditionally used as a purgative. Studies have reported an EP3 receptor-mediated action on intestinal smooth muscle.

herb/eranda.from: - Anti-arthritic use (Vatahara) supported by anti-inflammatory activity of ricinoleic acid through PPAR-gamma activation
herb/eranda.to: - Vatahara: traditionally used for arthritic conditions. Studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity of ricinoleic acid through PPAR-gamma activation.

herb/eranda.from: - Wound healing use confirmed by [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity and promotion of granulation tissue formation in wound models
herb/eranda.to: - Traditionally used for wounds. Studies have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity and the promotion of granulation tissue formation in wound models.

herb/eranda-patra.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects validated in carrageenan-induced paw edema and acetic acid writhing models, supporting traditional Ayurvedic use of [Eranda](/herb/eranda/) Patra poultice for Vataroga (pain and inflammation)
herb/eranda-patra.to: - Traditionally used as an [Eranda](/herb/eranda/) Patra poultice for Vataroga (pain and inflammation). Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects in carrageenan-induced paw edema and acetic acid writhing models.

herb/eranda-patra.from: - Wound healing activity confirmed through in vivo studies showing enhanced granulation and epithelialization, supporting traditional topical application for Vrana (wounds)
herb/eranda-patra.to: - Traditionally applied topically for Vrana (wounds). In vivo studies have reported enhanced granulation and epithelialization of wounds.

herb/eranda-patra.from: - Antibacterial properties validated against multiple pathogenic bacteria, supporting traditional use for infectious conditions
herb/eranda-patra.to: - Traditionally used for infectious conditions. Antibacterial activity against several pathogenic bacteria has been reported.

herb/gambhari.from: - Anti-arthritic and anti-inflammatory use validated by 45% reduction in swelling in rodent arthritis models over 14 days
herb/gambhari.to: - Traditionally used for arthritic and inflammatory conditions. Animal studies in rodent arthritis models have reported reduced swelling.

herb/gambhari.from: - Cardiotonic use (Hridya) supported by cardioprotective activity through reduction of myocardial oxidative stress
herb/gambhari.to: - Hridya (cardiotonic): traditionally used as a heart tonic. Research has reported cardioprotective activity, with reduced myocardial oxidative stress.

herb/gambhari.from: - Wound healing use confirmed by promotion of fibroblast proliferation and collagen synthesis in excision wound models
herb/gambhari.to: - Traditionally used for wounds. Studies in excision wound models have reported increased fibroblast proliferation and collagen synthesis.

herb/drakshavaleha.from: - Pandu (anemia): clinical study shows highly significant (p<0.001) improvement in pregnancy-related anemia
herb/drakshavaleha.to: - Pandu (anemia): traditionally used for anemia. A clinical study reported improvement in pregnancy-related anemia.

herb/drakshavaleha.from: - Daurbalya (debility/weakness): nutritive and energy-providing properties support recovery from chronic debility
herb/drakshavaleha.to: - Daurbalya (debility/weakness): traditionally used for chronic debility, valued in classical practice for its nutritive and energy-providing properties.

herb/drakshavaleha.from: - Yakrit Roga (liver disorders): classical Ashtanga Hridaya indication for hepatic conditions supported by [hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) ingredient profiles
herb/drakshavaleha.to: - Yakrit Roga (liver disorders): used in classical practice for hepatic conditions, as indicated in the Ashtanga Hridaya. Its ingredient profile is described as [hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/).

herb/drakshavaleha.from: - Garbhini Paricharya (pregnancy care): fetal protection demonstrated against cyclophosphamide-induced toxicity in animal model
herb/drakshavaleha.to: - Garbhini Paricharya (pregnancy care): traditionally used in pregnancy care. An animal study reported fetal protection against cyclophosphamide-induced toxicity.

herb/gambhari-phala.from: - Raktasthambhaka ([hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic)/anti-hemorrhagic) activity partially validated; Charaka Samhita states '[Gambhari](/herb/gambhari/) fruit is best among substances useful in bleeding disorders' - supported by tannin and phenolic content
herb/gambhari-phala.to: - Raktasthambhaka ([hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic)/anti-hemorrhagic): traditionally used for bleeding disorders. Charaka Samhita describes [Gambhari](/herb/gambhari/) fruit as best among substances useful in bleeding disorders. The fruit is reported to contain tannins and phenolic compounds.

herb/gambhari-phala.from: - Brain tonic (Medhya) and nourishing properties supported by nutritional analysis showing significant protein, mineral, and vitamin content in fruit preparations
herb/gambhari-phala.to: - Medhya (brain tonic): traditionally used as a brain tonic and for nourishment. Nutritional analysis has reported protein, mineral, and vitamin content in fruit preparations.

herb/gambhari-phala.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects validated in preclinical models supporting traditional use for Shotha (inflammation) and Jwara (fever)
herb/gambhari-phala.to: - Shotha (inflammation) and Jwara (fever): traditionally used for these conditions. Preclinical studies have reported anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects.

herb/dhanyamla.from: - Anti-inflammatory therapy for musculoskeletal disorders (Dhanyamla Dhara) - validated through clinical observations showing pain reduction in arthritis and myalgia
herb/dhanyamla.to: - Dhanyamla Dhara: traditionally used for musculoskeletal disorders such as arthritis and myalgia. Clinical observations have reported reduced pain in arthritis and myalgia.

herb/dhanyamla.from: - Digestive stimulant (Deepana) - confirmed through appetite-enhancing and digestive enzyme-stimulating properties of fermented acids
herb/dhanyamla.to: - Deepana (digestive stimulant): traditionally used to stimulate appetite and digestion, an action attributed to its fermented acids.

herb/dhanyamla.from: - Obesity management (Sthoulya Chikitsa) - Lekhana (fat-scraping) property supported by lipid metabolism enhancement in clinical practice
herb/dhanyamla.to: - Sthoulya Chikitsa (obesity): used in classical practice for obesity, based on its Lekhana (fat-scraping) property.

herb/dhanyamla.from: - Neurological rehabilitation (Vata Vyadhi) - used in stroke rehabilitation through Dhara therapy with documented clinical improvements
herb/dhanyamla.to: - Vata Vyadhi (neurological disorders): traditionally used as Dhara therapy in stroke rehabilitation.

herb/gajapippali.from: answer: "Gajapippali (Scindapsus officinalis (Roxb.) Schott) is a plant drug, from the Araceae family. Respiratory disease treatment (Kasa-Shwasa) partially validated by expectorant activity of saponin-rich extracts Antipyretic use supported by traditional clinical evidence and preliminary pharmacological data Galactagogue use (breast milk improvement) remains to be validated through modern clinical studies"
herb/gajapippali.to: answer: "Gajapippali (Scindapsus officinalis (Roxb.) Schott) is a plant drug from the Araceae family. It is traditionally used for respiratory disease (Kasa-Shwasa). Research has reported expectorant activity in saponin-rich extracts. It is also traditionally used to lower fever, and as a galactagogue to improve breast milk. Modern clinical studies of the galactagogue use are still lacking."

herb/gajapippali.from: - Respiratory disease treatment (Kasa-Shwasa) partially validated by expectorant activity of saponin-rich extracts
herb/gajapippali.to: - Kasa-Shwasa (respiratory disease): traditionally used for respiratory disease. Research has reported expectorant activity in saponin-rich extracts.

herb/gajapippali.from: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) use supported by traditional clinical evidence and preliminary pharmacological data
herb/gajapippali.to: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) use: traditionally used to lower fever.

herb/gajapippali.from: - [Galactagogue](/glossary/pharmacology/#galactagogue) use (breast milk improvement) remains to be validated through modern clinical studies
herb/gajapippali.to: - [Galactagogue](/glossary/pharmacology/#galactagogue) use: traditionally used to improve breast milk. Modern clinical studies of this use are still lacking.

herb/ela.from: - Digestive aid for nausea, flatulence, and indigestion - confirmed by pharmacological studies showing carminative and [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) effects
herb/ela.to: - Traditionally used as a digestive aid for nausea, flatulence, and indigestion. Pharmacological studies have reported carminative and [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) effects.

herb/ela.from: - Respiratory relief for asthma and bronchitis - validated by studies demonstrating bronchodilatory effects of 1,8-cineole (eucalyptol)
herb/ela.to: - Traditionally used for asthma and bronchitis. Studies have reported bronchodilatory effects of 1,8-cineole (eucalyptol).

herb/ela.from: - Oral health for teeth and gum infections - confirmed by RCTs showing antibacterial and anti-inflammatory activity against periodontal pathogens
herb/ela.to: - Traditionally used for teeth and gum infections. Randomized clinical trials have reported antibacterial and anti-inflammatory activity against periodontal pathogens.

herb/ela.from: - Blood pressure lowering - validated by meta-analysis of RCTs showing significant reduction in both systolic and diastolic blood pressure
herb/ela.to: - Blood pressure: a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials reported reductions in systolic and diastolic blood pressure.

herb/ela.from: - Anti-inflammatory for metabolic disorders - confirmed by RCTs demonstrating significant reduction in TNF-alpha, hs-CRP, and IL-6
herb/ela.to: - Metabolic disorders: randomized clinical trials have reported reductions in TNF-alpha, hs-CRP, and IL-6.

herb/ela.from: Validated antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties of cardamom extracts with specific therapeutic potential for managing periodontal infections.
herb/ela.to: Studies have reported antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties of cardamom extracts, with possible relevance to periodontal infections.

herb/gomeda-bhasma.from: - Neurological disorders (epilepsy, insomnia, paralysis): Traditional indications documented through extensive clinical practice; mineral composition provides mechanistic plausibility for neuromodulation
herb/gomeda-bhasma.to: - Neurological disorders (epilepsy, insomnia, paralysis): traditionally used for these conditions in classical practice.

herb/gomeda-bhasma.from: - Cardiac arrhythmias and palpitation: Traditional use for heart rhythm disorders supported by mineral electrolyte effects on cardiac conduction
herb/gomeda-bhasma.to: - Cardiac arrhythmias and palpitation: traditionally used for heart rhythm disorders and palpitation.

herb/gomeda-bhasma.from: - Stress and mental clarity: Anxiolytic properties supported by traditional clinical observations, though formal clinical trials lacking
herb/gomeda-bhasma.to: - Stress and mental clarity: traditionally used to calm the mind and support mental clarity. Formal clinical trials are lacking.

herb/godanti-bhasma.from: - Fever (Jwara): Significant antipyretic activity demonstrated in yeast-induced fever model, validating traditional anti-fever indication
herb/godanti-bhasma.to: - Fever (Jwara): traditionally used for fever. Animal studies have reported antipyretic activity in a yeast-induced fever model.

herb/godanti-bhasma.from: - Peptic ulcer and gastritis (Amlapitta): 44-45% gastroprotection in experimental ulcer models validates traditional use for acid-related disorders
herb/godanti-bhasma.to: - Peptic ulcer and gastritis (Amlapitta): traditionally used for acid-related disorders. Animal studies have reported gastroprotective activity in experimental ulcer models.

herb/godanti-bhasma.from: - Calcium deficiency and bone disorders: Bioavailable calcium content supports traditional use for Asthi Kshaya (bone depletion) conditions
herb/godanti-bhasma.to: - Calcium deficiency and bone disorders: traditionally used for Asthi Kshaya (bone depletion) conditions. It has been reported to contain bioavailable calcium.

herb/giloy-satva.from: - Immunomodulatory ([Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)) properties extensively validated through multiple preclinical and clinical studies, confirming premier use as Amrita (divine nectar) for immunity enhancement
herb/giloy-satva.to: - Traditionally used as Amrita (divine nectar) for immunity, with [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) properties. Preclinical and clinical studies have reported immunomodulatory activity.

herb/giloy-satva.from: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity validated through clinical studies in various febrile conditions, confirming traditional use in Jwara (fever) management including Vishama Jwara (intermittent/malarial fever)
herb/giloy-satva.to: - Traditionally used for Jwara (fever), including Vishama Jwara (intermittent/malarial fever). [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity has been reported in clinical studies in various febrile conditions.

herb/giloy-satva.from: - Antidiabetic activity validated through clinical trials showing improvement in glycemic parameters, confirming traditional use in Prameha (diabetes)
herb/giloy-satva.to: - Traditionally used for Prameha (diabetes). Clinical trials have reported improvement in glycemic parameters.

herb/gandhak-rasayan.from: - Antimicrobial and skin disease applications validated through in vitro studies showing activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Candida species, confirming use in Kushtha (skin diseases)
herb/gandhak-rasayan.to: - Kushtha (skin diseases): traditionally used for skin diseases. In vitro studies have reported antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Candida species.

herb/gandhak-rasayan.from: - [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (rejuvenation) properties partially validated through immunomodulatory studies and chronic toxicity safety data supporting long-term use
herb/gandhak-rasayan.to: - [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (rejuvenation): traditionally used as a rejuvenative. Studies have reported immunomodulatory activity.

herb/gandhak-rasayan.from: - Detoxification role supported by sulfur biochemistry (glutathione metabolism) and improvement in skin hydration demonstrated in pilot clinical study for eczema
herb/gandhak-rasayan.to: - Traditionally used for detoxification. A pilot clinical study in eczema reported improvement in skin hydration.

herb/gojihva.from: - Anti-asthmatic and respiratory tonic (Shvasa-hara) - validated through mast cell stabilization and bronchial hyper-responsiveness reduction studies
herb/gojihva.to: - Respiratory tonic (Shvasa-hara): traditionally used as a respiratory tonic and for asthma. Studies have reported mast cell stabilization and reduced bronchial hyper-responsiveness.

herb/gojihva.from: - Cooling and [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) (Jvarahara) - confirmed antipyretic activity in traditional Unani and Ayurvedic usage
herb/gojihva.to: - Cooling and [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) (Jvarahara): traditionally used in Unani and Ayurvedic practice as a cooling herb for fever.

herb/gojihva.from: - Throat and oral health (Mukha-roga) - supported by [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and anti-inflammatory studies
herb/gojihva.to: - Throat and oral health (Mukha-roga): traditionally used for throat and mouth conditions. Studies have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/gojihva.from: - Cardiotonic (Hridya) - traditional claim as heart tonic partially supported by pharmacological studies
herb/gojihva.to: - Heart tonic (Hridya): traditionally used as a heart tonic.

herb/gokarna.from: - Brain tonic and intellect enhancer (Medhya) - validated through multiple animal studies showing improved memory retention and learning
herb/gokarna.to: - Brain tonic and intellect enhancer (Medhya): traditionally used as a brain tonic and intellect enhancer. Animal studies have reported improved memory retention and learning.

herb/gokarna.from: - Anxiolytic (Manasa-Dosha-hara) - confirmed through pharmacological studies showing benzodiazepine-like anxiolytic activity
herb/gokarna.to: - Anxiolytic (Manasa-Dosha-hara): traditionally used as an anxiolytic. Pharmacological studies have reported benzodiazepine-like anxiolytic activity.

herb/gokarna.from: - Eye health ([Chakshushya](/herb/chakshushya/)) - partially validated through antioxidant protection of ocular tissues
herb/gokarna.to: - Eye health ([Chakshushya](/herb/chakshushya/)): traditionally used for eye health. Research has reported antioxidant protection of ocular tissues.

herb/gokarna.from: - Complexion and skin health (Varnya) - supported by antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms
herb/gokarna.to: - Complexion and skin health (Varnya): traditionally used for complexion and skin health. Antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity has been reported.

herb/ghrita.from: - Medhya [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (cognitive enhancement): Butyrate-mediated BDNF increase and fat-soluble vitamin transport validate traditional use of medicated ghees (Saraswata Ghrita, [Brahmi](/herb/brahmi/) Ghrita) for cognitive improvement
herb/ghrita.to: - Medhya [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (cognitive enhancement): medicated ghees such as Saraswata Ghrita and [Brahmi](/herb/brahmi/) Ghrita are traditionally used to support cognition.

herb/ghrita.from: - Agni Deepana without Pitta aggravation: Rapid metabolism of short/medium-chain fatty acids stimulates digestion while cooling virya prevents inflammatory overactivation - unique dual mechanism validated
herb/ghrita.to: - Agni Deepana without Pitta aggravation: traditionally used to stimulate digestion. Its cooling virya is traditionally held to keep this from aggravating Pitta.

herb/ghrita.from: - Snehana (oleation therapy in Panchakarma): Lipophilic drug delivery and membrane fluidity enhancement scientifically support ghee's role as the primary internal oleation medium
herb/ghrita.to: - Snehana (oleation therapy in Panchakarma): used in classical practice as the primary medium for internal oleation.

herb/gangeruki.from: - Anti-anemia (iron supplementation) validated through comparative clinical study demonstrating efficacy similar to ferrous gluconate in women with iron deficiency anemia
herb/gangeruki.to: - Anti-anemia (iron supplementation): a comparative clinical study in women with iron deficiency anemia reported results similar to ferrous gluconate.

herb/gangeruki.from: - Antidiarrhoeal and gut-soothing effects validated through in vivo and ex vivo pharmacodynamic studies supporting traditional Ayurvedic use for Atisara (diarrhea)
herb/gangeruki.to: - Atisara (diarrhea): traditionally used in Ayurveda for Atisara. In vivo and ex vivo pharmacodynamic studies have reported antidiarrhoeal and gut-soothing effects.

herb/gangeruki.from: - Hepatoprotective activity validated in CCl4-induced liver damage models, supporting traditional use for liver-related conditions
herb/gangeruki.to: - Liver-related conditions: traditionally used for liver-related conditions. Animal studies using carbon tetrachloride-induced liver damage models have reported hepatoprotective activity.

herb/godugdha.from: - Rasayana (rejuvenation therapy): Confirmed by modern evidence of immunoglobulin, lactoferrin, and growth factor content supporting tissue repair and immune function
herb/godugdha.to: - Rasayana (rejuvenation therapy): traditionally used as a rejuvenative. Modern analyses have reported that milk contains immunoglobulins, lactoferrin and growth factors.

herb/godugdha.from: - Insomnia and mental health (Nidrajanana): Tryptophan content and opioid peptides from casein digestion validated as promoting sleep and calming the nervous system
herb/godugdha.to: - Insomnia and mental health (Nidrajanana): traditionally used to promote sleep and calm the mind. Milk has been reported to contain tryptophan, and casein digestion has been reported to yield opioid peptides.

herb/godugdha.from: - Vehicle for herbal medicines (Anupana): Scientific evidence supports that milk proteins and fats enhance bioavailability of lipophilic herbal compounds
herb/godugdha.to: - Vehicle for herbal medicines (Anupana): used in classical practice as a vehicle for herbal medicines. Research has reported that milk proteins and fats may increase the bioavailability of fat-soluble herbal compounds.

herb/gomutra.from: - Shodhana (purification of toxins/minerals): Validated as an effective medium for reducing heavy metal toxicity in Ayurvedic mineral preparations through chelation and chemical transformation
herb/gomutra.to: - Shodhana (purification of toxins/minerals): used in classical practice as a medium for purifying Ayurvedic mineral preparations. Studies have reported reduced heavy metal toxicity in these preparations, attributed to chelation and chemical transformation.

herb/gomutra.from: - Bioenhancer (Yogavahi): US Patent and multiple studies confirm cow urine distillate enhances bioavailability of antibiotics, antifungals, and anti-tubercular drugs by 2-7 fold
herb/gomutra.to: - Bioenhancer (Yogavahi): traditionally used as a yogavahi. A US patent and several studies have reported that cow urine distillate increases the bioavailability of antibiotics, antifungals and anti-tubercular drugs.

herb/gomutra.from: - Wound healing and skin diseases: Allantoin content and antimicrobial properties provide scientific basis for traditional topical applications
herb/gomutra.to: - Wounds and skin diseases: traditionally applied topically. Its allantoin content and antimicrobial properties have been reported.

herb/icchabhedi-rasa.from: - Strong purgation (Virechana) for Panchakarma: The pharmacological basis is well-established - Croton oil's phorbol esters are potent activators of intestinal secretion and motility, validating the traditional use as a powerful cathartic
herb/icchabhedi-rasa.to: - Strong purgation (Virechana) for Panchakarma: traditionally used as a powerful cathartic. Croton oil's phorbol esters have been reported to stimulate intestinal secretion and motility.

herb/icchabhedi-rasa.from: - Ascites (Jalodara) and severe constipation: Historical use in fluid retention and obstinate constipation is mechanistically supported by the formulation's powerful secretagogue and peristalsis-stimulating properties
herb/icchabhedi-rasa.to: - Ascites (Jalodara) and severe constipation: traditionally used for fluid retention and obstinate constipation.

herb/hinguleshwar-ras.from: - Cough and cold (Kasa-Pratishyaya): Cinnabar's documented sedative/anti-tussive properties and [Pippali](/herb/pippali/)'s mucolytic action provide mechanistic support for the traditional anti-tussive use
herb/hinguleshwar-ras.to: - Cough and cold (Kasa-Pratishyaya): traditionally used for cough and cold. The formulation includes cinnabar and [Pippali](/herb/pippali/).

herb/hinguleshwar-ras.from: - Respiratory congestion: The combination of bioenhancer ([Pippali](/herb/pippali/)), [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/), and anti-inflammatory ingredients aligns with traditional use in respiratory disorders
herb/hinguleshwar-ras.to: - Respiratory congestion: traditionally used in respiratory disorders. The formulation combines [Pippali](/herb/pippali/) with ingredients traditionally regarded as [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) and anti-inflammatory.

herb/hajrul-yahood-bhasma.from: - Kidney stones (Ashmari): Lithontriptic and diuretic activity confirmed in research. Anodyne action reducing renal colic within 2-3 doses validated clinically.
herb/hajrul-yahood-bhasma.to: - Kidney stones (Ashmari): traditionally used for kidney stones. Studies have reported lithontriptic and diuretic activity. A clinical study reported reduced renal colic.

herb/hajrul-yahood-bhasma.from: - Gastric ulcers: Clinical trial showed 72% ulcer-healing rate with Hajrul Yahood + licorice vs 45% with ranitidine, validating gastroprotective use
herb/hajrul-yahood-bhasma.to: - Gastric ulcers: traditionally used for gastric ulcers. A clinical trial reported a higher rate of ulcer resolution with Hajrul Yahood plus licorice than with ranitidine.

herb/hajrul-yahood-bhasma.from: - Dysuria and urinary disorders: Diuretic and smooth muscle relaxant properties support traditional use for painful urination (Mutrakrichra)
herb/hajrul-yahood-bhasma.to: - Dysuria and urinary disorders: traditionally used for painful urination (Mutrakrichra). Studies have reported diuretic and smooth muscle relaxant properties.

herb/gorochana.from: - Apasmara (epilepsy/seizures): [Taurine](/glossary/compounds-t-z/#taurinetaurine) and bile acid-mediated GABA modulation provides scientific basis for traditional anticonvulsant use in pediatric and adult seizure management
herb/gorochana.to: - Apasmara (epilepsy/seizures): traditionally used for seizures in children and adults. Its constituents include [Taurine](/glossary/compounds-t-z/#taurinetaurine) and bile acids.

herb/gorochana.from: - Visha Chikitsa (toxicology/anti-poisoning): Bile salt chelation properties and hepatoprotective effects validate traditional use as a key ingredient in anti-poison formulations (Agada preparations)
herb/gorochana.to: - Visha Chikitsa (toxicology/anti-poisoning): used in classical practice as a key ingredient in anti-poison formulations (Agada preparations).

herb/gorochana.from: - Jwara and Unmada (fever and psychiatric disorders): Anti-inflammatory, antipyretic, and CNS-modulating effects of bile acids and bilirubin support classical indications
herb/gorochana.to: - Jwara and Unmada (fever and psychiatric disorders): used in classical practice for fever and psychiatric disorders.

herb/gorakhmundi.from: - Anti-obesity and [hypolipidemic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hypolipidemic) use validated through multiple RCTs showing significant weight loss and improved lipid parameters
herb/gorakhmundi.to: - Traditionally used as an anti-obesity and [hypolipidemic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hypolipidemic) herb. Clinical studies have reported weight loss and improved lipid parameters.

herb/gorakhmundi.from: - Anxiolytic use confirmed through modulation of GABAergic neurotransmission in elevated plus maze and open field test models
herb/gorakhmundi.to: - Traditionally used as an anxiolytic. Animal studies have reported anxiolytic activity involving GABAergic neurotransmission in elevated plus maze and open field test models.

herb/gorakhmundi.from: - Anti-diabetic use (Prameha-hara) supported by antihyperglycemic activity and insulin resistance prevention in glucocorticoid-induced diabetes model
herb/gorakhmundi.to: - Traditionally used as an anti-diabetic herb (Prameha-hara). Animal studies have reported antihyperglycemic activity and reduced insulin resistance in a glucocorticoid-induced diabetes model.

herb/haratala-bhasma.from: - Skin diseases (Kushtha): Traditional use partially supported by arsenic's known keratolytic properties, though modern safer alternatives exist
herb/haratala-bhasma.to: - Skin diseases (Kushtha): traditionally used for skin diseases. Safer modern alternatives exist.

herb/haratala-bhasma.from: - Asthma/respiratory disorders (Shwasa/Kasa): Some mechanistic support from bronchodilatory and mucolytic effects, but arsenic toxicity makes this indication unjustifiable
herb/haratala-bhasma.to: - Asthma/respiratory disorders (Shwasa/Kasa): traditionally used for asthma and respiratory disorders. Arsenic toxicity makes this use unjustifiable.

herb/haratala-bhasma.from: - Leukemia treatment: PARADOXICALLY VALIDATED - Arsenic trioxide is FDA-approved for acute promyelocytic leukemia. Haratala's apoptotic mechanism aligns with this approved indication.
herb/haratala-bhasma.to: - Leukemia: arsenic trioxide is FDA-approved for acute promyelocytic leukemia. That approval covers arsenic trioxide, not Haratala.

herb/himsra.from: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) effect through reduction of fasting blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose), HbA1c, and triglycerides (clinically validated at 400 mg TID for 2 months)
herb/himsra.to: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/): a clinical study reported reductions in fasting blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose), HbA1c, and triglycerides.

herb/himsra.from: - Hepatoprotective (Yakrit-hara) - strongly validated as key ingredient in Liv.52; clinical studies confirm protection against drug-induced and alcoholic liver damage
herb/himsra.to: - Hepatoprotective (Yakrit-hara): traditionally used to protect the liver. It is a key ingredient in Liv.52. Clinical studies have reported protection against drug-induced and alcoholic liver damage.

herb/himsra.from: - Antidiabetic (Prameha-hara) - validated through clinical trial showing significant blood glucose and HbA1c reduction
herb/himsra.to: - Antidiabetic (Prameha-hara): traditionally used for prameha. A clinical trial reported reductions in blood glucose and HbA1c.

herb/himsra.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) (Vedana-sthapana) - confirmed through multiple preclinical anti-inflammatory models
herb/himsra.to: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) (Vedana-sthapana): traditionally used to ease pain. Preclinical studies in several anti-inflammatory models have reported anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/himsra.from: - Digestive stimulant (Rochana) - traditional appetizer use validated through clinical observations of improved appetite
herb/himsra.to: - Digestive stimulant (Rochana): traditionally used as an appetizer. Clinical observations have reported improved appetite.

herb/himsra.from: Scoping review covering the entire genus documenting the diversity of bioactive compounds and their validated pharmacological activities including antidiabetic and [anticancer](/reference/anticancer/) potential.
herb/himsra.to: A scoping review covering the entire genus documented the diversity of bioactive compounds and their reported pharmacological activities, including antidiabetic and [anticancer](/reference/anticancer/) potential.

herb/hingupatri.from: - Digestive and carminative (Deepana, Anulomana) - validated through confirmed antispasmodic and carminative properties
herb/hingupatri.to: - Digestive and carminative (Deepana, Anulomana): traditionally used as a digestive and carminative. Studies have reported antispasmodic and carminative properties.

herb/hingupatri.from: - Anti-epileptic and nervine (Apasmara-hara) - partially supported by CNS-active sesquiterpene compounds
herb/hingupatri.to: - Anti-epileptic and nervine (Apasmara-hara): traditionally used for epilepsy and as a nervine. The plant has been reported to contain CNS-active sesquiterpene compounds.

herb/hingupatri.from: - Anti-infectious and antimicrobial (Krimighna) - confirmed broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity of organosulfides
herb/hingupatri.to: - Anti-infectious and antimicrobial (Krimighna): traditionally used as an anti-infectious agent. Studies have reported broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity of its organosulfides.

herb/hingupatri.from: - Respiratory conditions (Kasa-Shvasa) - validated [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) and bronchodilatory effects
herb/hingupatri.to: - Respiratory conditions (Kasa-Shvasa): traditionally used for respiratory conditions. Studies have reported [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) and bronchodilatory effects.

herb/hingupatri.from: Confirmed antispasmodic, expectorant, antiviral, and antifungal properties validating traditional Ayurvedic use as digestive, respiratory, and anti-infectious agent.
herb/hingupatri.to: Traditionally used in Ayurveda as a digestive, respiratory, and anti-infectious agent. Studies have reported antispasmodic, expectorant, antiviral, and antifungal properties.

herb/hingu.from: whoStatus: "Listed in the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India (API) and referenced in foundational Ayurvedic texts (Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita). Recognized in Unani medicine pharmacopoeia. Limited WHO-specific monograph coverage; identified as requiring further rigorous controlled clinical trials for formal therapeutic validation."
herb/hingu.to: whoStatus: "Listed in the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India (API) and referenced in foundational Ayurvedic texts (Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita). Recognized in Unani medicine pharmacopoeia. Limited WHO-specific monograph coverage. Further rigorous controlled clinical trials have been identified as needed before any therapeutic claims can be made."

herb/hingu.from: - Digestive aid for flatulence and dyspepsia - validated by double-blind RCT showing 81% improvement in functional dyspepsia symptoms
herb/hingu.to: - Traditionally used as a digestive aid for flatulence and dyspepsia. A double-blind randomized clinical study reported improvement in functional dyspepsia symptoms.

herb/hingu.from: - Antispasmodic for colic and abdominal pain - confirmed through smooth muscle relaxation studies
herb/hingu.to: - Traditionally used as an antispasmodic for colic and abdominal pain. Studies on smooth muscle have reported relaxant activity.

herb/hingu.from: - Expectorant for asthma and bronchitis - supported by network pharmacology and molecular docking studies identifying anti-asthmatic targets
herb/hingu.to: - Traditionally used as an expectorant for asthma and bronchitis. Network pharmacology and molecular docking studies have identified possible anti-asthmatic targets.

herb/hingu.from: - Antimicrobial agent against intestinal infections - validated by in vitro studies demonstrating broad-spectrum activity
herb/hingu.to: - Traditionally used for intestinal infections. In vitro studies have reported broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity.

herb/hingu.from: - Anti-inflammatory for pain and swelling - supported by multiple preclinical studies showing COX-2 and NF-kB inhibition
herb/hingu.to: - Traditionally used for pain and swelling. Preclinical studies have reported COX-2 and NF-kB inhibition.

herb/hingu.from: Network pharmacology analysis identified key molecular targets and signaling pathways through which asafoetida components exert anti-asthmatic effects, validating traditional use for respiratory conditions.
herb/hingu.to: A network pharmacology analysis identified molecular targets and signaling pathways through which asafoetida components may have anti-asthmatic effects.

herb/haridra.from: - Wound healing (Vranaropana): Validated by 2025 scoping review of multiple clinical trials confirming faster wound closure, enhanced collagen deposition, and increased vascular density
herb/haridra.to: - Vranaropana (wound care): traditionally used for wounds. A scoping review of clinical trials reported faster wound closure, greater collagen deposition and increased vascular density.

herb/haridra.from: - Psoriasis treatment (Ekakushtha): Validated by RCT showing 0.5% [curcumin](/herb/curcumin/) microemulgel significantly improved PASI scores and quality of life
herb/haridra.to: - Ekakushtha (psoriasis): traditionally used for Ekakushtha. A randomized controlled trial reported that a [curcumin](/herb/curcumin/) microemulgel improved psoriasis severity scores and quality of life.

herb/haridra.from: - Skin brightening and complexion (Varnya): Validated by demonstrated dual tyrosinase inhibition and MITF transcriptional regulation reducing melanin synthesis
herb/haridra.to: - Varnya (skin complexion): traditionally used for complexion. Research has reported tyrosinase inhibition and MITF regulation, with reduced melanin synthesis.

herb/haridra.from: - Anti-aging and photoprotection: Validated by 2025 research confirming UV-photoaging prevention through MMP suppression, [antioxidant](/reference/antioxidant/) protection, and anti-inflammatory mechanisms
herb/haridra.to: - Anti-aging and photoprotection: research has reported reduced UV-induced photoaging, linked to MMP suppression, [antioxidant](/reference/antioxidant/) protection and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/jeeraka.from: - Digestive and carminative properties extensively validated through clinical studies, confirming premier Ayurvedic use as Deepaniya (appetizer) and Pachaniya (digestive) herb
herb/jeeraka.to: - Traditionally used as a Deepaniya (appetizer) and Pachaniya (digestive) herb. Clinical studies have reported digestive and carminative properties.

herb/jeeraka.from: - Antidiabetic activity validated through clinical trials showing improvement in glycemic parameters, confirming traditional use in metabolic disorders
herb/jeeraka.to: - Traditionally used in metabolic disorders. Clinical studies have reported improvement in glycemic parameters.

herb/jeeraka.from: - [Hypolipidemic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hypolipidemic) effects validated through clinical studies showing reduction in total cholesterol and triglycerides, supporting traditional cardiovascular applications
herb/jeeraka.to: - Traditionally used in cardiovascular conditions. Clinical studies have reported [hypolipidemic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hypolipidemic) effects, including lower total cholesterol and triglycerides.

herb/jahar-mohra-pishti.from: - Cardiac tonic (Hridya): Magnesium's well-established role in cardiac function provides strong mechanistic support for the traditional cardiotonic claim, though specific clinical trials on [Jahar Mohra Pishti](/herb/jahar-mohra-pishti/) are lacking
herb/jahar-mohra-pishti.to: - Cardiac tonic (Hridya): traditionally used as a cardiac tonic. Specific clinical trials on [Jahar Mohra Pishti](/herb/jahar-mohra-pishti/) are lacking.

herb/jahar-mohra-pishti.from: - Antidote to poisons (Vishanashak) and anti-emetic: The magnesium silicate matrix's adsorptive properties provide a plausible mechanism for the traditional detoxifying/antidote claim
herb/jahar-mohra-pishti.to: - Antidote to poisons (Vishanashak) and anti-emetic: traditionally used as an antidote to poisons and as an anti-emetic.

herb/indravaruni.from: - Antidiabetic use validated through multiple preclinical studies showing alpha-glucosidase inhibition and improved insulin sensitivity
herb/indravaruni.to: - Traditionally used for diabetes. Preclinical studies have reported alpha-glucosidase inhibition and improved insulin sensitivity.
