herb/indravaruni.from: - Purgative use (Virechana) validated but requires strict dose control; traditional Ayurvedic Shodhana (purification) process reduces toxicity
herb/indravaruni.to: - Used in classical practice as a purgative (Virechana), with strict dose control. The traditional Ayurvedic Shodhana (purification) process is described as reducing toxicity.

herb/indravaruni.from: - Anti-inflammatory use confirmed by cucurbitacin-mediated suppression of NF-kB and pro-inflammatory cytokine production
herb/indravaruni.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation. Studies have reported cucurbitacin-mediated suppression of NF-kB and of pro-inflammatory cytokine production.

herb/jalavetasa.from: - Cooling and demulcent (Sheeta Virya) - supported by mucilaginous polysaccharide content providing soothing properties
herb/jalavetasa.to: - Cooling and demulcent (Sheeta Virya): traditionally described as cooling and demulcent. The plant contains mucilaginous polysaccharides.

herb/jalavetasa.from: - Mild diuretic (Mutrala) - partially supported by traditional reports from Kerala healers; limited scientific validation
herb/jalavetasa.to: - Mild diuretic (Mutrala): traditionally used as a mild diuretic, according to reports from Kerala healers. Scientific research on this use is limited.

herb/jalavetasa.from: - Skin soothing (Tvak Doshahara) - traditional topical use supported by anti-inflammatory flavonoid content
herb/jalavetasa.to: - Skin soothing (Tvak Doshahara): traditionally applied on the skin to soothe it. The plant contains flavonoids.

herb/jivaka.from: - Anti-inflammatory and photoprotective properties validated through in vitro enzyme inhibition assays, supporting traditional topical applications
herb/jivaka.to: - Traditionally used in topical applications. In vitro enzyme inhibition assays have reported anti-inflammatory and photoprotective activity.

herb/jivaka.from: - Rejuvenating ([Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)) role partially validated through antioxidant profiling showing potent free radical scavenging activity
herb/jivaka.to: - Traditionally used as a rejuvenating ([Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)) herb. Antioxidant profiling has reported strong free radical scavenging activity.

herb/jivaka.from: - [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac) traditional use indirectly supported by adaptogenic properties demonstrated in related species of Ashtavarga
herb/jivaka.to: - Traditionally used as an [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac). Studies on related Ashtavarga species, not on this herb itself, have reported adaptogenic properties.

herb/jivanti.from: - Reticulin and deniculatin modulate prolactin secretion through dopamine D2 receptor antagonism, enhancing lactogenesis - validated through in-silico molecular docking studies (2024)
herb/jivanti.to: - An in silico molecular docking study reported that reticulin and deniculatin may modulate prolactin secretion through dopamine D2 receptor antagonism, which may relate to lactogenesis.

herb/jivanti.from: - [Galactagogue](/glossary/pharmacology/#galactagogue) (Stanyajanana) activity validated through pharmacological studies and molecular docking confirming prolactin-modulating mechanism, supporting traditional Ayurvedic use for enhancing lactation
herb/jivanti.to: - [Galactagogue](/glossary/pharmacology/#galactagogue) (Stanyajanana): traditionally used in Ayurveda to enhance lactation. Pharmacological and molecular docking studies have reported prolactin-modulating activity.

herb/jivanti.from: - [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (rejuvenating/[adaptogenic](/reference/adaptogenic/)) properties partially validated through [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) and antioxidant studies supporting traditional classification as a life-giving (Jivanti) herb
herb/jivanti.to: - [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (rejuvenating/[adaptogenic](/reference/adaptogenic/)): traditionally classified as a life-giving (Jivanti) herb. Studies have reported [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) and antioxidant activity.

herb/jivanti.from: - Anti-abortifacient activity validated through preclinical studies, supporting traditional use for prevention of threatened abortion and as a uterine tonic
herb/jivanti.to: - Traditionally used for threatened abortion and as a uterine tonic. Preclinical studies have reported anti-abortifacient activity.

herb/ingudi.from: - Anthelmintic and antiparasitic use validated through molluscicidal and antischistosomal studies
herb/ingudi.to: - Traditionally used as an anthelmintic and antiparasitic. Studies have reported molluscicidal and antischistosomal activity.

herb/ingudi.from: - Wound healing validated through [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and tissue repair promotion studies
herb/ingudi.to: - Traditionally used on wounds. Studies have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity and promotion of tissue repair.

herb/ingudi.from: - [Laxative](/reference/laxative/) use confirmed through preclinical motility studies
herb/ingudi.to: - [Laxative](/reference/laxative/): traditionally used as a laxative. Preclinical studies have reported effects on motility.

herb/ingudi.from: - Skin disease treatment (leprosy, leukoderma) supported by antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory preclinical evidence
herb/ingudi.to: - Traditionally used for skin diseases, including leprosy and leukoderma. Preclinical studies have reported antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/ishwari.from: - Snake bite antidote (Sarpa-visha-hara) - partial in vitro validation of anti-venom properties but UNSAFE for human use due to aristolochic acid content
herb/ishwari.to: - Snake bite antidote (Sarpa-visha-hara): traditionally used for snake bite. An in vitro study reported partial anti-venom activity. Unsafe for human use due to aristolochic acid content.

herb/ishwari.from: - Emmenagogue (Artava-janana) - traditional use confirmed pharmacologically but CONTRAINDICATED due to carcinogenicity
herb/ishwari.to: - Emmenagogue (Artava-janana): traditionally used to promote menstruation. Contraindicated due to carcinogenicity.

herb/ishwari.from: - Anti-inflammatory (Shotha-hara) - confirmed but completely outweighed by cancer and kidney damage risk
herb/ishwari.to: - Anti-inflammatory (Shotha-hara): traditionally used for inflammation. Any such use is outweighed by the risk of cancer and kidney damage.

herb/ikshu.from: - [Kamala](/herb/kamala/) (jaundice/liver disorders): Hepatoprotective polyphenols (chlorogenic acid, flavonoids) and the CYP2E1/Keap1/NF-kB pathway modulation validate traditional use of fresh sugarcane juice in jaundice treatment
herb/ikshu.to: - [Kamala](/herb/kamala/) (jaundice/liver disorders): fresh sugarcane juice is traditionally used in jaundice.

herb/ikshu.from: - Mutrakricchra and Ashmari (dysuria and kidney stones): Diuretic and alkalinizing properties of sugarcane juice scientifically support traditional use in urinary disorders
herb/ikshu.to: - Mutrakricchra and Ashmari (dysuria and kidney stones): sugarcane juice is traditionally used in urinary disorders.

herb/ikshu.from: - Daha (burning sensation/Pitta conditions): Cooling virya, antioxidant polyphenols, and high potassium content validate traditional use as a Pitta-pacifying cooling agent
herb/ikshu.to: - Daha (burning sensation/Pitta conditions): traditionally used as a Pitta-pacifying cooling agent, described as having cooling virya.

herb/jayapala.from: - **Purgative (Virechana, Bhedana) for constipation and abdominal disorders.** Croton oil's powerful purgative action is well-established pharmacologically. It acts by stimulating intestinal secretion and motility through PKC-mediated prostaglandin release and direct irritation of GI mucosa. Used historically in Western medicine as a drastic cathartic before safer alternatives were developed.
herb/jayapala.to: - **Traditional purgative use (Virechana, Bhedana) for constipation and abdominal disorders.** Traditionally used as a strong purgative (Virechana, Bhedana) for constipation and abdominal disorders. Pharmacological studies have reported that croton oil stimulates intestinal secretion and motility and irritates the gut lining. It was used historically in Western medicine as a drastic cathartic before safer alternatives were developed.

herb/jayapala.from: - **Anti-inflammatory and anti-tumor (Shothahara, Granthi).** Paradoxically, while phorbol esters are tumor promoters, specific fractions and derivatives of Croton tiglium show anti-tumor activity. Research demonstrates PKC-modulated apoptosis in certain cancer cell lines. Traditional application as external anti-inflammatory paste (after purification) is supported by its counter-irritant properties.
herb/jayapala.to: - **Traditional anti-inflammatory and anti-tumor use (Shothahara, Granthi).** Used in classical practice as Shothahara and for Granthi. The phorbol esters in Croton tiglium are known tumor promoters. In vitro studies have reported anti-tumor activity, including cell death in certain cancer cell lines, for specific fractions and derivatives of the plant. Traditionally applied externally, after purification, as an anti-inflammatory paste for its counter-irritant action.

herb/kampillaka.from: - Anthelmintic use (Krimighna) against tapeworms extensively validated by in vitro and in vivo studies against cestodes
herb/kampillaka.to: - Krimighna (anthelmintic): traditionally used against tapeworms. In vitro and animal studies have reported activity against cestodes.

herb/kampillaka.from: - Anti-inflammatory use confirmed by superior COX-1/COX-2 inhibition compared to standard NSAIDs
herb/kampillaka.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation. Studies have reported COX-1 and COX-2 inhibition.

herb/kampillaka.from: - Skin disease treatment validated by [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and antifungal activity of [Kamala](/herb/kamala/) extract against dermatophytes
herb/kampillaka.to: - Traditionally used for skin diseases. Studies have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and antifungal activity of [Kamala](/herb/kamala/) extract against dermatophytes.

herb/kakoli.from: - Immunomodulatory and rejuvenation properties validated through preclinical studies demonstrating enhanced immune cell activity, confirming [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) application
herb/kakoli.to: - Traditionally used as a [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) for rejuvenation. Preclinical studies have reported enhanced immune cell activity.

herb/kakoli.from: - Hepatoprotective activity confirmed through experimental liver injury models, supporting traditional use in liver health
herb/kakoli.to: - Traditionally used for liver health. Studies in experimental liver injury models have reported hepatoprotective activity.

herb/kakoli.from: - Antioxidant and nutritive properties validated through chemical profiling showing rich mineral and carotenoid content, confirming traditional use as a body strengthener
herb/kakoli.to: - Traditionally used as a body strengthener. Chemical profiling has reported a rich mineral and carotenoid content.

herb/kaharuba-pishti.from: - Bleeding disorders (Raktapitta, Raktarsha): The astringent and hemostatic properties of amber/succinic acid provide mechanistic support; traditional use in bloody diarrhea, hemorrhoids, and excessive menstruation is well-documented in clinical practice
herb/kaharuba-pishti.to: - Bleeding disorders (Raktapitta, Raktarsha): traditionally used for bloody diarrhea, hemorrhoids, and excessive menstruation. Amber is described in classical practice as astringent.

herb/kaharuba-pishti.from: - Heart tonic (Hridya): Succinic acid's role in the Krebs cycle and mitochondrial energy production provides modern biochemical validation for the traditional cardiotonic claim
herb/kaharuba-pishti.to: - Heart tonic (Hridya): traditionally used as a cardiotonic.

herb/kamala.from: - Skin brightening and complexion (Varnya): Validated by clinical trial showing significant whitening effect in 21 volunteers with lotus callus extract cosmetics
herb/kamala.to: - Skin brightening and complexion (Varnya): traditionally used for skin brightening and complexion. A clinical study of cosmetics made with lotus callus extract reported a whitening effect.

herb/kamala.from: - Anti-aging and skin rejuvenation: Validated by in silico and in vitro studies identifying kaempferol-3-O-robinobioside as potent inhibitor of skin aging [enzymes](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#enzymes)
herb/kamala.to: - Anti-aging and skin rejuvenation: traditionally used for skin rejuvenation. In silico and in vitro studies reported kaempferol-3-O-robinobioside as an inhibitor of skin aging [enzymes](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#enzymes).

herb/kamala.from: - Anti-inflammatory skin soothing (Pitta-shamana): Validated by demonstrated NF-kB, MAPK, and COX-2 modulation reducing inflammatory mediators in skin
herb/kamala.to: - Anti-inflammatory skin soothing (Pitta-shamana): traditionally used for soothing the skin. Studies have reported modulation of NF-kB, MAPK, and COX-2, with lower levels of inflammatory mediators in skin.

herb/kadali.from: - Antidiarrhoeal activity of unripe banana (Apakva Kadali) validated through meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials in children, confirming traditional Ayurvedic use for Atisara (diarrhea) and Grahani (IBS)
herb/kadali.to: - Apakva Kadali (unripe banana): traditionally used in Ayurveda for Atisara (diarrhea) and Grahani (IBS). A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials in children reported antidiarrhoeal activity.

herb/kadali.from: - Anti-ulcerogenic activity validated through isolation of sitoindoside IV and demonstration of gastroprotective effects, supporting traditional use for Amlapitta (gastric ulcers)
herb/kadali.to: - Traditionally used for Amlapitta (gastric ulcers). A study that isolated sitoindoside IV reported anti-ulcerogenic and gastroprotective effects.

herb/kadali.from: - Anti-urolithiatic effects (kidney stone prevention) validated through studies showing reduction of urinary oxalate excretion in hyperoxaluric animal models
herb/kadali.to: - Anti-urolithiatic activity (kidney stones): animal studies in hyperoxaluric models have reported reduced urinary oxalate excretion.

herb/kadamba.from: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity against wound-infecting pathogens validated through disc diffusion and MIC studies
herb/kadamba.to: - In vitro studies using disc diffusion and MIC tests have reported [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity against wound-infecting pathogens.

herb/kadamba.from: - Anti-diarrheal use confirmed in castor oil-induced diarrhea models with significant reduction in stool frequency
herb/kadamba.to: - Traditionally used for diarrhea. Animal studies using castor oil-induced diarrhea models have reported a reduction in stool frequency.

herb/kadamba.from: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity validated in Brewer's yeast-induced pyrexia model in rats
herb/kadamba.to: - Animal studies have reported [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity in a Brewer's yeast-induced fever model in rats.

herb/kadamba.from: - Anti-inflammatory use confirmed through carrageenan-induced paw edema inhibition studies
herb/kadamba.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation. Animal studies have reported reduced paw edema in carrageenan-induced models.

herb/kadamba.from: - Standardized extracts, mechanistic validation, and clinical trials are recommended before therapeutic translation; no significant adverse effects reported in available preclinical studies
herb/kadamba.to: - Standardized extracts, mechanistic studies, and clinical trials would be needed before any therapeutic use. Available preclinical studies have reported no significant adverse effects.

herb/kalonji.from: - Digestive aid and carminative for bowel and indigestion problems - validated by pharmacological studies confirming [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) and carminative effects
herb/kalonji.to: - Traditionally used as a digestive aid and carminative for bowel and indigestion problems. Pharmacological studies have reported [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) and carminative effects.

herb/kalonji.from: - Anti-asthmatic and respiratory relief - validated by clinical trials showing bronchodilatory effects and improved lung function in asthma patients
herb/kalonji.to: - Traditionally used for asthma and other respiratory complaints. Clinical studies have reported bronchodilatory effects and improved lung function in people with asthma.

herb/kalonji.from: - Blood sugar control in diabetes - supported by year-long adjuvant clinical trial (114 patients, 2 g/day) showing improved glycemic control in type 2 diabetes
herb/kalonji.to: - Traditionally used for blood sugar control in diabetes. A clinical study reported improved glycemic control in people with type 2 diabetes when it was used as an adjuvant.

herb/kalonji.from: - Lipid-lowering and cardiovascular protection - confirmed by meta-analyses showing significant improvements in lipid profiles
herb/kalonji.to: - Traditionally used to lower lipids and protect the heart. Meta-analyses have reported improvements in lipid profiles.

herb/kalonji.from: - Immune modulation and anti-infective use - validated by immunological studies demonstrating enhanced immune cell function and antimicrobial activity
herb/kalonji.to: - Traditionally used for immune modulation and against infections. Immunological studies have reported enhanced immune cell function and antimicrobial activity.

herb/kadali-pushpa.from: - Anti-menorrhagic (reducing excessive menstrual bleeding) activity partially validated through traditional use documentation and supported by astringent tannin content and beta-sitosterol effects
herb/kadali-pushpa.to: - Traditionally used to reduce excessive menstrual bleeding (anti-menorrhagic use). The flower contains astringent tannins and beta-sitosterol.

herb/kadali-pushpa.from: - Anti-inflammatory properties validated through in vivo acute lung injury models and in vitro studies, supporting traditional use of banana flower decoction for inflammatory conditions
herb/kadali-pushpa.to: - Banana flower decoction is traditionally used for inflammatory conditions. Animal studies using acute lung injury models and in vitro studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/kadali-pushpa.from: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) effects supported by alpha-glucosidase inhibition studies, validating traditional use for blood sugar management
herb/kadali-pushpa.to: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) use: traditionally used for high blood sugar. Studies have reported alpha-glucosidase inhibition.

herb/kalajaji.from: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) activity validated through multiple clinical trials demonstrating improved glycemic control in type 2 diabetes patients, confirming traditional use for blood sugar management
herb/kalajaji.to: - Traditionally used for raised blood sugar. [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) activity has been reported in clinical studies, with improved glycemic control in people with type 2 diabetes.

herb/kalajaji.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects confirmed in clinical and preclinical studies supporting traditional use for rheumatic conditions and pain relief
herb/kalajaji.to: - Traditionally used for rheumatic conditions and pain. Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects have been reported in clinical and preclinical studies.

herb/kalajaji.from: - [Immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) effects validated through clinical evidence showing enhanced immune response, supporting the traditional Islamic medicine description as 'cure for everything except death'
herb/kalajaji.to: - Held in very high regard in traditional Islamic medicine. [Immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) effects, with an enhanced immune response, have been reported in clinical studies.

herb/kachura.from: - Digestive stimulant and carminative (Deepana) - validated through studies confirming carminative and digestive enzyme stimulation
herb/kachura.to: - Digestive stimulant and carminative (Deepana): traditionally used as a digestive stimulant and carminative. Studies have reported carminative activity and stimulation of digestive enzymes.

herb/kachura.from: - Anti-flatulence (Anulomana) - confirmed through [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) activity on gastrointestinal smooth muscle
herb/kachura.to: - Anti-flatulence (Anulomana): traditionally used for flatulence. Studies have reported [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) activity on gastrointestinal smooth muscle.

herb/kachura.from: - Anti-cancer adjunct (Arbuda-hara) - validated through multiple studies showing antiproliferative activity against gastric, ovarian, and breast cancer cells
herb/kachura.to: - Arbuda-hara: a traditional use in classical practice. Laboratory studies have reported antiproliferative activity against gastric, ovarian, and breast cancer cells.

herb/kachura.from: - Anti-inflammatory (Shotha-hara) - confirmed through [curcumin](/herb/curcumin/) and germacrone-mediated anti-inflammatory pathways
herb/kachura.to: - Anti-inflammatory (Shotha-hara): traditionally used for inflammation. Studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity linked to [curcumin](/herb/curcumin/) and germacrone.

herb/kanmad-bhasma.from: - Iron-deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga): Iron supplementation efficacy well-established; magnetite form provides superior bioavailability per Ayurvedic and modern analysis
herb/kanmad-bhasma.to: - Iron-deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga): traditionally used for iron-deficiency anemia.

herb/kanmad-bhasma.from: - Diabetes (Madhumeha): Traditional use supported by iron's role in [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) metabolism regulation and insulin sensitivity enhancement
- Chronic fevers (Jeerna Jwara): Anti-microbial and immune-supporting properties of iron compounds provide partial mechanistic validation
herb/kanmad-bhasma.to: - Chronic fevers (Jeerna Jwara): traditionally used for chronic fevers.

herb/kamsya-bhasma.from: - Worm infestations (Krimi Roga): Anti-parasitic properties of copper compounds provide mechanistic support for traditional use
herb/kamsya-bhasma.to: - Worm infestations (Krimi Roga): traditionally used for worm infestations.

herb/kamsya-bhasma.from: - Skin diseases (Kushtha): Combined antimicrobial properties of copper and tin oxides support traditional dermatological applications
herb/kamsya-bhasma.to: - Skin diseases (Kushtha): traditionally used for skin diseases.

herb/kamsya-bhasma.from: - Eye disorders (Netra Roga): Historical use of Kansa instruments in eye treatments documented since Charaka period, supported by anti-inflammatory copper properties
herb/kamsya-bhasma.to: - Eye disorders (Netra Roga): traditionally used for eye disorders. Classical texts record the use of Kansa instruments in eye care since the Charaka period.

herb/kantakari.from: - Bronchodilatory use for asthma and cough (Shwasa-Kasahara) validated through histamine-induced bronchospasm reversal in animal models
herb/kantakari.to: - Traditionally used for asthma and cough (Shwasa-Kasahara) as a bronchodilator. Animal studies have reported reversal of histamine-induced bronchospasm.

herb/kantakari.from: - [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) action (Mutrala) confirmed by significant increase in urine volume and electrolyte excretion in rats
herb/kantakari.to: - Traditionally used as a [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) (Mutrala). Animal studies in rats have reported increased urine volume and electrolyte excretion.

herb/kantakari.from: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) use supported by fever reduction in Brewer's yeast-induced pyrexia model
herb/kantakari.to: - Traditionally used as an [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/). A study using a Brewer's yeast-induced pyrexia model reported reduced fever.

herb/kankola.from: - Digestive and carminative (Deepana-Pachana) - validated through confirmed stimulant and carminative properties
herb/kankola.to: - Digestive and carminative (Deepana-Pachana): traditionally used as a digestive and carminative.

herb/kankola.from: - Respiratory disorders and cough (Kasa-hara) - supported by traditional [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) use; essential oil has [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity against respiratory pathogens
herb/kankola.to: - Respiratory disorders and cough (Kasa-hara): traditionally used as an [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) for respiratory complaints and cough. Laboratory studies have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity of the essential oil against respiratory pathogens.

herb/kankola.from: - Urogenital health (Mutra-roga) - traditional use for urinary tract infections partially supported by antimicrobial data
herb/kankola.to: - Urogenital health (Mutra-roga): traditionally used for urinary tract infections. Laboratory studies have reported antimicrobial activity.

herb/kankola.from: - Oral health freshener (Mukha-shodhana) - traditional oral care use supported by antibacterial activity
herb/kankola.to: - Oral health freshener (Mukha-shodhana): traditionally used for oral care and to freshen the mouth. Laboratory studies have reported antibacterial activity.

herb/kapittha.from: - Anti-diarrheal and dysentery treatment validated through antimicrobial and anti-motility preclinical studies
herb/kapittha.to: - Traditionally used for diarrhea and dysentery. Preclinical studies have reported antimicrobial and anti-motility activity.

herb/kapittha.from: - Peptic ulcer treatment confirmed through aspirin/ethanol-induced ulcer models
herb/kapittha.to: - Traditionally used for peptic ulcer. Preclinical studies in aspirin- and ethanol-induced ulcer models have reported anti-ulcer activity.

herb/kapittha.from: - Hepatoprotective use supported by CCl4-induced liver damage models with significant restoration of liver function markers
herb/kapittha.to: - Traditionally used to protect the liver. Preclinical studies in CCl4-induced liver damage models have reported restoration of liver function markers.

herb/kapittha.from: - Respiratory ailment use supported by antihistaminic and bronchodilatory effects in preclinical studies
herb/kapittha.to: - Traditionally used for respiratory ailments. Preclinical studies have reported antihistaminic and bronchodilatory effects.

herb/karanja.from: - Skin disease (Kushtha) treatment validated through antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory studies on dermatophytes and skin pathogens
herb/karanja.to: - Kushtha (skin disease): traditionally used for skin disease. Studies have reported antimicrobial activity against dermatophytes and skin pathogens, as well as anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/karanja.from: - Anti-hemorrhoidal use supported by anti-inflammatory and wound healing preclinical studies
herb/karanja.to: - Traditionally used for hemorrhoids. Preclinical studies have reported anti-inflammatory and wound-healing activity.

herb/karanja.from: - Anthelmintic activity confirmed against Pheretima posthuma and Ascaridia galli in vitro
herb/karanja.to: - In vitro studies have reported anthelmintic activity against Pheretima posthuma and Ascaridia galli.

herb/karanja.from: - Anti-inflammatory use validated in carrageenan-induced paw edema and cotton pellet granuloma models
herb/karanja.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation. Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity in carrageenan-induced paw edema and cotton pellet granuloma models.

herb/kasamarda.from: - Skin fungal infections (Dadru/Kushtha): Validated by 2024 study confirming antifungal activity of root extracts against Candida albicans, Rhodotorula glutinis, and Aspergillus niger
herb/kasamarda.to: - Skin fungal infections (Dadru/Kushtha): traditionally used for these skin conditions. A study reported antifungal activity of root extracts against Candida albicans, Rhodotorula glutinis, and Aspergillus niger.

herb/kasamarda.from: - Anti-inflammatory skin conditions: Supported by demonstrated anti-inflammatory activity of chromone and flavone constituents
herb/kasamarda.to: - Inflammatory skin conditions: traditionally used for inflammatory skin conditions. Studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity of its chromone and flavone constituents.

herb/kasamarda.from: - Wound healing: Traditional leaf poultice application supported by [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and anti-inflammatory mechanisms
herb/kasamarda.to: - Wounds: traditionally applied to wounds as a leaf poultice. Studies have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/karkatashringi.from: - Anti-asthmatic use in children (Balaka Shwasa) supported by bronchial smooth muscle relaxation and mast cell stabilization in preclinical studies
herb/karkatashringi.to: - Balaka Shwasa (asthma in children): traditionally used for asthma in children. Preclinical studies have reported bronchial smooth muscle relaxation and mast cell stabilization.

herb/karkatashringi.from: - Antitussive use (Kasa-hara) confirmed by reduction of cough frequency in SO2-induced cough model and [citric acid](/glossary/compounds-c-d/#citric-acidcitric-acid)-induced cough model
herb/karkatashringi.to: - Kasa-hara (antitussive): traditionally used for cough. Studies in sulfur dioxide-induced and [citric acid](/glossary/compounds-c-d/#citric-acidcitric-acid)-induced cough models have reported reduced cough frequency.

herb/karkatashringi.from: - Digestive use (Deepana) supported by enhancement of gastric enzyme secretion and carminative activity of essential oil components
herb/karkatashringi.to: - Deepana (digestive): traditionally used for digestion. Studies have reported increased gastric enzyme secretion and carminative activity of its essential oil components.

herb/kankshi.from: - Sweetener and demulcent (Madhura) - [glycyrrhizin](/glossary/compounds-g-l/#glycyrrhizinglycyrrhizin) and abrusoside content validated as 30-100x sweeter than [sucrose](/glossary/compounds-q-t/#sucrose) with potential pharmaceutical applications
herb/kankshi.to: - Sweetener and demulcent (Madhura): traditionally used as a sweetener and demulcent. Its [glycyrrhizin](/glossary/compounds-g-l/#glycyrrhizinglycyrrhizin) and abrusoside content has been reported to be far sweeter than [sucrose](/glossary/compounds-q-t/#sucrose), with possible pharmaceutical applications.

herb/kankshi.from: - Anti-inflammatory (Shotha-hara) - [glycyrrhizin](/glossary/compounds-g-l/#glycyrrhizinglycyrrhizin)-mediated anti-inflammatory action validated in multiple studies
herb/kankshi.to: - Anti-inflammatory (Shotha-hara): traditionally used for inflammation. Several studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity linked to [glycyrrhizin](/glossary/compounds-g-l/#glycyrrhizinglycyrrhizin).

herb/kankshi.from: - Hair care and external applications - traditional hair oil preparations using purified seeds supported by antimicrobial data
herb/kankshi.to: - Hair care and external applications: traditionally used in hair oil preparations made with purified seeds. Antimicrobial activity has been reported.

herb/kankshi.from: - Contraceptive (Garbha-nirodha) - antifertility activity documented in animal studies but too toxic for safe human use
herb/kankshi.to: - Contraceptive (Garbha-nirodha): traditionally used as a contraceptive. Animal studies have reported antifertility activity, but it is considered too toxic for safe human use.

herb/kanchanar.from: - Anti-goitrogenic and thyroid-supportive use validated through clinical case series showing improved TSH and thyroid hormone levels
herb/kanchanar.to: - Traditionally used as an anti-goitrogenic and for the thyroid. A clinical case series reported improved TSH and thyroid hormone levels.

herb/kanchanar.from: - Lymphadenitis (Gandamala) treatment confirmed through clinical observations and Kanchanar [Guggulu](/formulation/guggulu/) studies
herb/kanchanar.to: - Gandamala (lymphadenitis): traditionally used for this condition, including as Kanchanar [Guggulu](/formulation/guggulu/).

herb/kanchanar.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects validated through carrageenan-induced paw edema model with 46-77% inhibition
herb/kanchanar.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation and pain. Animal studies have reported reduced swelling in the carrageenan-induced paw edema model, along with [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects.

herb/kanchanar.from: - [Hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic) and anti-hemorrhagic use supported by astringent tannin content and clinical observations in menorrhagia
herb/kanchanar.to: - [Hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic) and anti-hemorrhagic use: traditionally used to check bleeding. The plant contains astringent tannins.

herb/kshara-parpati.from: answer: "Kshara Parpati is a rasa preparation, a herbo-mineral formulation of the rasa shastra tradition. Mutrashmari (urinary calculi/kidney stones) - traditional use supported by comparative clinical study showing litholytic and diuretic efficacy Mutrakrichra (dysuria/painful urination) - traditional primary indication validated through pharmaceutical review and clinical practice observations"
herb/kshara-parpati.to: answer: "Kshara Parpati is a rasa preparation, a herbo-mineral formulation of the rasa shastra tradition. It is traditionally used for Mutrashmari (urinary calculi/kidney stones). A comparative clinical study reported litholytic and diuretic activity. In classical practice, Mutrakrichra (dysuria/painful urination) is a primary traditional indication."

herb/kshara-parpati.from: - Mutrashmari (urinary calculi/kidney stones) - traditional use supported by comparative clinical study showing litholytic and diuretic efficacy
herb/kshara-parpati.to: - Mutrashmari (urinary calculi/kidney stones): traditionally used for this condition. A comparative clinical study reported litholytic and diuretic activity.

herb/kshara-parpati.from: - Mutrakrichra (dysuria/painful urination) - traditional primary indication validated through pharmaceutical review and clinical practice observations
herb/kshara-parpati.to: - Mutrakrichra (dysuria/painful urination): a primary traditional indication in classical practice.

herb/khadira.from: - Psoriasis management (Ekakushtha): Validated by clinical study showing significant PASI score improvement in 40 patients treated with Khadira powder
herb/khadira.to: - Psoriasis (Ekakushtha): traditionally used for psoriasis. A clinical study reported improvement in PASI scores in patients given Khadira powder.

herb/khadira.from: - Blood purification for skin diseases (Raktashodhaka): Khadirarishta formulation validated for eczema, acne, and chronic skin disorders through systemic polyphenol activity
herb/khadira.to: - Blood purification for skin diseases (Raktashodhaka): Khadirarishta is used in classical practice for eczema, acne, and chronic skin disorders.

herb/khadira.from: - Skin allergies and urticaria (Sheetapitta): Traditional use supported by demonstrated T-cell [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) properties
herb/khadira.to: - Skin allergies and urticaria (Sheetapitta): traditionally used for skin allergies and urticaria. Research has reported T-cell [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) properties.

herb/kovidara.from: - Anti-inflammatory and analgesic use validated with significant edema inhibition (46-77%) in carrageenan model
herb/kovidara.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation and pain. Animal studies have reported reduced edema in a carrageenan model.

herb/kovidara.from: - Wound healing confirmed through enhanced collagen deposition and epithelialization in excision wound models
herb/kovidara.to: - Traditionally used for wound healing. Animal studies in excision wound models have reported more collagen deposition and epithelialization.

herb/kovidara.from: - Antidiabetic use supported by hypoglycemic effects in alloxan-induced diabetic rat models
herb/kovidara.to: - Traditionally used for diabetes. Animal studies in alloxan-induced diabetic rats have reported hypoglycemic effects.

herb/kovidara.from: - Anti-diarrheal activity confirmed in castor oil-induced diarrhea models
herb/kovidara.to: - Traditionally used for diarrhea. Animal studies have reported anti-diarrheal activity in castor oil-induced diarrhea models.

herb/kasani.from: - Hepatoprotective use (Yakrit-Shodhaka) validated through clinical and preclinical studies showing reduction of liver [enzymes](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#enzymes) and hepatocyte regeneration
herb/kasani.to: - Yakrit-Shodhaka (liver): traditionally used for the liver. Clinical and preclinical studies have reported lower liver [enzymes](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#enzymes) and hepatocyte regeneration.

herb/kasani.from: - Digestive and prebiotic use confirmed by enhancement of beneficial gut microbiota (Bifidobacteria) through inulin fermentation
herb/kasani.to: - Traditionally used for digestion. Research has reported that inulin fermentation increased beneficial gut bacteria (Bifidobacteria).

herb/kasani.from: - Antidiabetic use supported by clinical evidence of improved glycemic control and insulin sensitivity
herb/kasani.to: - Traditionally used in diabetes. Clinical studies have reported improved glycemic control and insulin sensitivity.

herb/krimi-kuthar-rasa.from: - Intestinal parasites (Krimi Roga) including roundworms, tapeworms, and pinworms - traditional primary indication; supported by anthelmintic activity of [Vidanga](/herb/vidanga/) (embelin) and Palash seeds (palasonin)
herb/krimi-kuthar-rasa.to: - Intestinal parasites (Krimi Roga), including roundworms, tapeworms, and pinworms: traditionally used as the primary indication. Ingredients include [Vidanga](/herb/vidanga/) (embelin) and Palash seeds (palasonin), which are described as having anthelmintic activity.

herb/krimi-kuthar-rasa.from: - Digestive disorders associated with parasitic infection - traditional use supported by the carminative, digestive, and anti-amoebic properties of [Indrayava](/herb/indrayava/), Ajamoda, and Karpura
herb/krimi-kuthar-rasa.to: - Digestive disorders associated with parasitic infection: traditionally used for this purpose. Ingredients include [Indrayava](/herb/indrayava/), Ajamoda, and Karpura, which are described as having carminative, digestive, and anti-amoebic properties.

herb/kshavaka.from: answer: "Kshavaka (Amaranthus spinosus L.) is a plant drug, also called Tanduliya and Kamta caulai, from the Amaranthaceae family. Diuretic activity validated through pharmacological studies supporting traditional Ayurvedic use for Mutrakrichchhra (dysuria) and urinary disorders Anti-inflammatory and wound healing properties confirmed in preclinical models, supporting traditional topical use for skin conditions and wound management"
herb/kshavaka.to: answer: "Kshavaka (Amaranthus spinosus L.) is a plant drug, also called Tanduliya and Kamta caulai, from the Amaranthaceae family. Traditionally used in Ayurveda for Mutrakrichchhra (dysuria) and urinary disorders. Pharmacological studies have reported diuretic activity. Traditionally applied topically for skin conditions and wounds. Preclinical studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity and effects on wound repair."

herb/kshavaka.from: - Diuretic activity validated through pharmacological studies supporting traditional Ayurvedic use for Mutrakrichchhra (dysuria) and urinary disorders
herb/kshavaka.to: - Mutrakrichchhra (dysuria): traditionally used in Ayurveda for Mutrakrichchhra and urinary disorders. Pharmacological studies have reported diuretic activity.

herb/kshavaka.from: - Anti-inflammatory and wound healing properties confirmed in preclinical models, supporting traditional topical use for skin conditions and wound management
herb/kshavaka.to: - Skin conditions and wounds: traditionally applied topically. Preclinical studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity and effects on wound repair.

herb/kasturi.from: - Hridya (cardiac tonic): Muscone's cardioprotective and inotropic effects validate traditional use in cardiac formulations including Kasturi Bhairava Rasa and Mrigamadasava
herb/kasturi.to: - Hridya (cardiac tonic): traditionally used in cardiac formulations including Kasturi Bhairava Rasa and Mrigamadasava. Studies have reported cardioprotective and inotropic effects of muscone.

herb/kasturi.from: - Unmada and Apasmara (psychiatric/neurological disorders): Muscone's ability to cross BBB and modulate neuroinflammation supports classical Ayurvedic use in stroke, seizures, and psychiatric conditions
herb/kasturi.to: - Unmada and Apasmara (psychiatric/neurological disorders): used in classical Ayurvedic practice for stroke, seizures, and psychiatric conditions. Studies have reported that muscone can cross the blood-brain barrier and modulate neuroinflammation.

herb/kasturi.from: - Vishamjwara (intermittent fevers) and Sannipata: Anti-inflammatory and [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) properties provide basis for traditional use in severe febrile and toxic conditions
herb/kasturi.to: - Vishamjwara (intermittent fevers) and Sannipata: traditionally used in severe febrile and toxic conditions. Studies have reported anti-inflammatory and [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) properties.

herb/kasis-bhasma.from: - [Hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) action through [antioxidant](/reference/antioxidant/) activity and cellular membrane stabilization, protecting liver cells from toxic damage (validated against CCl4 toxicity)
herb/kasis-bhasma.to: - [Hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) activity, with [antioxidant](/reference/antioxidant/) activity and cellular membrane stabilization, has been reported in studies of CCl4-induced liver toxicity.

herb/kasis-bhasma.from: - Iron-deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga): Improved hemoglobin and ferritin levels confirmed in clinical evaluations without GI side effects of conventional iron
herb/kasis-bhasma.to: - Iron-deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga): traditionally used for Pandu Roga. Clinical evaluations have reported improved hemoglobin and ferritin levels without the GI side effects of conventional iron.

herb/kasis-bhasma.from: - Liver disorders: Hepatoprotective activity against CCl4-induced hepatotoxicity validated in animal models
herb/kasis-bhasma.to: - Liver disorders: traditionally used for liver disorders. Animal studies have reported hepatoprotective activity against CCl4-induced hepatotoxicity.

herb/kasis-bhasma.from: - Digestive disorders (Agnimandya, Ajirna): Deepana-Pachana properties confirmed through improved appetite and digestion in clinical observations
herb/kasis-bhasma.to: - Digestive disorders (Agnimandya, Ajirna): traditionally used for its Deepana-Pachana properties. Clinical observations have reported improved appetite and digestion.

herb/kataka.from: - Water purification (Jala-shodhana) - strongly validated as natural coagulant and [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) agent for water treatment; extensively studied
herb/kataka.to: - Water purification (Jala-shodhana): traditionally used to purify water. Studies have reported activity as a natural coagulant and [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) agent.

herb/kataka.from: - Eye health ([Chakshushya](/herb/chakshushya/)) - traditional eye drops (Kataka seed water) supported by antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory data
herb/kataka.to: - Eye health ([Chakshushya](/herb/chakshushya/)): traditionally used as eye drops made from Kataka seed water. Research has reported antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/kataka.from: - Anti-diarrheal (Atisara-nashaka) - validated through tannin-mediated astringent and antimicrobial activity
herb/kataka.to: - Anti-diarrheal (Atisara-nashaka): traditionally used for diarrhea. Research has reported astringent and antimicrobial activity attributed to tannins.

herb/kataka.from: - Diabetes management (Prameha) - supported by preclinical antidiabetic studies showing blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) reduction
herb/kataka.to: - Diabetes (Prameha): traditionally used for prameha. Preclinical studies have reported reduced blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose).

herb/kataka.from: Documented comprehensive phytochemical profile with tannins, saponins, and alkaloids as major classes; validated antimicrobial, antidiarrheal, [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/), and contraceptive activities.
herb/kataka.to: Studies have described a phytochemical profile with tannins, saponins, and alkaloids as major classes. Research has reported antimicrobial, antidiarrheal, [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/), and contraceptive activities.

herb/kharjura.from: - [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac) and fertility enhancement (Vajikara) validated through spermatogenic studies with date palm pollen in animal models
herb/kharjura.to: - [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac) and fertility enhancement (Vajikara): traditionally used as an aphrodisiac and to enhance fertility. Animal studies with date palm pollen have reported spermatogenic effects.

herb/kharjura.from: - [Expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) and antitussive use validated through demulcent and bronchodilatory effects in preclinical models
herb/kharjura.to: - [Expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) and antitussive: traditionally used as an expectorant and antitussive. Preclinical studies have reported demulcent and bronchodilatory effects.

herb/kharjura.from: - Nutritive tonic (Balya) use supported by rich mineral, vitamin and caloric profile documentation
herb/kharjura.to: - Nutritive tonic (Balya): traditionally used as a nutritive tonic. Its mineral, vitamin and caloric content has been documented.

herb/kharjura.from: - [Laxative](/reference/laxative/) use validated through high dietary fiber content and bulk-forming mechanism studies
herb/kharjura.to: - [Laxative](/reference/laxative/): traditionally used as a laxative. It has a high dietary fiber content, and studies have described a bulk-forming mechanism.

herb/kharjura.from: Date palm pollen extract demonstrated significant fertility-enhancing effects in male rats with increased sperm count, motility and testosterone levels, validating traditional aphrodisiac use.
herb/kharjura.to: An animal study reported that date palm pollen extract increased sperm count, motility and testosterone levels in male rats. Date palm pollen is traditionally used as an aphrodisiac.

herb/kushmanda.from: - Neuroprotective and Medhya (intellect-promoting) use validated through restoration of neurotransmitter levels in Alzheimer's disease animal model
herb/kushmanda.to: - Medhya (intellect-promoting): traditionally used to support the mind and intellect. Animal studies of an Alzheimer's disease model have reported restoration of neurotransmitter levels.

herb/kushmanda.from: - Anti-ulcer use confirmed by gastroprotective activity through reduction of gastric acid secretion and enhancement of mucosal defense
herb/kushmanda.to: - Traditionally used for ulcers. Studies have reported gastroprotective activity, with reduced gastric acid secretion and enhanced mucosal defense.

herb/kushmanda.from: - [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) and nephroprotective use (Mutrala) supported by increased urine output and renal stone dissolution activity
herb/kushmanda.to: - Mutrala: traditionally used as a [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) and for the kidneys. Studies have reported increased urine output and renal stone dissolution activity.

herb/lavali.from: - Antidiabetic and antihyperglycemic activity partially validated through preliminary pharmacological studies supporting traditional tribal use for diabetes management
herb/lavali.to: - Traditionally used in tribal practice for diabetes. Preliminary pharmacological studies have reported antidiabetic and antihyperglycemic activity.

herb/lavali.from: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) properties confirmed in vitro against bacterial and fungal pathogens, supporting traditional use for treating dysentery and skin infections in folk medicine
herb/lavali.to: - Traditionally used in folk medicine for dysentery and skin infections. [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity against bacterial and fungal pathogens has been reported in vitro.

herb/kulattha.from: - Anti-urolithiatic (kidney stone dissolving) activity validated through in vitro and in vivo studies, confirming premier Ayurvedic use in Ashmari (renal calculi)
herb/kulattha.to: - Used in classical practice for Ashmari (renal calculi). In vitro and in vivo studies have reported anti-urolithiatic (kidney stone dissolving) activity.

herb/kulattha.from: - Antidiabetic potential confirmed through enzyme inhibition and in vivo blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) studies, supporting traditional use in Prameha
herb/kulattha.to: - Traditionally used for Prameha. Enzyme inhibition studies and in vivo blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) studies have reported antidiabetic potential.

herb/kulattha.from: - Bronchodilatory and anti-asthmatic properties supported by preliminary studies, partially validating traditional use in Shwasa (respiratory conditions)
herb/kulattha.to: - Traditionally used for Shwasa (respiratory conditions). Preliminary studies have reported bronchodilatory and anti-asthmatic properties.

herb/kukkutanda-twak-bhasma.from: - Calcium deficiency and bone disorders: 60.83% calcium content with high bioavailability confirmed analytically, validating use for Asthi Kshaya (bone depletion), rickets, and osteoporosis
herb/kukkutanda-twak-bhasma.to: - Calcium deficiency and bone disorders: traditionally used for Asthi Kshaya (bone depletion), rickets, and osteoporosis. Analytical studies have reported a high calcium content with high bioavailability.

herb/kukkutanda-twak-bhasma.from: - Leukorrhea (Shweta Pradar): Traditional gynecological use supported by calcium's role in reproductive health and mucosal integrity
herb/kukkutanda-twak-bhasma.to: - Leukorrhea (Shweta Pradar): traditionally used in gynecological practice for this condition.

herb/kukkutanda-twak-bhasma.from: - Urinary tract infections: Antimicrobial CaO nanoparticle activity and alkaline pH effects support traditional use for Mutra Krichra (dysuria)
herb/kukkutanda-twak-bhasma.to: - Urinary tract infections: traditionally used for Mutra Krichra (dysuria). Laboratory studies have reported antimicrobial activity of CaO nanoparticles and an alkaline pH.

herb/laghu-sutshekhar-ras.from: - Hyperacidity and acid reflux (Amlapitta): Pilot clinical study (2019) showed 68% symptom relief in functional dyspepsia within 2 weeks, supporting traditional use as an antacid and digestive aid
herb/laghu-sutshekhar-ras.to: - Hyperacidity and acid reflux (Amlapitta): traditionally used as an antacid and digestive aid. A pilot clinical study reported improvement in functional dyspepsia symptoms.

herb/laghu-sutshekhar-ras.from: - Digestive disorders: The calcium carbonate content from [Shankha Bhasma](/herb/shankha-bhasma/) has a well-established acid-neutralizing mechanism directly relevant to the traditional indication, providing strong mechanistic validation
herb/laghu-sutshekhar-ras.to: - Digestive disorders: traditionally used for digestive disorders. Its calcium carbonate content from [Shankha Bhasma](/herb/shankha-bhasma/) is described as having an acid-neutralizing action.

herb/lodhra.from: - Menorrhagia management supported by observational clinical data showing reduced menstrual bleeding.
herb/lodhra.to: - Traditionally used for menorrhagia. Observational clinical data have reported reduced menstrual bleeding.

herb/lodhra.from: - Wound healing confirmed in clinical trial comparing Lodhra paste to placebo.
herb/lodhra.to: - Traditionally used for wounds. A clinical trial comparing Lodhra paste with placebo reported improved wound repair.

herb/lodhra.from: - Anti-inflammatory activity validated through COX-2 inhibition studies.
herb/lodhra.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation. Studies of COX-2 inhibition have reported anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/lodhra.from: - Leucorrhoea management supported by herbal infusion formulation studies.
- Astringent and hemostatic properties confirmed through tannin-mediated protein precipitation mechanisms.
herb/lodhra.to: - Traditionally described as astringent and hemostatic. Studies have reported tannin-mediated protein precipitation as a possible mechanism for these properties.

herb/lavanga.from: - Toothache and dental pain relief - extensively validated; eugenol is an established dental analgesic and antiseptic used worldwide in dental practice
herb/lavanga.to: - Toothache and dental pain: traditionally used for toothache and dental pain. Eugenol is used in dental practice as an analgesic and antiseptic.

herb/lavanga.from: - Antimicrobial for oral infections and wound care - confirmed by in vitro and clinical studies showing broad-spectrum activity including against MDR bacteria
herb/lavanga.to: - Oral infections and wounds: traditionally used for oral infections and wound care. In vitro and clinical studies have reported broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including against multidrug-resistant bacteria.

herb/lavanga.from: - Digestive aid for flatulence, colic, and nausea - supported by pharmacological studies demonstrating [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) and carminative effects
herb/lavanga.to: - Flatulence, colic and nausea: traditionally used as a digestive aid for flatulence, colic and nausea. Pharmacological studies have reported [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) and carminative effects.

herb/lavanga.from: - Anti-inflammatory for joint and muscle pain - validated by studies showing COX-2 inhibition and reduced inflammatory markers
herb/lavanga.to: - Joint and muscle pain: traditionally used for joint and muscle pain. Studies have reported COX-2 inhibition and reduced inflammatory markers.

herb/lavanga.from: - Respiratory relief for cough and sore throat - supported by [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) and antimicrobial studies relevant to upper respiratory infections
herb/lavanga.to: - Cough and sore throat: traditionally used for cough and sore throat. Studies have reported [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) and antimicrobial activity.

herb/lasuna.from: - Cardiovascular protection (Hridya, Raktachapa-hara) extensively validated through clinical trials showing reduction in blood pressure, cholesterol, and platelet aggregation
herb/lasuna.to: - Cardiovascular use (Hridya, Raktachapa-hara): traditionally used for the heart and blood pressure. Clinical studies have reported reductions in blood pressure, cholesterol, and platelet aggregation.

herb/lasuna.from: - Antimicrobial use (Krimighna) confirmed against broad spectrum of pathogens including antibiotic-resistant bacteria (MRSA)
herb/lasuna.to: - Antimicrobial use (Krimighna): traditionally used against infections. Studies have reported activity against a broad range of pathogens, including antibiotic-resistant bacteria (MRSA).

herb/lasuna.from: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) use supported by clinical evidence of improved insulin sensitivity and reduced fasting blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) in type 2 diabetes patients
herb/lasuna.to: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) use: traditionally used in this role. Clinical studies in people with type 2 diabetes have reported improved insulin sensitivity and lower fasting blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose).

herb/laung.from: - Toothache and dental pain relief - extensively validated; eugenol is an established dental analgesic and antiseptic used worldwide in dental practice
herb/laung.to: - Toothache and dental pain: traditionally used for toothache and dental pain. Its component eugenol is used in dental practice as an analgesic and antiseptic.

herb/laung.from: - Antimicrobial for oral infections and wound care - confirmed by in vitro and clinical studies showing broad-spectrum activity including against MDR bacteria
herb/laung.to: - Oral infections and wound care: traditionally used for oral infections and wound care. In vitro and clinical studies have reported broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including against multidrug-resistant bacteria.

herb/laung.from: - Digestive aid for flatulence, colic, and nausea - supported by pharmacological studies demonstrating [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) and carminative effects
herb/laung.to: - Flatulence, colic and nausea: traditionally used as a digestive aid for flatulence, colic and nausea. Pharmacological studies have reported [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) and carminative effects.

herb/laung.from: - Anti-inflammatory for joint and muscle pain - validated by studies showing COX-2 inhibition and reduced inflammatory markers
herb/laung.to: - Joint and muscle pain: traditionally used for joint and muscle pain. Studies have reported COX-2 inhibition and reduced inflammatory markers.

herb/laung.from: - Respiratory relief for cough and sore throat - supported by [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) and antimicrobial studies relevant to upper respiratory infections
herb/laung.to: - Cough and sore throat: traditionally used for cough and sore throat. Studies have reported [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) and antimicrobial activity.

herb/ksheera.from: - [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (rejuvenating) and Ojas-enhancing properties validated through clinical nutrition studies confirming milk's role in improving immune function and tissue nourishment
herb/ksheera.to: - Traditionally used as a [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (rejuvenating) and Ojas-enhancing food. Clinical nutrition studies have reported a role for milk in immune function and tissue nourishment.

herb/ksheera.from: - Use as a pharmaceutical vehicle (Anupana/Ksheera Paka) validated - milk-based processing of herbs enhances bioavailability of lipophilic compounds while reducing irritant properties
herb/ksheera.to: - Used in classical practice as a pharmaceutical vehicle (Anupana/Ksheera Paka). Studies have reported that milk-based processing of herbs may increase the bioavailability of lipophilic compounds and reduce irritant properties.

herb/ksheera.from: - Ksheera Basti (milk enema) efficacy for Vataroga (neurological/musculoskeletal conditions) supported by clinical evidence for sciatica management
herb/ksheera.to: - Ksheera Basti (milk enema): traditionally used for Vataroga (neurological/musculoskeletal conditions). Clinical studies have reported benefit in sciatica.

herb/ksheera.from: Milk-based processing (Ksheera Paka) of Terminalia [arjuna](/herb/arjuna/) enhanced anti-inflammatory activity, validating the traditional Ayurvedic practice of using milk as a pharmaceutical vehicle/adjuvant.
herb/ksheera.to: A study reported that milk-based processing (Ksheera Paka) of Terminalia [arjuna](/herb/arjuna/) increased anti-inflammatory activity. In classical practice, milk is used as a pharmaceutical vehicle/adjuvant.

herb/makaradhwaj-vati.from: - [Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana) ([aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac)/vitality): Partially validated by Rasasindura studies showing activation of calcium channels, increased sperm count and motility, and rejuvenating effects in animal models
herb/makaradhwaj-vati.to: - [Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana) ([aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac)/vitality): traditionally used as an aphrodisiac and for vitality. Animal studies on Rasasindura have reported activation of calcium channels, increased sperm count and motility, and rejuvenating effects.

herb/makaradhwaj-vati.from: - Rasayana (rejuvenation) and general debility: Animal studies confirm absence of toxicity at therapeutic doses and suggest [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) and metabolic-enhancing properties, consistent with traditional claims of life-enhancing effects
herb/makaradhwaj-vati.to: - Rasayana (rejuvenation) and general debility: traditionally used for rejuvenation and general debility. Animal studies have reported no toxicity at the doses tested. They also suggested [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) and metabolic-enhancing properties.

herb/loha-bhasma.from: - Iron-deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga): Multiple clinical trials including multi-center and double-blind studies confirmed efficacy comparable to ferrous sulfate with better tolerability
herb/loha-bhasma.to: - Iron-deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga): traditionally used for iron-deficiency anemia. Clinical studies, including multi-center and double-blind studies, reported results comparable to ferrous sulfate with better tolerability.

herb/loha-bhasma.from: - Digestive disorders: Improved digestion and appetite confirmed through clinical observations; Agni-deepana (digestive fire enhancement) property validated
herb/loha-bhasma.to: - Digestive disorders: traditionally used to improve digestion and appetite, described as Agni-deepana (digestive fire enhancement). Clinical observations have reported improved digestion and appetite.

herb/loha-bhasma.from: - General debility and weakness (Daurbalya): Iron supplementation effects validated through hemoglobin improvement and clinical symptom resolution in multiple studies
herb/loha-bhasma.to: - General debility and weakness (Daurbalya): traditionally used for general debility and weakness. Clinical studies have reported improved hemoglobin levels and improved clinical symptoms.

herb/mahalakshmi-vilas-rasa.from: - Upper respiratory disorders (Urdhwa Jatrugata Roga): Clinical practice experience supports efficacy in rhinitis, sinusitis, and respiratory infections; the [camphor](/herb/camphor/) and nutmeg components have documented mucolytic and bronchodilatory properties
herb/mahalakshmi-vilas-rasa.to: - Upper respiratory disorders (Urdhwa Jatrugata Roga): traditionally used for rhinitis, sinusitis, and respiratory infections. The formulation includes [camphor](/herb/camphor/) and nutmeg.

herb/mahalakshmi-vilas-rasa.from: - Rheumatoid arthritis (Amavata): Traditional use supported by the multi-mineral anti-inflammatory composition; gold bhasma's [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) properties are relevant to autoimmune inflammatory conditions
herb/mahalakshmi-vilas-rasa.to: - Rheumatoid arthritis (Amavata): traditionally used for this condition. The formulation has a multi-mineral composition that includes gold bhasma.

herb/lohasava.from: - Iron deficiency anemia - validated by comparative study showing Lohasava was more effective than conventional iron therapy in improving hemoglobin and iron parameters
herb/lohasava.to: - Iron deficiency anemia: traditionally used for iron deficiency anemia. A comparative study reported greater improvement in hemoglobin and iron parameters with Lohasava than with conventional iron therapy.

herb/lohasava.from: - Liver and digestive disorders - traditional [hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) and digestive claims supported by pharmacological actions of [Triphala](/herb/triphala/) and [Trikatu](/herb/trikatu/) components and the bioenhancing fermentation process
herb/lohasava.to: - Liver and digestive disorders: traditionally used as a [hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) and digestive formulation. In classical practice, these uses are attributed to its [Triphala](/herb/triphala/) and [Trikatu](/herb/trikatu/) components and its fermentation process.

herb/madanaphala.from: - Therapeutic emetic use (Vamana) validated by saponin-mediated gastric mucosal irritation and CTZ stimulation
herb/madanaphala.to: - Traditionally used as a therapeutic emetic in Vamana.

herb/madanaphala.from: - Anti-inflammatory use for respiratory disorders supported by IL-1beta reduction in human lung epithelial cells
herb/madanaphala.to: - Traditionally used for respiratory disorders. An in vitro study in human lung epithelial cells reported reduced IL-1beta.

herb/madanaphala.from: - Wound healing activity confirmed through [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and collagen synthesis promotion in excision wound models
herb/madanaphala.to: - Traditionally used for wound healing. Animal studies in excision wound models have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity and increased collagen synthesis.

herb/mahamanjishthadi.from: - Blood purification and skin disease management (Raktashodhana for Kushtha/Twak Vikara) validated through antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory studies of the formulation and its principal ingredient [Manjistha](/herb/manjistha/)
herb/mahamanjishthadi.to: - Traditionally used for blood purification and skin disease (Raktashodhana for Kushtha/Twak Vikara). Studies of the formulation and its principal ingredient [Manjistha](/herb/manjistha/) have reported antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/mahamanjishthadi.from: - Anti-allergic application validated through pharmacological studies demonstrating histamine inhibition, confirming traditional use in Sheetapitta (urticaria) and allergic conditions
herb/mahamanjishthadi.to: - Traditionally used in Sheetapitta (urticaria) and allergic conditions. Pharmacological studies have reported histamine inhibition.

herb/mahamanjishthadi.from: - Lymphatic system support and anti-inflammatory application partially validated through documented anti-inflammatory and [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) activities, supporting use in chronic inflammatory conditions like PCOS and arthritis
herb/mahamanjishthadi.to: - Traditionally used for lymphatic system support and in chronic inflammatory conditions such as PCOS and arthritis. Studies have reported anti-inflammatory and [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) activity.

herb/madhu-mandur.from: answer: "Madhu Mandur is a bhasma, a mineral or metal preparation reduced to ash by repeated calcination. Iron deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga) - validated by clinical studies showing significant hemoglobin improvement, especially with honey co-administration Anemia in children - validated by clinical evaluation showing 21.86% hemoglobin increase with honey + Mandur Bhasma combination"
herb/madhu-mandur.to: answer: "Madhu Mandur is a bhasma, a mineral or metal preparation reduced to ash by repeated calcination. It is traditionally used for iron deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga), including anemia in children. Clinical studies have reported improvement in hemoglobin, especially when it was given with honey. A clinical evaluation in children reported an increase in hemoglobin with a combination of honey and Mandur Bhasma."

herb/madhu-mandur.from: - Iron deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga) - validated by clinical studies showing significant hemoglobin improvement, especially with honey co-administration
herb/madhu-mandur.to: - Iron deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga): traditionally used for this condition. Clinical studies have reported improvement in hemoglobin, especially when it was given with honey.

herb/madhu-mandur.from: - Anemia in children - validated by clinical evaluation showing 21.86% hemoglobin increase with honey + Mandur Bhasma combination
herb/madhu-mandur.to: - Anemia in children: traditionally used for anemia in children. A clinical evaluation reported an increase in hemoglobin with a combination of honey and Mandur Bhasma.

herb/madhu.from: - Anupana (drug carrier): Scientific evidence confirms honey enhances bioavailability of herbal compounds through osmotic facilitation, enzyme-mediated absorption, and tissue penetration - validating Yogavahi concept
herb/madhu.to: - Anupana (drug carrier): traditionally used as a carrier for other herbs, reflecting the Yogavahi concept. Studies have reported that honey may enhance the bioavailability of herbal compounds through osmotic facilitation, enzyme-mediated absorption, and tissue penetration.

herb/madhu.from: - Vrana Ropana (wound healing): Extensive clinical evidence supports honey's antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and tissue-regenerative properties in both acute and chronic wounds
herb/madhu.to: - Vrana Ropana (wound healing): traditionally used on wounds. Clinical studies have reported antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and tissue-regenerative properties of honey in both acute and chronic wounds.

herb/madhu.from: - Kasa-Shwasa (cough and respiratory disorders): WHO recommends honey for childhood cough; clinical trials show honey is more effective than dextromethorphan for nocturnal cough relief
herb/madhu.to: - Kasa-Shwasa (cough and respiratory disorders): traditionally used for cough and respiratory complaints. Clinical studies have reported that honey reduced nocturnal cough in children more than dextromethorphan.

herb/madhu.from: - Heating honey above 40 degrees C produces hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), a potentially toxic compound; Ayurvedic prohibition of heated honey validated by modern chemistry
herb/madhu.to: - Classical Ayurvedic practice prohibits heating honey. Chemical analyses have reported that heating honey produces hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), a potentially toxic compound.

herb/mahabala.from: - Anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties validated through multiple in vivo models, confirming traditional use in Vataroga (joint and muscular conditions)
herb/mahabala.to: - Traditionally used in Vataroga (joint and muscular conditions). Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory and analgesic activity.

herb/mahabala.from: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity confirmed against bacteria and fungi, supporting traditional use in wound healing and infectious conditions
herb/mahabala.to: - Traditionally used for wounds and infectious conditions. [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity against bacteria and fungi has been reported in studies.

herb/mahabala.from: - Antimalaria activity validated against Plasmodium species, confirming ethnomedicinal use in fever and malaria treatment
herb/mahabala.to: - Used in ethnomedicine for fever and malaria. Studies have reported antimalarial activity against Plasmodium species.

herb/madhuka.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) use validated through carrageenan-induced paw edema and hot plate models
herb/madhuka.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation and as an [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/). Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory and analgesic activity in paw edema and hot plate models.

herb/madhuka.from: - Antiulcer activity confirmed in aspirin-induced and ethanol-induced gastric ulcer models
herb/madhuka.to: - Animal studies have reported antiulcer activity in aspirin-induced and ethanol-induced gastric ulcer models.

herb/madhuka.from: - Oral health use validated through antibacterial activity against Streptococcus mutans
herb/madhuka.to: - Traditionally used for oral health. In vitro studies have reported antibacterial activity against Streptococcus mutans.

herb/madhuka.from: - Skin emollient use of seed oil (mahua butter) validated through moisturizing and barrier function studies
herb/madhuka.to: - The seed oil (mahua butter) is traditionally used as a skin emollient. Studies have reported moisturizing and skin barrier activity.

herb/madhuka.from: Madhuca longifolia stem extract demonstrated significant antibacterial activity against Streptococcus mutans, validating traditional use for oral health and dental hygiene.
herb/madhuka.to: Madhuca longifolia is traditionally used for oral health and dental hygiene. An in vitro study reported antibacterial activity of the stem extract against Streptococcus mutans.

herb/meda.from: - Antimalarial and [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) properties validated through in vivo studies using Plasmodium models and fever-inducing paradigms
herb/meda.to: - Animal studies using Plasmodium models and fever-inducing models have reported antimalarial and [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity.

herb/meda.from: - [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) activity confirmed through experimental models, supporting traditional use in urinary disorders and as a body purifier
herb/meda.to: - Traditionally used in urinary disorders and as a body purifier. Experimental studies have reported [diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) activity.

herb/meda.from: - Antibacterial and antifungal activity validated against multiple pathogenic organisms, confirming traditional use in infection management
herb/meda.to: - Traditionally used for infections. Laboratory studies have reported antibacterial and antifungal activity against several disease-causing organisms.

herb/mishreya.from: - Carminative and digestive properties extensively validated through clinical and pharmacological studies, confirming premier Ayurvedic use as Deepana-Pachana (appetite and digestion promoter)
herb/mishreya.to: - Traditionally used as Deepana-Pachana (appetite and digestion promoter). Clinical and pharmacological studies have reported carminative and digestive activity.

herb/mishreya.from: - Galactagogue (breast milk promoting) activity supported by clinical evidence showing increased milk production in breastfeeding women, confirming traditional Stanyajanana use
herb/mishreya.to: - Traditionally used as Stanyajanana (breast milk promoting). Clinical studies have reported increased milk production in breastfeeding women.

herb/mishreya.from: - Antispasmodic activity in infantile colic validated through randomized clinical trials, confirming traditional use for pediatric GI complaints
herb/mishreya.to: - Traditionally used for pediatric GI complaints. Randomized clinical trials have reported antispasmodic activity in infantile colic.

herb/mudgaparni.from: - Hepatoprotective property validated through preclinical studies showing protection against chemically induced liver damage, confirming traditional use in [Kamala](/herb/kamala/) (jaundice)
herb/mudgaparni.to: - Traditionally used for [Kamala](/herb/kamala/) (jaundice). Preclinical studies have reported protection against chemically induced liver damage.

herb/mudgaparni.from: - Antidiabetic activity experimentally confirmed with significant blood glucose reduction, supporting traditional use as a nutritive and metabolic regulator
herb/mudgaparni.to: - Traditionally used as a nutritive and metabolic regulator. Experimental studies have reported a reduction in blood glucose.

herb/mudgaparni.from: - Anthelmintic traditional use supported by documented antimicrobial activities against various pathogens
herb/mudgaparni.to: - Traditionally used as an anthelmintic. Studies have reported antimicrobial activity against various pathogens.

herb/manikya-pishti.from: - Immunostimulation and tuberculosis (Rajayakshma): The documented anticancer/apoptotic and immunomodulatory properties of ruby nanoparticles provide preliminary mechanistic support for traditional immune-enhancing claims
herb/manikya-pishti.to: - Immunostimulation and tuberculosis (Rajayakshma): traditionally used to enhance immunity and for Rajayakshma. Studies on ruby nanoparticles have reported anticancer, apoptotic and immunomodulatory activity.

herb/manikya-pishti.from: - Cognitive enhancement and neuroprotection: Preclinical neuroprotective studies validate the traditional use for improving Buddhi (intellect) and Smriti (memory)
herb/manikya-pishti.to: - Cognitive enhancement and neuroprotection: traditionally used for improving Buddhi (intellect) and Smriti (memory). Preclinical studies have reported neuroprotective effects.

herb/mandura-bhasma.from: - Iron-deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga): Clinical trials confirmed significant hemoglobin improvement (1.2 g/dL over 8 weeks) with no adverse effects
herb/mandura-bhasma.to: - Iron-deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga): traditionally used for this condition. Clinical studies have reported improvement in hemoglobin levels, with no adverse effects reported.

herb/mandura-bhasma.from: - Menstrual disorders (Raktapradar): Over 40% reduction in menstrual blood loss in 65 women within two treatment cycles
herb/mandura-bhasma.to: - Menstrual disorders (Raktapradar): traditionally used for this condition. A clinical study in women reported reduced menstrual blood loss.

herb/mandura-bhasma.from: - Liver and spleen enlargement (Yakrit-Pleeha Vikara): Hepatoprotective activity and reticuloendothelial support partially validated through preclinical studies
herb/mandura-bhasma.to: - Liver and spleen enlargement (Yakrit-Pleeha Vikara): traditionally used for this condition. Preclinical studies have reported hepatoprotective activity and reticuloendothelial support.

herb/matulunga.from: - Digestive stimulant (Deepana-Pachana) activity validated through pharmacological studies confirming enhanced gastric motility and enzyme secretion, supporting traditional Ayurvedic use for Agnimandya (digestive weakness)
herb/matulunga.to: - Digestive stimulant (Deepana-Pachana): traditionally used in Ayurveda for Agnimandya (digestive weakness). Pharmacological studies have reported enhanced gastric motility and enzyme secretion.

herb/matulunga.from: - Anti-emetic and Hridya (cardiac tonic) effects confirmed through hesperidin-mediated cardioprotective studies, supporting traditional use in Pitta disorders and cardiac conditions
herb/matulunga.to: - Anti-emetic and Hridya (cardiac tonic): traditionally used in Pitta disorders and cardiac conditions. Studies on hesperidin have reported cardioprotective effects.

herb/matulunga.from: - Anthelmintic activity confirmed through in vitro studies against intestinal parasites, supporting traditional use of citron rind preparations for Krimi (worms)
herb/matulunga.to: - Anthelmintic: citron rind preparations are traditionally used for Krimi (worms). In vitro studies have reported activity against intestinal parasites.

herb/mashaparni.from: - Anti-inflammatory activity validated through isolation of vitexin as a key 5-LOX inhibitor, confirming traditional use in inflammatory conditions and rheumatism
herb/mashaparni.to: - Traditionally used for inflammatory conditions and rheumatism. A study that isolated vitexin reported it as a key 5-LOX inhibitor with anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/mashaparni.from: - Immunomodulatory properties experimentally confirmed, supporting traditional use as a body strengthener and vitality enhancer
herb/mashaparni.to: - Traditionally used as a body strengthener and vitality enhancer. Experimental studies have reported immunomodulatory properties.

herb/mashaparni.from: - Antidiabetic potential supported by in vivo studies with [coumarin](/glossary/compounds-c-d/#coumarin)-rich fractions, partially validating traditional use in Prameha (metabolic disorders)
herb/mashaparni.to: - Traditionally used in Prameha (metabolic disorders). In vivo studies with [coumarin](/glossary/compounds-c-d/#coumarin)-rich fractions have reported antidiabetic potential.

herb/mrigashringa-bhasma.from: - Respiratory infections (pneumonia, bronchitis, influenza): Mucolytic and anti-inflammatory properties provide mechanistic basis; traditional use extensively documented
herb/mrigashringa-bhasma.to: - Respiratory infections (pneumonia, bronchitis, influenza): traditionally used for these conditions. This traditional use is extensively documented.

herb/mrigashringa-bhasma.from: - Bone disorders and osteoporosis: Optimal Ca:P ratio and osteoporosis prevention in animal model (Calci-7 study) validates traditional use for Asthi Kshaya
