herb/mrigashringa-bhasma.to: - Bone disorders and osteoporosis: traditionally used for Asthi Kshaya. An animal study reported an optimal Ca:P ratio and a protective effect against osteoporosis.

herb/mrigashringa-bhasma.from: - Cardiac conditions (Hritshula - cardiac pain): Calcium and potassium content supports cardiac function; traditional use for angina pectoris and cardiac pain documented since Samhita period
herb/mrigashringa-bhasma.to: - Cardiac conditions (Hritshula - cardiac pain): traditionally used for angina pectoris and cardiac pain. This use is documented since the Samhita period.

herb/mochras.from: - Hemostatic and styptic (Raktastambhana) - validated through astringent tannin-mediated hemostatic action in wound care
herb/mochras.to: - Hemostatic and styptic (Raktastambhana): traditionally used to stop bleeding in wound care. This action is attributed to its astringent tannins.

herb/mochras.from: - Anti-diarrheal (Atisara-nashaka) - confirmed through tannin-mediated reduction of intestinal secretion and hypermotility
herb/mochras.to: - Anti-diarrheal (Atisara-nashaka): traditionally used for diarrhea. This action is attributed to its tannins, which are described as reducing intestinal secretion and hypermotility.

herb/mochras.from: - Bone and tissue regeneration (Asthi-Sandhanakara) - traditional reputation as bone setter supported by anti-inflammatory and wound healing data
herb/mochras.to: - Bone and tissue regeneration (Asthi-Sandhanakara): traditionally known as a bone setter. Studies have reported anti-inflammatory and wound healing activity.

herb/mochras.from: - [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac) ([Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana)) - traditional use of [Shalmali](/herb/shalmali/) resin for sexual health partially supported by nutritional and hormonal modulation studies
herb/mochras.to: - [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac) ([Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana)): [Shalmali](/herb/shalmali/) resin is traditionally used for sexual health. Studies have looked at its nutritional value and reported hormonal modulation.

herb/navayasa-loha.from: - Iron deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga) - validated in multiple clinical and observational studies showing statistically significant increases in hemoglobin, PCV, and RBC count
herb/navayasa-loha.to: - Iron deficiency anemia (Pandu Roga): traditionally used for this condition. Clinical and observational studies have reported increases in hemoglobin, PCV, and RBC count.

herb/navayasa-loha.from: - General debility and weakness associated with anemia - clinical studies confirm improvement in energy levels, appetite, and overall vitality metrics
herb/navayasa-loha.to: - General debility and weakness associated with anemia: traditionally used for this condition. Clinical studies have reported improvement in energy levels, appetite, and overall vitality.

herb/mukta-pishti.from: - Anxiety and palpitations (Hridrava, Chittodvega): Clinical practice evidence and mechanistic rationale (calcium-mediated cardiac stabilization, conchiolin peptide neurotransmitter modulation) support the traditional use for heart and mind calming
herb/mukta-pishti.to: - Anxiety and palpitations (Hridrava, Chittodvega): traditionally used to calm the heart and mind.

herb/mukta-pishti.from: - Gastric disorders (Amlapitta, Parinamashoola): 2025 preclinical study validated anti-ulcerogenic activity; the calcium carbonate-based acid neutralization mechanism directly supports the traditional antacid use
herb/mukta-pishti.to: - Gastric disorders (Amlapitta, Parinamashoola): traditionally used as an antacid. A preclinical study reported anti-ulcerogenic activity.

herb/nikochaka.from: answer: "Nikochaka (Alangium salviifolium) is a plant drug, also called Ankolah, Akola and Nikocaka. Traditional uses cannot be validated without confirmed botanical identity Name may appear in specific Nighantu (Ayurvedic lexicon) texts such as Dhanvantari Nighantu, Raja Nighantu, or Bhavaprakasha Nighantu requiring targeted scholarly investigation"
herb/nikochaka.to: answer: "Nikochaka (Alangium salviifolium) is a plant drug, also called Ankolah, Akola and Nikocaka. Its traditional uses remain uncertain until its botanical identity is settled. The name may appear in specific Nighantu (Ayurvedic lexicon) texts such as Dhanvantari Nighantu, Raja Nighantu, or Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, which would need targeted scholarly investigation."

herb/nikochaka.from: - Traditional uses cannot be validated without confirmed botanical identity
herb/nikochaka.to: - Traditional uses remain uncertain until the botanical identity is settled

herb/nagabala.from: - Nervine tonic (Medhya) use partially supported by antioxidant activity in brain tissue and [neuroprotective](/reference/neuroprotective/) properties of phenolic constituents
herb/nagabala.to: - Nervine tonic (Medhya): traditionally used as a nervine tonic. Studies have reported antioxidant activity in brain tissue and [neuroprotective](/reference/neuroprotective/) properties of phenolic constituents.

herb/nagabala.from: - [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac) and rejuvenative ([Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana)-[Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)) use based on traditional clinical evidence; awaits modern clinical validation
herb/nagabala.to: - [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac) and rejuvenative ([Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana)-[Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)): used in classical practice as an aphrodisiac and rejuvenative.

herb/nagabala.from: - Cardiac tonic (Hridya) use supported by preliminary evidence of positive inotropic effect and [cardioprotective](/reference/cardioprotective/) antioxidant activity
herb/nagabala.to: - Cardiac tonic (Hridya): traditionally used as a cardiac tonic. Preliminary studies have reported a positive inotropic effect and [cardioprotective](/reference/cardioprotective/) antioxidant activity.

herb/navaratna-raja-mriganka-rasa.from: - Rejuvenation and anti-aging (Rasayana) - traditional use as a potent rejuvenative for debility and aging; limited modern validation due to safety concerns precluding clinical trials
herb/navaratna-raja-mriganka-rasa.to: - Rejuvenation and anti-aging (Rasayana): traditionally used as a potent rejuvenative for debility and aging. Modern research is limited because safety concerns have precluded clinical trials.

herb/navaratna-raja-mriganka-rasa.from: - Tridosha balance and multi-system tonic - traditional claim for balancing all three Doshas; conceptually supported by the multi-mineral composition but lacks rigorous clinical evidence
herb/navaratna-raja-mriganka-rasa.to: - Tridosha balance and multi-system tonic: traditionally used for balancing all three Doshas. Rigorous clinical evidence is lacking.

herb/neelam-pishti.from: - Respiratory conditions (Shwasa, Kasa): Traditional indications for dyspnea and cough lack specific clinical validation for [Neelam Pishti](/herb/neelam-pishti/); the aluminum oxide base has no established respiratory pharmacology
herb/neelam-pishti.to: - Respiratory conditions (Shwasa, Kasa): traditionally, [Neelam Pishti](/herb/neelam-pishti/) is used for dyspnea and cough.

herb/neelam-pishti.from: - General tonic and Tridosha balancer: Traditional claim of nourishing all Dhatus and pacifying Tridosha has theoretical Ayurvedic rationale but no modern scientific validation
herb/neelam-pishti.to: - General tonic and Tridosha balancer: traditionally used to nourish all Dhatus and pacify Tridosha.

herb/narikela.from: - Urinary disorder (Mutraroga) treatment validated through [diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) and nephroprotective preclinical studies
herb/narikela.to: - Mutraroga (urinary disorders): traditionally used for urinary disorders. Preclinical studies have reported [diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) and nephroprotective activity.

herb/narikela.from: - Wound healing use of [coconut oil](/glossary/concepts-a-m/#coconut-oil) validated through antimicrobial and epithelialization studies
herb/narikela.to: - Wounds: [coconut oil](/glossary/concepts-a-m/#coconut-oil) is traditionally applied to wounds. Studies have reported antimicrobial activity and effects on epithelialization.

herb/narikela.from: - Rehydration use of coconut water validated through electrolyte composition analysis comparable to ORS formulations
herb/narikela.to: - Rehydration: coconut water is traditionally used for rehydration. An analysis of its electrolyte composition reported it as comparable to ORS formulations.

herb/narikela.from: - Skin care (Charma roga) use validated through emollient, antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties of virgin [coconut oil](/glossary/concepts-a-m/#coconut-oil)
herb/narikela.to: - Charma roga (skin disorders): traditionally used in skin care. Studies have reported emollient, antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties of virgin [coconut oil](/glossary/concepts-a-m/#coconut-oil).

herb/nili.from: - Psoriasis treatment: Validated by 2024 comprehensive review and transdermal patch studies confirming synergistic anti-psoriatic activity of indigo, indirubin, and tryptanthrin
herb/nili.to: - Psoriasis: a review and transdermal patch studies have reported combined anti-psoriatic activity of indigo, indirubin, and tryptanthrin.

herb/nili.from: - Hair and scalp health: Validated by traditional use as hair dye and conditioner, with EU safety assessment confirming safety for hair coloring applications
herb/nili.to: - Hair and scalp health: traditionally used as a hair dye and conditioner. An EU safety assessment has reported on its safety for hair coloring applications.

herb/nili.from: - Eczema management: Validated by 2023 pilot clinical trial showing 70% symptom improvement with 3% Nili extract gel in 30 patients
herb/nili.to: - Eczema: a pilot clinical study reported symptom improvement with a Nili extract gel.

herb/nili.from: - Wound healing: Supported by animal studies showing accelerated wound closure, enhanced collagen synthesis, and reduced inflammatory markers
herb/nili.to: - Wound healing: animal studies have reported faster wound closure, increased collagen synthesis, and reduced inflammatory markers.

herb/murva.from: - Anti-tumor and anti-cancer activity validated through extensive in vitro and in vivo studies showing inhibition of multiple cancer cell lines (A549, HepG2, Caco-2, K562)
herb/murva.to: - In vitro and animal studies have reported anti-tumor activity, including inhibition of several cancer cell lines.

herb/murva.from: - Anti-HIV activity confirmed through laboratory studies demonstrating inhibition of viral replication
herb/murva.to: - Laboratory studies have reported anti-HIV activity, including inhibition of viral replication.

herb/murva.from: - [Immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) properties validated through polysaccharide-mediated activation of immune signaling pathways
herb/murva.to: - [Immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) properties have been reported in studies, linked to polysaccharides activating immune signaling pathways.

herb/naga-bhasma.from: - Purported splenic decongestant action (Pleehodara) through unknown mechanisms; traditional claim not validated by modern research
herb/naga-bhasma.to: - Pleehodara: traditionally described as having a splenic decongestant action. The mechanism is unknown, and modern research has not backed this traditional claim.

herb/naga-bhasma.from: - Diabetes (Madhumeha): UNVALIDATED - No modern clinical evidence supports lead as safe or effective anti-diabetic agent. Risk far outweighs any theoretical benefit.
herb/naga-bhasma.to: - Diabetes (Madhumeha): traditionally used for this condition. No modern clinical evidence shows lead to be safe for this use. The risk far outweighs any theoretical benefit.

herb/naga-bhasma.from: - Spleen enlargement (Pleehodara): UNVALIDATED - No clinical trials support this use. Lead toxicity itself causes organ damage.
herb/naga-bhasma.to: - Spleen enlargement (Pleehodara): traditionally used for this condition. No clinical trial evidence exists for this use. Lead toxicity itself causes organ damage.

herb/naga-bhasma.from: - Skin diseases (Kushtha): UNVALIDATED and DANGEROUS - Lead exposure causes additional skin and systemic toxicity rather than healing.
herb/naga-bhasma.to: - Skin diseases (Kushtha): traditionally used for these conditions. This use is untested and dangerous. Lead exposure causes more skin and systemic toxicity.

herb/panna-pishti.from: - Digestive and hepatic disorders: Traditional use in liver disorders has theoretical support from the trace chromium content's potential role in metabolic regulation, but no clinical trials validate this specific indication
herb/panna-pishti.to: - Digestive and hepatic disorders: traditionally used for liver disorders. No clinical trials have been reported for this specific use.

herb/panna-pishti.from: - Cooling and Pitta-pacifying: Traditional cooling use has Ayurvedic theoretical basis but lacks modern pharmacological validation specific to emerald-derived preparations
herb/panna-pishti.to: - Cooling and Pitta-pacifying: traditionally used in Ayurveda as a cooling, Pitta-pacifying preparation. No modern pharmacological studies specific to emerald-derived preparations have been reported.

herb/panchamrita-parpati.from: answer: "Panchamrita Parpati is a rasa preparation, a herbo-mineral formulation of the rasa shastra tradition. Grahani Roga (malabsorption syndrome/chronic diarrhea/IBS-like conditions) - validated by RCT and clinical studies showing improvement in digestive symptoms Agni Mandya (weak digestive fire) with Ama formation - traditional primary indication supported by known Deepana-Pachana properties of constituent Bhasmas"
herb/panchamrita-parpati.to: answer: "Panchamrita Parpati is a rasa preparation, a herbo-mineral formulation of the rasa shastra tradition. It is traditionally used for Grahani Roga (malabsorption syndrome/chronic diarrhea/IBS-like conditions). Clinical studies, including a randomized controlled trial, have reported improvement in digestive symptoms. It is also traditionally used for Agni Mandya (weak digestive fire) with Ama formation, a primary classical indication. Its constituent Bhasmas are traditionally described as having Deepana-Pachana properties."

herb/panchamrita-parpati.from: - Grahani Roga (malabsorption syndrome/chronic diarrhea/IBS-like conditions) - validated by RCT and clinical studies showing improvement in digestive symptoms
herb/panchamrita-parpati.to: - Grahani Roga (malabsorption syndrome/chronic diarrhea/IBS-like conditions): traditionally used for this condition. Clinical studies, including a randomized controlled trial, have reported improvement in digestive symptoms.

herb/panchamrita-parpati.from: - Agni Mandya (weak digestive fire) with Ama formation - traditional primary indication supported by known Deepana-Pachana properties of constituent Bhasmas
herb/panchamrita-parpati.to: - Agni Mandya (weak digestive fire) with Ama formation: a primary traditional indication. The constituent Bhasmas are traditionally described as having Deepana-Pachana properties.

herb/nityananda-rasa.from: - Shlipada (elephantiasis/lymphatic filariasis) - primary traditional indication referenced in Bhaishajya Ratnavali; modern toxicity study supports safety at therapeutic doses enabling continued traditional use under supervision
herb/nityananda-rasa.to: - Shlipada (elephantiasis/lymphatic filariasis): primary traditional indication, referenced in Bhaishajya Ratnavali. A toxicity study reported no safety concerns at the doses tested.

herb/nityananda-rasa.from: - Gout (Vatarakta) and obesity (Sthoulya) - traditional use supported by the Kapha-[Meda](/herb/meda/) reducing (Lekhaniya) properties of [Tamra Bhasma](/herb/tamra-bhasma/) and the metabolic-enhancing actions of [Trikatu](/herb/trikatu/)
herb/nityananda-rasa.to: - Vatarakta (gout) and Sthoulya (obesity): traditionally used for these conditions. In classical description, [Tamra Bhasma](/herb/tamra-bhasma/) is Kapha- and [Meda](/herb/meda/)-reducing (Lekhaniya), and [Trikatu](/herb/trikatu/) is described as metabolism-enhancing.

herb/nimbu.from: - Digestive aid (Deepana-Pachana) use validated through carminative and stomachic effects in clinical observations
herb/nimbu.to: - Digestive aid (Deepana-Pachana): traditionally used as a digestive aid. Clinical observations have reported carminative and stomachic effects.

herb/nimbu.from: - Scurvy prevention and Vitamin C source validated historically and through nutritional studies
herb/nimbu.to: - Scurvy: traditionally used for scurvy and valued as a source of Vitamin C. Nutritional studies have reported it to be a source of Vitamin C.

herb/nimbu.from: - Antimicrobial and preservative use validated through extensive food science and MIC studies against multiple pathogens
herb/nimbu.to: - Antimicrobial and preservative: traditionally used as an antimicrobial and preservative. Food science and MIC studies have reported activity against multiple pathogens.

herb/nimbu.from: - Kidney stone prevention supported by urinary citrate-increasing effects documented in clinical studies
herb/nimbu.to: - Kidney stones: traditionally used for kidney stones. Clinical studies have reported an increase in urinary citrate.

herb/parijata.from: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) and antimalarial use for fevers validated through Plasmodium berghei-infected mouse models and clinical observations
herb/parijata.to: - Traditionally used for fevers as an [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) and antimalarial. Animal studies in Plasmodium berghei-infected mice have reported antimalarial activity.

herb/parijata.from: - Anti-arthritic use confirmed through adjuvant-induced arthritis models with significant reduction in paw edema and joint inflammation
herb/parijata.to: - Traditionally used for arthritis. Animal studies in adjuvant-induced arthritis models have reported reduced paw edema and joint inflammation.

herb/parijata.from: - Anthelmintic activity validated against Ascaridia galli and Pheretima posthuma in vitro
herb/parijata.to: - In vitro studies have reported anthelmintic activity against Ascaridia galli and Pheretima posthuma.

herb/parijata.from: - Hepatoprotective effects confirmed against paracetamol-induced liver damage in rodent models
herb/parijata.to: - Animal studies in rodents have reported protective effects against paracetamol-induced liver damage.

herb/nyagrodha.from: - Antidiabetic use confirmed through multiple in vivo studies demonstrating significant hypoglycemic activity
herb/nyagrodha.to: - Antidiabetic use: animal studies have reported hypoglycemic activity.

herb/nyagrodha.from: - Anti-diarrheal and dysentery treatment validated via castor oil-induced diarrhea models and [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) testing
herb/nyagrodha.to: - Traditionally used for diarrhea and dysentery. Animal studies using castor oil-induced diarrhea models have reported anti-diarrheal activity. Laboratory testing has also reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity.

herb/nyagrodha.from: - Wound healing confirmed through excision wound models with accelerated closure and collagen synthesis
herb/nyagrodha.to: - Traditionally used for wounds. Animal studies using excision wound models have reported faster wound closure and increased collagen synthesis.

herb/nyagrodha.from: - [Analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) properties validated in hot plate and tail flick animal models
herb/nyagrodha.to: - [Analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) properties: animal studies using hot plate and tail flick models have reported pain-reducing activity.

herb/nimba.from: - Acne treatment (Yauvanpidika): Validated by clinical trial showing 79% of participants had reduced inflammatory acne with [neem](/herb/neem/) face wash
herb/nimba.to: - Acne (Yauvanpidika): traditionally used for acne. A clinical study reported reduced inflammatory acne in participants using a [neem](/herb/neem/) face wash.

herb/nimba.from: - Antifungal skin infections (Dadru/Kushtha): Validated by demonstrated broad-spectrum antifungal activity against dermatophytes and Malassezia
herb/nimba.to: - Fungal skin infections (Dadru/Kushtha): traditionally used for fungal skin infections. Research has reported broad-spectrum antifungal activity against dermatophytes and Malassezia.

herb/nimba.from: - Dandruff/scalp conditions: 2025 clinical study confirmed efficacy of [neem](/herb/neem/) leaf paste for dandruff reduction
herb/nimba.to: - Dandruff/scalp conditions: traditionally used for dandruff and scalp conditions. A clinical study reported reduced dandruff with [neem](/herb/neem/) leaf paste.

herb/nimba.from: - Wound healing and antiseptic use (Vrana): Supported by antimicrobial activity against major wound-infecting pathogens
herb/nimba.to: - Wounds and antiseptic use (Vrana): traditionally used on wounds and as an antiseptic. Research has reported antimicrobial activity against major wound-infecting pathogens.

herb/nimba.from: Clinical study demonstrated neem leaf paste application significantly reduced dandruff symptoms, validating traditional antifungal use for scalp conditions caused by Malassezia species.
herb/nimba.to: A clinical study reported that applying neem leaf paste reduced dandruff symptoms. Neem is traditionally used for scalp conditions, including those linked to Malassezia species.

herb/palankya.from: - Cooling and pitta-pacifying (Pittahara) - validated through confirmed anti-inflammatory and [antioxidant](/reference/antioxidant/) cooling properties
herb/palankya.to: - Cooling and pitta-pacifying (Pittahara): traditionally used as a cooling herb to pacify pitta.

herb/palankya.from: - [Laxative](/reference/laxative/) (Bhedana) - confirmed mild laxative effect through dietary fiber and [magnesium](/glossary/compounds-l-o/#magnesium) content
herb/palankya.to: - [Laxative](/reference/laxative/) (Bhedana): traditionally used as a mild laxative. The leaves contain dietary fiber and [magnesium](/glossary/compounds-l-o/#magnesium).

herb/palankya.from: - Blood builder (Raktavardhaka) - supported by high folate and iron content for hemoglobin synthesis (though iron bioavailability reduced by oxalates)
herb/palankya.to: - Blood builder (Raktavardhaka): traditionally used to build the blood. The leaves contain folate and iron, though oxalates reduce how well the iron is absorbed.

herb/palankya.from: - Eye health ([Chakshushya](/herb/chakshushya/)) - strongly validated through lutein and zeaxanthin's proven role in macular health and AMD prevention
herb/palankya.to: - Eye health ([Chakshushya](/herb/chakshushya/)): traditionally used to support the eyes. The leaves contain lutein and zeaxanthin.

herb/nirgundi.from: - Anti-arthritic and anti-inflammatory use (Amavata treatment) extensively validated through carrageenan, formaldehyde, and adjuvant arthritis models
herb/nirgundi.to: - Amavata: traditionally used in classical practice for this condition. Animal studies using carrageenan, formaldehyde, and adjuvant arthritis models have reported anti-arthritic and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/nirgundi.from: - Analgesic use (Vedana-sthapana) confirmed through central and peripheral pain models (hot plate, acetic acid writhing, formalin test)
herb/nirgundi.to: - Vedana-sthapana: traditionally used for pain. Animal studies using central and peripheral pain models (hot plate, acetic acid writhing, formalin test) have reported analgesic activity.

herb/nirgundi.from: - [Hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) use validated by reduction of AST, ALT, and restoration of liver architecture in CCl4-induced hepatotoxicity models
herb/nirgundi.to: - [Hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) use: animal studies of carbon tetrachloride-induced liver toxicity have reported lower AST and ALT levels and restored liver architecture.

herb/nirgundi.from: Identified pharmacologically significant flavonoids (vitexin, casticin), iridoid glycosides (agnuside), [lignans](/glossary/compounds-g-l/#lignans), and essential oils with validated analgesic and anti-inflammatory mechanisms.
herb/nirgundi.to: Identified pharmacologically significant flavonoids (vitexin, casticin), iridoid glycosides (agnuside), [lignans](/glossary/compounds-g-l/#lignans), and essential oils, with reported analgesic and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/padmaka.from: - Complexion enhancement (Varnya): Traditional face pack use supported by antioxidant activity and development of Padmaka-based cosmetic face serum (2024 study)
herb/padmaka.to: - Complexion enhancement (Varnya): traditionally used in face packs. Research has reported antioxidant activity, and a Padmaka-based cosmetic face serum has been developed.

herb/padmaka.from: - Anti-inflammatory skin rash relief: Validated by bark powder application studies showing reduction in skin rashes and itching through NF-kB suppression
herb/padmaka.to: - Skin rashes and itching: studies of bark powder application have reported reduced skin rashes and itching, linked to NF-kB suppression.

herb/padmaka.from: - Skin discoloration treatment: Traditional heartwood use for discoloration partially supported by antioxidant mechanisms, though clinical trials are needed
herb/padmaka.to: - Skin discoloration: the heartwood is traditionally used for discoloration. Research has reported antioxidant activity, but clinical trials are still needed.

herb/prishniparni.from: - Anti-inflammatory activity validated through in vivo studies, confirming its traditional role in treating Shotha (edema/inflammation)
herb/prishniparni.to: - Traditionally used for Shotha (edema/inflammation). Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/prishniparni.from: - Cardioprotective properties supported by preclinical studies showing improvement in cardiac biomarkers
herb/prishniparni.to: - Preclinical studies have reported improvement in cardiac biomarkers.

herb/prishniparni.from: - Wound healing activity confirmed through experimental models, validating its use in traditional wound management
herb/prishniparni.to: - Traditionally used on wounds. Experimental studies have reported wound healing activity.

herb/pradarantak-lauh.from: - Menorrhagia and metrorrhagia (Pradara/excessive menstrual bleeding) - traditional use supported by clinical observations showing reduced menstrual blood loss and improved hemoglobin
herb/pradarantak-lauh.to: - Menorrhagia and metrorrhagia (Pradara/excessive menstrual bleeding): traditionally used for excessive menstrual bleeding. Clinical observations have reported reduced menstrual blood loss and improved hemoglobin.

herb/pradarantak-lauh.from: - Leucorrhea (Shweta Pradara) - traditional gynecological application validated through clinical practice with reported improvement in vaginal discharge and associated symptoms
herb/pradarantak-lauh.to: - Leucorrhea (Shweta Pradara): used in classical practice as a gynecological application for leucorrhea. Reports from clinical practice have described improvement in vaginal discharge and associated symptoms.

herb/priyangu.from: - Anti-inflammatory activity confirmed in carrageenan-induced paw edema models.
herb/priyangu.to: - Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity in carrageenan-induced paw edema models.

herb/priyangu.from: - [Analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) activity validated and found comparable to standard analgesics.
herb/priyangu.to: - Experimental studies have reported [Analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) activity comparable to standard analgesics.

herb/priyangu.from: - Antipyretic effects demonstrated in experimental fever models.
herb/priyangu.to: - Experimental studies have reported antipyretic effects in fever models.

herb/priyangu.from: - Antimicrobial activity confirmed against multiple pathogens.
herb/priyangu.to: - Laboratory studies have reported antimicrobial activity against multiple pathogens.

herb/priyangu.from: - Anti-arthritic potential validated in Freund's adjuvant arthritis model.
herb/priyangu.to: - Animal studies have reported anti-arthritic activity in a Freund's adjuvant arthritis model.

herb/pushkarmool.from: - Cardioprotective use (Hridya) validated through HMG-CoA reductase inhibition and myocardial ischemia protection in animal models
herb/pushkarmool.to: - Hridya (cardioprotective): traditionally used for the heart. Animal studies have reported HMG-CoA reductase inhibition and protection against myocardial ischemia.

herb/pushkarmool.from: - Anti-asthmatic and bronchodilatory use (Shwasahara) confirmed by bronchial smooth muscle relaxation and anti-histaminic activity
herb/pushkarmool.to: - Shwasahara (anti-asthmatic and bronchodilatory): traditionally used for asthma and breathing difficulty. Studies have reported bronchial smooth muscle relaxation and anti-histaminic activity.

herb/pushkarmool.from: - Angina treatment use supported by coronary vasodilatory effect and reduction of myocardial oxygen demand in preclinical studies
herb/pushkarmool.to: - Angina: traditionally used for angina. Preclinical studies have reported a coronary vasodilatory effect and lower myocardial oxygen demand.

herb/pravala-pishti.from: - Calcium deficiency and bone disorders: Preclinical study (2003) demonstrated prevention of calcium and estrogen deficit bone loss; multicenter clinical study (2020) supported safety and efficacy in menopausal calcium management
herb/pravala-pishti.to: - Calcium deficiency and bone disorders: traditionally used for calcium deficiency and bone disorders. A preclinical study reported less bone loss linked to calcium and estrogen deficit. A multicenter clinical study in menopausal women reported on its safety.

herb/pravala-pishti.from: - Hyperacidity (Amlapitta) and bleeding disorders (Raktapitta): The calcium carbonate content provides direct mechanistic validation for antacid use; calcium's role in coagulation cascade supports the traditional hemostatic indication
herb/pravala-pishti.to: - Hyperacidity (Amlapitta) and bleeding disorders (Raktapitta): traditionally used as an antacid and for bleeding disorders. It contains calcium carbonate.

herb/prasarini.from: - Anti-rheumatic use (Vatahara) validated through anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) activity in carrageenan and formalin models
herb/prasarini.to: - Traditionally used as an anti-rheumatic (Vatahara). Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) activity in carrageenan and formalin models.

herb/prasarini.from: - Antidiarrheal use confirmed by reduction of gastrointestinal motility and fluid accumulation in castor oil-induced diarrhea model
herb/prasarini.to: - Traditionally used for diarrhea. Animal studies have reported reduced gastrointestinal motility and fluid accumulation in a castor oil-induced diarrhea model.

herb/prasarini.from: - Gastroprotective use validated by PGE2-mediated increase in gastric mucus secretion and ulcer protection
herb/prasarini.to: - Traditionally used to protect the stomach. Research has reported a PGE2-mediated increase in gastric mucus secretion and a protective effect against ulcers.

herb/pattanga.from: - Complexion enhancement (Varnya): Validated by demonstrated brazilin-mediated melanin synthesis suppression in human melanoma cells
herb/pattanga.to: - Complexion enhancement (Varnya): traditionally used for complexion enhancement. An in vitro study in human melanoma cells reported that brazilin suppressed melanin synthesis.

herb/pattanga.from: - Wound healing (Vrana Ropana): Validated by 2024 animal study showing significant improvement in incision wound healing with 6.5% sappanwood extract
herb/pattanga.to: - Wound healing (Vrana Ropana): traditionally used for wound healing. An animal study reported improved incision wound healing with sappanwood extract.

herb/pattanga.from: - Anti-inflammatory skin care (Daha Prashamana): Validated by demonstrated inhibition of NO and PGE2 production through iNOS and COX-2 suppression
herb/pattanga.to: - Anti-inflammatory skin care (Daha Prashamana): traditionally used in skin care for inflammatory conditions. Studies have reported inhibition of NO and PGE2 production through iNOS and COX-2 suppression.

herb/pippali-moola.from: - Bioavailability enhancement (Yogavahi) validated - piperine's ability to increase absorption of co-administered compounds is well-established pharmacologically, confirming the traditional Ayurvedic concept of Yogavahi (bioenhancer)
herb/pippali-moola.to: - Yogavahi (bioenhancer): traditionally used to enhance the action of co-administered substances. Pharmacological studies have reported that piperine can increase the absorption of co-administered compounds.

herb/pippali-moola.from: - Respiratory disease treatment (Shwasa, Kasa) supported by documented anti-inflammatory, bronchodilatory, and [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) effects, though high-quality RCTs are still needed
herb/pippali-moola.to: - Shwasa, Kasa (respiratory disease): traditionally used for respiratory conditions. Studies have reported anti-inflammatory, bronchodilatory, and [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/) effects. High-quality randomized controlled trials are still lacking.

herb/pippali-moola.from: - Deepana-Pachana (digestive stimulant) activity validated through studies showing enhanced gastric secretion and gastrointestinal motility
herb/pippali-moola.to: - Deepana-Pachana (digestive stimulant): traditionally used to stimulate digestion. Studies have reported increased gastric secretion and gastrointestinal motility.

herb/plaksha.from: - Wound healing and anti-ulcer properties validated through clinical and preclinical studies on non-healing ulcers
herb/plaksha.to: - Traditionally used for wounds and ulcers. Clinical and preclinical studies on non-healing ulcers have reported wound-healing and anti-ulcer activity.

herb/plaksha.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects confirmed in carrageenan-induced paw edema models
herb/plaksha.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation and pain. Preclinical studies in carrageenan-induced paw edema models have reported anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) effects.

herb/plaksha.from: - [Hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic) (bleeding disorder) use validated via in vitro clotting studies and astringent tannin activity
herb/plaksha.to: - Traditionally used for its [Hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic) (bleeding disorder) action. In vitro clotting studies have reported clotting activity, along with astringent tannin activity.

herb/plaksha.from: - Anti-diarrheal action confirmed through reduction of gastrointestinal motility in preclinical models
herb/plaksha.to: - Traditionally used for diarrhea. Preclinical studies have reported reduced gastrointestinal motility.

herb/pudina.from: - Digestive aid for bloating, indigestion, and IBS - validated by double-blind clinical trial showing reduced bloating and discomfort with spearmint extract
herb/pudina.to: - Traditionally used as a digestive aid for bloating, indigestion, and IBS. A double-blind clinical study of spearmint extract reported reduced bloating and discomfort.

herb/pudina.from: - Cooling and fever-reducing properties - supported by pharmacological studies confirming [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity
herb/pudina.to: - Traditionally used for its cooling and fever-reducing properties. Pharmacological studies have reported [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity.

herb/pudina.from: - Respiratory relief for cough, cold, and asthma - confirmed through bronchodilatory and [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) studies
herb/pudina.to: - Traditionally used for cough, cold, and asthma. Studies have reported bronchodilatory and [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) activity.

herb/pudina.from: - Antimicrobial use for oral and skin infections - validated by studies showing activity against drug-resistant bacteria including MRSA
herb/pudina.to: - Traditionally used for oral and skin infections. Studies have reported activity against drug-resistant bacteria, including MRSA.

herb/pudina.from: - Anxiolytic and calming effects - supported by preclinical studies demonstrating significant anxiolytic and sedative activity through GABAergic modulation
herb/pudina.to: - Traditionally used for its calming effects. Preclinical studies have reported anxiolytic and sedative activity through GABAergic modulation.

herb/pudina.from: Identified 35 chemical constituents in spearmint; validated pharmacological properties support traditional uses including digestive, cooling, and toxin-clearing applications in Ayurveda.
herb/pudina.to: A chemical analysis identified a range of constituents in spearmint. In Ayurveda, it is traditionally used for digestive, cooling, and toxin-clearing purposes.

herb/riddhi.from: - Antioxidant and free radical scavenging activity experimentally validated, confirming its traditional Rasayana (rejuvenation) role
herb/riddhi.to: - Traditionally used as a Rasayana (rejuvenation) herb. Experimental studies have reported antioxidant and free radical scavenging activity.

herb/riddhi.from: - [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac) and general tonic properties partially supported by nutritional profiling showing high calcium and mineral content
herb/riddhi.to: - Traditionally used as an [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac) and general tonic. Nutritional profiling has reported high calcium and mineral content.

herb/riddhi.from: - Immune-boosting activity supported by preliminary immunological studies, confirming traditional use as a vitality-enhancing herb
herb/riddhi.to: - Traditionally used as a vitality-enhancing herb. Preliminary immunological studies have reported immune-boosting activity.

herb/rasona-patra.from: - Antimicrobial properties validated through demonstrated activity of organosulfur compounds against bacteria, fungi, and parasites, supporting traditional use of garlic leaf preparations for infections
herb/rasona-patra.to: - Garlic leaf preparations are traditionally used for infections. Studies have reported activity of organosulfur compounds against bacteria, fungi, and parasites.

herb/rasona-patra.from: - Antioxidant activity confirmed through phenolic and flavonoid content analysis, supporting traditional use of fresh garlic greens as a health-promoting food in Ayurvedic dietary recommendations
herb/rasona-patra.to: - Fresh garlic greens are traditionally valued as a health-promoting food in Ayurvedic dietary recommendations. Analyses of their phenolic and flavonoid content have reported antioxidant activity.

herb/raupya-bhasma.from: - Insomnia and anxiety: Reverse pharmacological study confirmed significant sedative-hypnotic effect in mice, validating traditional use for Anidra (insomnia) and Chittodvega (anxiety)
herb/raupya-bhasma.to: - Insomnia and anxiety: traditionally used for Anidra (insomnia) and Chittodvega (anxiety). An animal study in mice reported a sedative-hypnotic effect.

herb/raupya-bhasma.from: - Pain management: Demonstrated analgesic activity comparable to aspirin in animal models, supporting traditional use for Shula (pain) and neuralgias
herb/raupya-bhasma.to: - Pain: traditionally used for Shula (pain) and neuralgias. Animal studies have reported analgesic activity comparable to aspirin.

herb/raupya-bhasma.from: - Neurological disorders: Evidence for safety on neurobehavioral parameters in rats, partially validating traditional use for memory loss, convulsions, and nervous system disorders
herb/raupya-bhasma.to: - Neurological disorders: traditionally used for memory loss, convulsions, and nervous system disorders. Animal studies in rats have reported safety on neurobehavioral parameters.

herb/rasamanikya.from: - Skin diseases (Kushtha): Traditional use in psoriasis and chronic dermatoses has indirect validation from historical Western medical use of arsenic for psoriasis (Fowler's solution, 19th century) and modern understanding of arsenic's anti-proliferative effects on keratinocytes - however, the practice was abandoned in Western medicine due to carcinogenic risk
herb/rasamanikya.to: - Skin diseases (Kushtha): traditionally used for psoriasis and chronic dermatoses. Arsenic was historically used in Western medicine for psoriasis (Fowler's solution). Arsenic has been reported to have anti-proliferative effects on keratinocytes. Western medicine abandoned this practice because of carcinogenic risk.

herb/rasamanikya.from: - Fever and respiratory conditions: Traditional use in Jwara (fever) and Shwasa (asthma) partially supported by arsenic's documented immunomodulatory properties, but no specific clinical trials validate these indications for Rasamanikya
herb/rasamanikya.to: - Fever and respiratory conditions: traditionally used for Jwara (fever) and Shwasa (asthma). Arsenic has been reported to have immunomodulatory properties. No clinical trials specific to Rasamanikya have been reported for these uses.

herb/rakta-chandana.from: - Wound healing (Vranaropana): Validated in animal models showing significantly accelerated healing of punch and burn wounds with enhanced collagen synthesis
herb/rakta-chandana.to: - Wound repair (Vranaropana): traditionally used for wounds. Animal studies have reported faster closure of punch and burn wounds, with increased collagen synthesis.

herb/rakta-chandana.from: - Anti-inflammatory skin care (Daha-shamana): Validated by in vitro studies showing selective inhibition of pro-inflammatory genes in IL-1 stimulated cells
herb/rakta-chandana.to: - Anti-inflammatory skin care (Daha-shamana): traditionally used in skin care. In vitro studies have reported selective inhibition of pro-inflammatory genes in IL-1 stimulated cells.

herb/rakta-chandana.from: - Complexion enhancement (Varnya): Traditional face pack use partially supported by antioxidant activity of [pterostilbene](/glossary/compounds-o-q/#pterostilbene), though large-scale clinical trials are lacking
herb/rakta-chandana.to: - Complexion enhancement (Varnya): traditionally used as a face pack. Antioxidant activity has been reported for [pterostilbene](/glossary/compounds-o-q/#pterostilbene). Large-scale clinical trials are lacking.

herb/rishabhaka.from: - [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac) and tonic properties supported by preclinical studies demonstrating [adaptogenic](/reference/adaptogenic/) effects, confirming traditional [Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana) use
herb/rishabhaka.to: - [Aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac) and tonic: traditionally used in [Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana). Preclinical studies have reported [adaptogenic](/reference/adaptogenic/) effects.

herb/rishabhaka.from: - Antibacterial activity validated against multiple pathogenic strains, supporting traditional use in infectious and dental conditions
herb/rishabhaka.to: - Traditionally used in infectious and dental conditions. Studies have reported antibacterial activity against several pathogenic strains.

herb/rishabhaka.from: - Antiulcer activity confirmed through gastroprotective studies in animal models, validating traditional use in digestive disorders
herb/rishabhaka.to: - Traditionally used for digestive disorders. Animal studies have reported antiulcer and gastroprotective activity.

herb/rasona-garlic.from: - Cardiovascular protection (Hridya) validated through extensive clinical evidence showing reduction of blood pressure, serum cholesterol, and platelet aggregation, confirming traditional [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) use
herb/rasona-garlic.to: - Hridya (for the heart): traditionally used for the heart and as a [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/). Clinical studies have reported reductions in blood pressure, serum cholesterol, and platelet aggregation.

herb/rasona-garlic.from: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity validated against broad spectrum of bacteria, fungi, viruses, and parasites, supporting traditional use for Krimighna (antimicrobial) applications in Ayurveda
herb/rasona-garlic.to: - Krimighna (antimicrobial): traditionally used in Ayurveda for antimicrobial applications. [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity has been reported against a broad range of bacteria, fungi, viruses, and parasites.

herb/rasona-garlic.from: - Immunostimulant properties confirmed through clinical and preclinical studies, supporting traditional use as Rasayana (rejuvenating/immune-boosting) herb
herb/rasona-garlic.to: - Rasayana (rejuvenating/immune-boosting): traditionally used as a rejuvenating herb. Clinical and preclinical studies have reported immunostimulant properties.

herb/rasna.from: - Anti-rheumatic and anti-arthritic use (Amavata treatment) validated by reduction of inflammation markers and joint edema in animal models
herb/rasna.to: - Amavata: traditionally used for rheumatic and arthritic conditions. Animal studies have reported reduced inflammation markers and joint edema.

herb/rasna.from: - [Analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) use (Vedana-sthapana) confirmed through significant pain reduction in hot plate and tail flick assays
herb/rasna.to: - Vedana-sthapana: traditionally used as an [Analgesic](/reference/analgesic/). Studies using hot plate and tail flick assays have reported reduced pain responses.

herb/rasna.from: - Immunomodulatory ([Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)) activity validated by enhancement of phagocytic function and antibody response
herb/rasna.to: - Used in classical practice as a [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/). Studies have reported immunomodulatory activity, including enhanced phagocytic function and antibody response.

herb/rasna.from: Documented triterpenoids, [sterols](/glossary/compounds-q-t/#sterols), flavonoids and lactones as prominent constituents; validated anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and immunomodulatory activities.
herb/rasna.to: Documented prominent constituents include triterpenoids, [sterols](/glossary/compounds-q-t/#sterols), flavonoids and lactones. Studies have reported anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and immunomodulatory activities.

herb/renuka.from: - Menstrual regulation and PMS relief - strongly validated through multiple clinical trials showing significant PMS symptom reduction
herb/renuka.to: - Menstrual regulation and PMS: traditionally used for menstrual regulation and premenstrual complaints. Clinical studies have reported reduced PMS symptoms.

herb/renuka.from: - Prolactin lowering (Stanya-shodhana) - confirmed through clinical studies demonstrating prolactin reduction via dopamine D2 receptor mechanism
herb/renuka.to: - Stanya-shodhana: used in classical practice under this category. Clinical studies have reported reduced prolactin levels and proposed a dopamine D2 receptor mechanism.

herb/renuka.from: - Menopausal symptom management - validated in clinical studies showing reduction of vasomotor symptoms, mood disorders, and sleep disturbances
herb/renuka.to: - Menopausal symptoms: traditionally used for menopausal complaints. Clinical studies have reported reductions in vasomotor symptoms, mood disorders and sleep disturbances.

herb/renuka.from: - Female reproductive health (Stri-roga) - broadly validated through clinical evidence supporting menstrual cycle normalization and fertility support
herb/renuka.to: - Female reproductive health (Stri-roga): traditionally used for female reproductive conditions. Clinical studies have reported menstrual cycle normalization.

herb/renuka.from: **Standardized Extract:** Renuka seed extract (10:1) standardized to casticin >0.5% and agnuside >0.2% (if V. agnus-castus). Total diterpenes >1%. BNO 1095 or Ze 440 are clinically validated extract specifications (European Vitex standards).
herb/renuka.to: **Standardized Extract:** Renuka seed extract (10:1) standardized to casticin >0.5% and agnuside >0.2% (if V. agnus-castus). Total diterpenes >1%. BNO 1095 and Ze 440 are the extract specifications used in European clinical studies of Vitex.

herb/senna.from: - Laxative efficacy extensively validated through clinical studies and pharmacological research, confirming premier traditional use as a bowel stimulant (Virechana dravya)
herb/senna.to: - Traditionally used as a bowel stimulant (Virechana dravya). Clinical studies and pharmacological research have reported laxative activity.

herb/senna.from: - Antimicrobial properties validated against multiple bacterial and fungal strains, supporting broader traditional applications beyond purgation
herb/senna.to: - Traditionally used beyond purgation. In vitro studies have reported antimicrobial activity against several bacterial and fungal strains.

herb/senna.from: - Anti-inflammatory properties partially validated through preclinical studies, though this is not the primary traditional indication
herb/senna.to: - Preclinical studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity, though this is not the primary traditional use.

herb/sameer-pannag-rasa.from: - Bronchial asthma (Tamaka Shwasa): Validated by a randomized double-blind clinical study (2014) showing significant improvement in peak expiratory flow rate, reduced eosinophil count, and clinical symptom improvement in 52 patients
herb/sameer-pannag-rasa.to: - Bronchial asthma (Tamaka Shwasa): traditionally used for this condition. A randomized double-blind clinical study reported improvement in peak expiratory flow rate, a reduced eosinophil count, and improved clinical symptoms.

herb/sameer-pannag-rasa.from: - Respiratory disorders: Chronic cough and mild asthma uses supported by clinical practice experience and the documented anti-inflammatory and bronchodilatory effects
herb/sameer-pannag-rasa.to: - Respiratory disorders: traditionally used for chronic cough and mild asthma.

herb/saptamrit-lauh.from: - Hemorrhagic retinopathies (diabetic and hypertensive) - validated by clinical study showing rapid hemorrhage absorption and reduced recurrence
herb/saptamrit-lauh.to: - Hemorrhagic retinopathies (diabetic and hypertensive): traditionally used for these conditions. A clinical study reported rapid absorption of hemorrhage and less recurrence.

herb/saptamrit-lauh.from: - Myopia and visual disorders (Timira) - validated by comparative clinical study showing improvement in visual acuity with [Saptamrit Lauh](/herb/saptamrit-lauh/) therapy
herb/saptamrit-lauh.to: - Myopia and visual disorders (Timira): traditionally used for these conditions. A comparative clinical study reported improved visual acuity with [Saptamrit Lauh](/herb/saptamrit-lauh/) therapy.

herb/sala.from: - Wound healing use validated through excision wound models with significantly accelerated closure and improved histological markers
herb/sala.to: - Traditionally used for wounds. Animal studies using excision wound models have reported faster wound closure and improved histological markers.

herb/sala.from: - Anti-inflammatory activity confirmed in carrageenan-induced paw edema and cotton pellet granuloma models
herb/sala.to: - Animal studies using carrageenan-induced paw edema and cotton pellet granuloma models have reported anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/sala.from: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity confirmed in Brewer's yeast-induced fever model in rodents
herb/sala.to: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity has been reported in animal studies using a Brewer's yeast-induced fever model in rodents.

herb/sala.from: - Antibacterial properties validated against common wound pathogens including S. aureus and E. coli
herb/sala.to: - Laboratory studies have reported antibacterial activity against common wound pathogens, including S. aureus and E. coli.

herb/shalparni.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) properties validated through multiple preclinical models, confirming its traditional use in pain and swelling
herb/shalparni.to: - Traditionally used for pain and swelling. Preclinical studies have reported anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) activity.

herb/shalparni.from: - [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) activity supported by in vivo studies showing blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) reduction, validating its use in Prameha (diabetes management)
herb/shalparni.to: - Traditionally used in Prameha (diabetes). [Antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) activity, including lower blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose), has been reported in in vivo studies.

herb/shalparni.from: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) properties confirmed against multiple bacterial and fungal strains, supporting its traditional use in infectious conditions
herb/shalparni.to: - Traditionally used for infectious conditions. [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity against several bacterial and fungal strains has been reported in laboratory studies.

herb/saptala.from: - Purgative (Virechana) - validated through confirmed stimulant [laxative](/reference/laxative/) action of diterpene esters on intestinal smooth muscle
herb/saptala.to: - Purgative (Virechana): traditionally used as a purgative. Studies have reported stimulant [laxative](/reference/laxative/) action of diterpene esters on intestinal smooth muscle.

herb/saptala.from: - Skin diseases (Kushtha) - traditional use against psoriasis, ringworm, and warts partially supported by [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and anti-inflammatory data
herb/saptala.to: - Skin diseases (Kushtha): traditionally used for psoriasis, ringworm, and warts. Studies have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/saptala.from: - Anti-rheumatic (Amavata) - supported by anti-inflammatory and analgesic studies in animal models
herb/saptala.to: - Anti-rheumatic (Amavata): traditionally used for Amavata. Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory and analgesic activity.

herb/saptala.from: - [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) (Mutrala) - traditional diuretic use cited in Ayurvedic texts; limited pharmacological validation
herb/saptala.to: - [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) (Mutrala): traditionally used as a diuretic, as described in Ayurvedic texts.

herb/sarpagandha.from: - Antihypertensive use (Raktachapa-hara) extensively validated; reserpine was one of the first effective antihypertensive drugs used in Western medicine
herb/sarpagandha.to: - Raktachapa-hara (antihypertensive): traditionally used to lower blood pressure. Reserpine was one of the first antihypertensive drugs used in Western medicine.

herb/sarpagandha.from: - Sedative and [anxiolytic](/reference/anxiolytic/) use (Nidrajanana) confirmed through VMAT2 inhibition and central monoamine depletion mechanism
herb/sarpagandha.to: - Nidrajanana (sedative): traditionally used as a sedative and [anxiolytic](/reference/anxiolytic/). A mechanism involving VMAT2 inhibition and central monoamine depletion has been described.

herb/sarpagandha.from: - Anti-arrhythmic use validated: ajmaline is still used clinically in the Ajmaline test for diagnosis of Brugada syndrome
herb/sarpagandha.to: - Anti-arrhythmic use: traditionally used for irregular heart rhythm. Ajmaline is still used clinically in the Ajmaline test, a diagnostic test for Brugada syndrome.

herb/saindhava-lavana.from: - Agni Deepana (digestive stimulant): Validated by evidence showing rock salt stimulates salivary and gastric enzyme production and bile secretion without inflammatory side effects
herb/saindhava-lavana.to: - Agni Deepana (digestive stimulant): traditionally used as a digestive stimulant. Rock salt has been reported to stimulate salivary and gastric enzyme production and bile secretion.

herb/saindhava-lavana.from: - Netra Hita (beneficial for eyes): Traditional eye wash preparations with Saindhava have [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) basis; trace minerals support ocular surface health
herb/saindhava-lavana.to: - Netra Hita (beneficial for eyes): used in classical practice in eye wash preparations with Saindhava. These preparations have been described as having an [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) basis.

herb/saindhava-lavana.from: - Hridya (cardiotonic): Balanced mineral profile and lower sodium-per-weight ratio compared to refined salt provide modest cardiovascular advantage, partially validating the classical claim
herb/saindhava-lavana.to: - Hridya (cardiotonic): traditionally described as a cardiotonic. Rock salt is described as having a balanced mineral profile and a lower sodium-per-weight ratio than refined salt.

herb/samudra-lavana.from: - Virechana support (purgation therapy): Osmotic laxative mechanism of magnesium salts validates traditional use as a mild purgative in Ayurvedic Panchakarma support
herb/samudra-lavana.to: - Virechana support (purgation therapy): traditionally used as a mild purgative in Ayurvedic Panchakarma support.

herb/samudra-lavana.from: - Shula (colic pain): Magnesium-mediated smooth muscle relaxation provides scientific basis for traditional anti-colic application
herb/samudra-lavana.to: - Shula (colic pain): traditionally used for colic pain.

herb/samudra-lavana.from: - Deepana (digestive stimulant): Salt-mediated gastric acid stimulation and enzyme activation confirmed by modern physiology
herb/samudra-lavana.to: - Deepana (digestive stimulant): traditionally used as a digestive stimulant.

herb/shallaki.from: - Anti-arthritic use (Sandhivata) extensively validated through multiple RCTs showing significant improvement in knee OA symptoms comparable to NSAIDs
herb/shallaki.to: - Traditionally used for Sandhivata (arthritic conditions). Randomized clinical trials have reported improvement in knee osteoarthritis symptoms comparable to NSAIDs.

herb/shallaki.from: - Anti-inflammatory use confirmed through 5-LOX inhibition, NF-kB suppression, and clinical improvement in inflammatory bowel disease trials
herb/shallaki.to: - Traditionally used for inflammatory conditions. Studies have reported 5-LOX inhibition and NF-kB suppression. Clinical trials in inflammatory bowel disease have reported improvement.

herb/shallaki.from: - Anti-asthmatic use (Shwasahara) supported by clinical trials showing improvement in FEV1 and reduction in eosinophil count in bronchial asthma patients
herb/shallaki.to: - Traditionally used as Shwasahara for asthma. Clinical trials in bronchial asthma patients have reported improvement in FEV1 and a reduction in eosinophil count.

herb/shallaki.from: - [Curcumin](/herb/curcumin/)/[Haridra](/herb/haridra/) (potent anti-inflammatory synergy, clinically validated for osteoarthritis)
herb/shallaki.to: - [Curcumin](/herb/curcumin/)/[Haridra](/herb/haridra/) (combination described as having anti-inflammatory synergy; clinical studies have reported improvement in osteoarthritis)

herb/shyonaka.from: - Anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic properties confirmed through in vivo studies on both root bark and stem bark, validating classical use in Vataroga
herb/shyonaka.to: - Traditionally used in Vataroga. Animal studies on the root bark and stem bark have reported anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic activity.

herb/shyonaka.from: - [Hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) activity validated through experimental models demonstrating restoration of liver [enzymes](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#enzymes), supporting its traditional use in liver disorders
herb/shyonaka.to: - Traditionally used for liver disorders. Animal studies have reported [hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) activity, with liver [enzymes](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#enzymes) returning toward normal levels.

herb/shyonaka.from: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) spectrum confirmed against multiple pathogens, validating traditional topical applications for wound infections and skin diseases
herb/shyonaka.to: - Traditionally applied topically for wound infections and skin diseases. Laboratory studies have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity against multiple pathogens.

herb/siddha-makardhwaj.from: - Rejuvenation and vitality: Animal safety studies indirectly support the Rasayana claim by demonstrating that the preparation enhances metabolic parameters without causing organ toxicity at therapeutic doses
herb/siddha-makardhwaj.to: - Rejuvenation and vitality: traditionally used as a Rasayana for rejuvenation and vitality. Animal safety studies have reported improved metabolic parameters without organ toxicity.

herb/siddha-makardhwaj.from: - Rheumatoid arthritis and neurological disorders: Traditional use documented in classical texts; the anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory mechanisms identified in related formulation studies provide preliminary mechanistic support
herb/siddha-makardhwaj.to: - Rheumatoid arthritis and neurological disorders: traditionally used for these conditions, as documented in classical texts. Studies on related formulations have reported anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activity.

herb/shatavari-ksheera.from: - Galactagogue use (Stanya-janana) validated through RCTs showing increased breast milk volume and prolactin levels in lactating women
herb/shatavari-ksheera.to: - Stanya-janana (galactagogue): traditionally used to support breast milk production. Randomized controlled trials have reported increased breast milk volume and prolactin levels in lactating women.

herb/shatavari-ksheera.from: - Menopausal symptom relief confirmed by 2025 RCT demonstrating significant reduction in hot flushes and sleep disturbance
herb/shatavari-ksheera.to: - Traditionally used for menopausal symptoms. A randomized controlled trial reported a reduction in hot flushes and sleep disturbance.

herb/shatavari-ksheera.from: - Adaptogenic-[Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) use supported by HPA axis modulation and improvement of stress biomarkers in clinical and preclinical studies
herb/shatavari-ksheera.to: - Traditionally used as an adaptogen and [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/). Clinical and preclinical studies have reported HPA axis modulation and improvement in stress biomarkers.

herb/shukti-bhasma.from: - Hyperacidity and peptic ulcer (Amlapitta): 68% symptom reduction in heartburn validated in clinical trial, confirming traditional antacid use
herb/shukti-bhasma.to: - Hyperacidity and peptic ulcer (Amlapitta): traditionally used as an antacid for these conditions. A clinical study reported a reduction in heartburn symptoms.

herb/shukti-bhasma.from: - Osteoporosis and bone disorders (Asthi Kshaya): 2.5% lumbar spine BMD improvement in 25 osteopenic subjects over 6 months validates calcium supplementation claim
herb/shukti-bhasma.to: - Osteoporosis and bone disorders (Asthi Kshaya): traditionally used as a source of calcium. A clinical study in osteopenic subjects reported an improvement in lumbar spine bone mineral density.

herb/shukti-bhasma.from: - Respiratory and musculoskeletal diseases: Cross-system review (Ayurveda, Siddha) confirms traditional use for diverse conditions including respiratory and joint disorders
herb/shukti-bhasma.to: - Respiratory and musculoskeletal diseases: traditionally used in Ayurveda and Siddha for diverse conditions, including respiratory and joint disorders.

herb/shankha-bhasma.from: - Hyperacidity and GERD (Amlapitta): Clinical study confirmed significant GERD symptom resolution (p < 0.005) with lemon-purified [Shankha Bhasma](/herb/shankha-bhasma/)
herb/shankha-bhasma.to: - Hyperacidity and GERD (Amlapitta): traditionally used for these conditions. A clinical study reported a reduction in GERD symptoms with lemon-purified [Shankha Bhasma](/herb/shankha-bhasma/).

herb/shankha-bhasma.from: - Digestive disorders (Agnimandya, Ajirna): High acid neutralization capacity validated traditional use as digestive aid and antacid
herb/shankha-bhasma.to: - Digestive disorders (Agnimandya, Ajirna): traditionally used as a digestive aid and antacid. A high acid neutralization capacity has been reported.

herb/shankha-bhasma.from: - Calcium deficiency: Marine-derived bioavailable calcium content supports traditional use for bone health and Asthi Dhatu nourishment
herb/shankha-bhasma.to: - Calcium deficiency: traditionally used for bone health and Asthi Dhatu nourishment. It is described as containing marine-derived calcium.

herb/shankhpushpi.from: Comprehensive umbrella review validated ethnomedicinal uses ([antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic), [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/), anti-inflammatory, anti-anxiety, memory-boosting) through neuropharmacological studies. Highlighted need for multicentric clinical trials across diverse populations.
herb/shankhpushpi.to: Traditionally used as an [antispasmodic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antispasmodic) and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/), and for inflammation, anxiety and memory. An umbrella review of neuropharmacological studies reported antispasmodic, analgesic, anti-inflammatory, anti-anxiety and memory-boosting effects. The review noted a need for multicentric clinical trials across diverse populations.

herb/shati.from: - Cough and respiratory disorders (Kasa-hara, Shvasa-hara) - validated through confirmed antihistaminic, bronchodilatory, and [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) properties
herb/shati.to: - Cough and respiratory disorders (Kasa-hara, Shvasa-hara): traditionally used for cough and breathing complaints. Studies have reported antihistaminic, bronchodilatory, and [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) properties.

herb/shati.from: - Fever reduction (Jvarahara) - confirmed [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity through anti-inflammatory mechanisms
herb/shati.to: - Fever (Jvarahara): traditionally used to reduce fever. Studies have reported [antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity, attributed to anti-inflammatory mechanisms.

herb/shati.from: - Anti-emetic and nausea relief (Chhardi-nigrahana) - traditional digestive use supported by carminative and [antiemetic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antiemetic) studies
herb/shati.to: - Nausea and vomiting (Chhardi-nigrahana): traditionally used as a digestive remedy for nausea. Studies have reported carminative and [antiemetic](/glossary/pharmacology/#antiemetic) activity.

herb/shati.from: - Anti-inflammatory (Shotha-hara) - validated through in vivo carrageenan-induced paw edema models
herb/shati.to: - Inflammation (Shotha-hara): traditionally used for swelling. Animal studies using carrageenan-induced paw edema models have reported anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/shrigataka.from: - Ellagic acid and gallic acid [polyphenols](/glossary/compounds-o-q/#polyphenols) inhibit alpha-glucosidase and alpha-amylase [enzymes](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#enzymes), reducing postprandial [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) absorption and providing [antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) effects validated in myotube glucose uptake assays
herb/shrigataka.to: - In vitro studies have reported that ellagic acid and gallic acid [polyphenols](/glossary/compounds-o-q/#polyphenols) inhibit alpha-glucosidase and alpha-amylase [enzymes](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#enzymes). Myotube assays have reported increased [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) uptake, described as [antidiabetic](/reference/antidiabetic/) activity.

herb/shrigataka.from: - Anti-inflammatory and cooling effects validated through macrophage polarization studies and [antioxidant](/reference/antioxidant/) assays, supporting traditional Ayurvedic use as a Pittahara (Pitta-pacifying) food medicine
herb/shrigataka.to: - Traditionally used in Ayurveda as a cooling, Pittahara (Pitta-pacifying) food medicine. Laboratory studies on macrophage polarization have reported anti-inflammatory activity, and [antioxidant](/reference/antioxidant/) assays have reported antioxidant activity.

herb/shrigataka.from: - Antidiabetic activity validated through isolation of specific hypoglycemic constituents from pericarps that enhance cellular glucose uptake, supporting traditional use for Prameha (diabetes)
herb/shrigataka.to: - Traditionally used for Prameha (diabetes). Laboratory studies have reported that hypoglycemic constituents isolated from the pericarps increase cellular glucose uptake.

herb/shrigataka.from: - Nutritive and strength-promoting properties (Brimhana) supported by nutritional analysis showing high [starch](/glossary/compounds-q-t/#starch), protein, mineral, and vitamin content
herb/shrigataka.to: - Traditionally valued as nutritive and strength-promoting (Brimhana). Nutritional analysis has reported high [starch](/glossary/compounds-q-t/#starch), protein, mineral, and vitamin content.

herb/shothari-loha.from: - Shotha (edema/swelling) - traditional use supported by known anti-edema and [diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) properties of [Yavakshara](/herb/yavakshara/) and anti-inflammatory effects of [Trikatu](/herb/trikatu/)
herb/shothari-loha.to: - Shotha (edema/swelling): traditionally used for edema and swelling. In classical practice, [Yavakshara](/herb/yavakshara/) is regarded as anti-edema and [diuretic](/reference/diuretic/), and [Trikatu](/herb/trikatu/) as anti-inflammatory.

herb/shothari-loha.from: - Anemia with associated inflammatory conditions - validated through clinical practice showing improvement in hemoglobin levels alongside reduction in inflammatory symptoms
herb/shothari-loha.to: - Anemia with associated inflammatory conditions: used in classical practice for anemia with associated inflammatory conditions. Reports from clinical practice have described improved hemoglobin levels alongside fewer inflammatory symptoms.

herb/shirisha.from: - Anti-allergic and anti-asthmatic use validated through mast cell stabilization, antihistaminic activity and clinical studies showing improved PEFR and reduced eosinophil count
herb/shirisha.to: - Traditionally used for allergic and asthmatic conditions. Studies have reported mast cell stabilizing and antihistaminic activity. Clinical studies have reported improved PEFR and reduced eosinophil count.

herb/shirisha.from: - Anti-inflammatory use confirmed in carrageenan-induced paw edema and adjuvant arthritis models
herb/shirisha.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation. Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity in carrageenan-induced paw edema and adjuvant arthritis models.

herb/shirisha.from: - Vishaghna (anti-toxic) use supported by [hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) and detoxification studies
herb/shirisha.to: - Vishaghna (anti-toxic): traditionally used against toxins. Studies have reported [hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) and detoxification activity.

herb/shirisha.from: - Anti-diarrheal activity confirmed through castor oil-induced diarrhea models with significant reduction in frequency
herb/shirisha.to: - Traditionally used for diarrhea. Animal studies using castor oil-induced diarrhea models have reported reduced stool frequency.

herb/tamalaki.from: - Antilithiatic (kidney stone breaking) activity validated through clinical trials showing reduced stone recurrence, confirming premier traditional use as [Pashanabheda](/herb/pashanabheda/) (stone breaker)
herb/tamalaki.to: - Traditionally used as a [Pashanabheda](/herb/pashanabheda/) (stone breaker) for kidney stones. Clinical studies have reported reduced stone recurrence.

herb/tamalaki.from: - Hepatoprotective and antiviral (Hepatitis B) properties extensively validated through in vitro and clinical studies, confirming traditional use in liver diseases (Yakrit Vikara)
herb/tamalaki.to: - Traditionally used in liver diseases (Yakrit Vikara). In vitro and clinical studies have reported hepatoprotective and antiviral (Hepatitis B) activity.

herb/tamalaki.from: - Anti-inflammatory and diuretic properties validated through multiple pharmacological studies, confirming traditional Ayurvedic uses in urinary and inflammatory conditions
herb/tamalaki.to: - Traditionally used in Ayurveda for urinary and inflammatory conditions. Pharmacological studies have reported anti-inflammatory and diuretic activity.

herb/souvarchala-lavana.from: - Gulma and Shula (abdominal tumor/colic pain): Bile-stimulating and smooth muscle-relaxing effects of sulfur compounds validate traditional use in abdominal pain and colic
herb/souvarchala-lavana.to: - Gulma and Shula (abdominal tumor/colic pain): traditionally used for abdominal pain and colic.

herb/souvarchala-lavana.from: - Vibandha (constipation): Bile secretion enhancement and mild osmotic effect from mineral content support traditional [laxative](/reference/laxative/) indication
- Pandu (anemia): Iron sulfide content providing bioavailable iron validates traditional use in anemia management as dietary supplement
herb/souvarchala-lavana.to: - Pandu (anemia): traditionally used as a dietary supplement in anemia.

herb/swarna-vasant-malti-ras.from: - Rejuvenative and [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/): The clinical study confirmed systemic bioavailability of gold and absence of acute toxicity, partially supporting the traditional Rasayana (rejuvenative) claim, though large-scale controlled trials are needed
herb/swarna-vasant-malti-ras.to: - Rejuvenative and [immunomodulatory](/reference/immunomodulatory/): traditionally used as a Rasayana (rejuvenative). A clinical study reported systemic bioavailability of gold and no acute toxicity. Larger controlled trials are needed.

herb/swarna-vasant-malti-ras.from: - Chronic fever and respiratory conditions: Traditional use in Jirna Jwara (chronic fever), Kasa (cough), and Shwasa (asthma) is empirically supported by clinical practice but lacks rigorous clinical trial validation
herb/swarna-vasant-malti-ras.to: - Chronic fever and respiratory conditions: traditionally used for Jirna Jwara (chronic fever), Kasa (cough), and Shwasa (asthma) in clinical practice. Rigorous clinical trials of these uses are lacking.

herb/surana.from: - Anti-hemorrhoidal efficacy validated through clinical trials showing significant symptom relief, confirming premier Ayurvedic indication as Arsha (piles) remedy
herb/surana.to: - Arsha (piles): traditionally used as a premier Ayurvedic remedy for piles. Clinical studies have reported reduced symptoms.

herb/surana.from: - [Hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) activity confirmed through experimental models, supporting traditional use in liver disorders
herb/surana.to: - [Hepatoprotective](/reference/hepatoprotective/) activity has been reported in experimental studies. Traditionally used in liver disorders.

herb/surana.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) properties validated in preclinical studies, confirming traditional use in Shotha (inflammation) and pain conditions
herb/surana.to: - Shotha (inflammation): traditionally used for inflammation and pain conditions. Preclinical studies have reported anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) activity.

herb/sphatika-bhasma.from: - Bleeding disorders (Raktapitta): Styptic and astringent properties well-documented in modern pharmacology, validating traditional hemostatic use
herb/sphatika-bhasma.to: - Bleeding disorders (Raktapitta): traditionally used to stop bleeding. Pharmacological studies have reported styptic and astringent properties.

herb/sphatika-bhasma.from: - Respiratory diseases (Kasa, Shwasa): Antibacterial activity against respiratory pathogens and mucosal-drying properties support traditional use for cough and bronchitis
herb/sphatika-bhasma.to: - Respiratory diseases (Kasa, Shwasa): traditionally used for cough and bronchitis. Studies have reported antibacterial activity against respiratory pathogens and mucosal-drying properties.

herb/sphatika-bhasma.from: - Skin diseases and wounds: Broad-spectrum antimicrobial and anti-biofilm activity validates traditional use for skin infections and wound management
herb/sphatika-bhasma.to: - Skin diseases and wounds: traditionally used for skin infections and wounds. Studies have reported broad-spectrum antimicrobial and anti-biofilm activity.

herb/swarna-parpati.from: - Rajayakshma (tuberculosis/chronic wasting diseases) - primary classical indication; supported by immunomodulatory and Rasayana properties of gold nanoparticles demonstrated in safety studies
herb/swarna-parpati.to: - Rajayakshma (tuberculosis/chronic wasting diseases): traditionally used for this condition, which is its primary classical indication. Safety studies have reported immunomodulatory properties of gold nanoparticles, which are traditionally regarded as Rasayana.

herb/swarna-parpati.from: - Chronic bronchial diseases and respiratory conditions - traditional use supported by the anti-inflammatory and immunoenhancing properties of [Swarna Bhasma](/herb/swarna-bhasma/) demonstrated in preclinical research
herb/swarna-parpati.to: - Chronic bronchial diseases and respiratory conditions: traditionally used for these conditions. Preclinical studies have reported anti-inflammatory and immunoenhancing properties of [Swarna Bhasma](/herb/swarna-bhasma/).

herb/sthneyaka.from: - Anticancer activity spectacularly validated - paclitaxel is among the most successful plant-derived anticancer drugs, used globally for ovarian, breast, lung, and Kaposi's sarcoma treatment
herb/sthneyaka.to: - Paclitaxel, a plant-derived anticancer drug from this plant, is used globally in ovarian, breast and lung cancer and in Kaposi's sarcoma.

herb/sthneyaka.from: - Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) properties validated in Ayurvedic context for regulated traditional use (under strict supervision), supporting kapha-pacifying indications described in classical texts
herb/sthneyaka.to: - Used in classical practice, under strict supervision, for kapha-pacifying indications described in classical texts. Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) properties have been described in the Ayurvedic context.

herb/sthneyaka.from: - Traditional use requires extreme caution: validated pharmacological activity exists but therapeutic window is extremely narrow, making unsupervised use potentially fatal
herb/sthneyaka.to: - Traditional use requires extreme caution. Pharmacological activity has been reported, but the therapeutic window is extremely narrow. Unsupervised use can be fatal.

herb/talisa.from: - [Bronchodilator](/reference/bronchodilator/) and antitussive activity validated through pharmacological studies showing calcium channel-mediated smooth muscle relaxation, confirming use in Kasa (cough) and Shwasa (asthma)
herb/talisa.to: - [Bronchodilator](/reference/bronchodilator/) and antitussive activity has been reported in pharmacological studies, linked to calcium channel-mediated smooth muscle relaxation. Traditionally used for Kasa (cough) and Shwasa (asthma).

herb/talisa.from: - Anti-inflammatory activity validated through in vivo models, supporting traditional use in respiratory inflammation
herb/talisa.to: - Traditionally used for respiratory inflammation. Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/talisa.from: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity supported by preclinical evidence, confirming traditional use in Jwara (fever)
herb/talisa.to: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) activity has been reported in preclinical studies. Traditionally used for Jwara (fever).

herb/takra.from: - Grahani Roga (malabsorption/IBS): Probiotic, sphingolipid, and digestive-stimulant mechanisms provide strong scientific basis for the classical primary indication of Takra
herb/takra.to: - Grahani Roga (malabsorption/IBS): used in classical practice as the primary indication of Takra.
