herb/takra.from: - Arsha (hemorrhoids/piles): Anti-inflammatory lactic acid bacteria and improved bowel regularity validate traditional use; Takra with Chitraka or [Pippali](/herb/pippali/) enhances efficacy
herb/takra.to: - Arsha (hemorrhoids/piles): traditionally used for Arsha. In classical practice, Takra is combined with Chitraka or [Pippali](/herb/pippali/).

herb/takra.from: - Shotha (edema): [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) properties of potassium-rich, light buttermilk and its ability to reduce Kapha accumulation support traditional anti-edema applications
herb/takra.to: - Shotha (edema): traditionally used for edema. Light buttermilk is classically regarded as [Diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) and as reducing Kapha accumulation.

herb/swarna-bhasma.from: - Immunomodulation and [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (rejuvenation): Validated by multiple studies showing enhanced immune cell activity, increased WBC counts, and improved adaptive immune responses in animal models
herb/swarna-bhasma.to: - Immunomodulation and [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (rejuvenation): traditionally used as a rasayana for rejuvenation. Animal studies have reported increased immune cell activity, higher WBC counts and stronger adaptive immune responses.

herb/swarna-bhasma.from: - Anti-diabetic activity: Gold nanoparticles demonstrated profound control over anti-oxidant enzymes and blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose) in diabetic mice models, supporting traditional use in Prameha (diabetes)
herb/swarna-bhasma.to: - Anti-diabetic activity: traditionally used in Prameha (diabetes). Animal studies in diabetic mice have reported that gold nanoparticles influenced antioxidant enzymes and blood [glucose](/glossary/compounds-d-g/#glucose).

herb/swarna-bhasma.from: - Rheumatoid arthritis management: Comprehensive review (2024) confirmed anti-inflammatory mechanisms via NF-kB pathway inhibition, validating traditional use in Amavata (joint inflammation)
herb/swarna-bhasma.to: - Rheumatoid arthritis: traditionally used in Amavata (joint inflammation). A review reported anti-inflammatory activity through NF-kB pathway inhibition.

herb/swarna-bhasma.from: - Nervous system disorders: Behavioral assessment in zebrafish and rat models confirmed no neurotoxicity and showed analgesic and anti-depressant activities, supporting use in neurological conditions
herb/swarna-bhasma.to: - Nervous system disorders: traditionally used for neurological conditions. Animal studies in zebrafish and rats have reported no neurotoxicity, along with analgesic and anti-depressant activity.

herb/udumbara.from: - Antidiabetic activity validated in alloxan and STZ-induced diabetic animal models with significant blood glucose reduction
herb/udumbara.to: - Animal studies using alloxan- and STZ-induced diabetic models have reported reduced blood glucose.

herb/udumbara.from: - Anti-diarrheal properties confirmed through castor oil-induced diarrhea models showing significant reduction in frequency and volume
herb/udumbara.to: - Animal studies using castor oil-induced diarrhea models have reported reduced frequency and volume of diarrhea.

herb/udumbara.from: - Wound healing activity demonstrated in excision and incision wound models with improved collagen deposition and epithelialization
herb/udumbara.to: - Animal studies using excision and incision wound models have reported improved collagen deposition and epithelialization.

herb/udumbara.from: - Gastroprotective activity validated against aspirin and ethanol-induced gastric ulcer models
herb/udumbara.to: - Animal studies have reported gastroprotective activity in aspirin- and ethanol-induced gastric ulcer models.

herb/tamra-bhasma.from: - Digestive disorders (Agnimandya): Multiple clinical studies confirmed efficacy in improving digestive function with no adverse effects at therapeutic doses
herb/tamra-bhasma.to: - Digestive disorders (Agnimandya): traditionally used for digestive disorders. Clinical studies have reported improved digestive function, with no adverse effects reported at the doses studied.

herb/tamra-bhasma.from: - Skin diseases (Kushtha): Antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties validated through in-vitro studies supporting traditional dermatological applications
herb/tamra-bhasma.to: - Skin diseases (Kushtha): traditionally used for skin diseases. In vitro studies have reported antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/tamra-bhasma.from: - Liver disorders (Yakrit Vikara): Hepatoprotective action demonstrated in animal models, though this is dose-dependent and reverses to hepatotoxicity at high doses
herb/tamra-bhasma.to: - Liver disorders (Yakrit Vikara): traditionally used for liver disorders. Animal studies have reported a liver-protective action that depended on dose, with liver toxicity reported at high doses.

herb/tankana-bhasma.from: - Respiratory disorders (Kasa, Shwasa): Anti-inflammatory activity (decreased TNF-alpha, IL-6) in animal models validates traditional use for cough and bronchitis
herb/tankana-bhasma.to: - Respiratory disorders (Kasa, Shwasa): traditionally used for cough and bronchitis. Animal studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity, with decreased TNF-alpha and IL-6.

herb/tankana-bhasma.from: - Skin disorders and acne: 18% acne severity reduction in dermatological study supports traditional topical applications
herb/tankana-bhasma.to: - Skin disorders and acne: traditionally applied topically for skin disorders and acne. A dermatological study reported reduced acne severity.

herb/tankana-bhasma.from: - Dysmenorrhea (Kashtartava): Emmenagogue action validated through traditional clinical observations, but pregnancy contraindication must be emphasized
herb/tankana-bhasma.to: - Dysmenorrhea (Kashtartava): traditionally used for its emmenagogue action, based on traditional clinical observation. It is contraindicated in pregnancy.

herb/tila.from: - Hepatoprotective activity validated through multiple in vivo studies and NRF2 pathway research, confirming traditional use in liver disorders
herb/tila.to: - Traditionally used for liver disorders. In vivo studies have reported hepatoprotective activity, and research has looked at the NRF2 pathway.

herb/tila.from: - Anti-inflammatory and wound healing properties confirmed through modern pharmacological studies, supporting traditional topical oil applications (Abhyanga)
herb/tila.to: - Traditionally applied as a topical oil in Abhyanga. Pharmacological studies have reported anti-inflammatory and wound healing properties.

herb/tila.from: - Cholesterol-lowering and [cardioprotective](/reference/cardioprotective/) effects validated through clinical and preclinical studies, confirming Ayurvedic use for heart health and as a [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)
herb/tila.to: - Used in Ayurveda for heart health and as a [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/). Clinical and preclinical studies have reported cholesterol-lowering and [cardioprotective](/reference/cardioprotective/) effects.

herb/tribhuvan-kirti-rasa.from: - Antipyretic in all types of fever (Jvara): The [Trikatu](/herb/trikatu/) and [Tulsi](/herb/tulsi/) components have well-documented antipyretic and anti-inflammatory properties validated in multiple pharmacological studies; the combined formulation's efficacy in fever is empirically well-established in clinical practice
herb/tribhuvan-kirti-rasa.to: - Jvara (all types of fever): traditionally used in classical practice for all types of fever. Pharmacological studies have reported antipyretic and anti-inflammatory activity for the [Trikatu](/herb/trikatu/) and [Tulsi](/herb/tulsi/) components.

herb/tribhuvan-kirti-rasa.from: - Respiratory infections (Pratishyaya - common cold): The diaphoretic, [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/), and immunostimulatory properties of [Tulsi](/herb/tulsi/), [Trikatu](/herb/trikatu/), and processed aconite provide a plausible multi-target mechanism for traditional use in upper respiratory infections
herb/tribhuvan-kirti-rasa.to: - Pratishyaya (common cold): traditionally used for upper respiratory infections. The formulation contains [Tulsi](/herb/tulsi/), [Trikatu](/herb/trikatu/), and processed aconite.

herb/trivrit.from: - Purgative use (Virechana) validated through stimulation of colonic peristalsis and fluid secretion in animal models
herb/trivrit.to: - Virechana (purgation): traditionally used as a purgative. Animal studies have reported stimulation of colonic peristalsis and fluid secretion.

herb/trivrit.from: - Anti-helminthic use (Krimighna) confirmed by in vitro activity against intestinal parasites including Ascaris and Taenia species
herb/trivrit.to: - Krimighna (anti-helminthic): traditionally used against intestinal worms. In vitro studies have reported activity against intestinal parasites, including Ascaris and Taenia species.

herb/trivrit.from: - Anti-inflammatory use supported by COX-2 and iNOS inhibition through scopoletin and lupeol in carrageenan-induced edema model
herb/trivrit.to: - Anti-inflammatory use: traditionally used for inflammation. An animal study using a carrageenan-induced edema model reported COX-2 and iNOS inhibition linked to scopoletin and lupeol.

herb/tapyadi-loha.from: - Pandu (anemia) and Kamla (jaundice-like conditions) - validated through traditional clinical use and supported by the known hematinic and hepatoprotective actions of constituent ingredients
herb/tapyadi-loha.to: - Pandu (anemia) and Kamla (jaundice-like conditions): traditionally used for these conditions in classical practice.

herb/tapyadi-loha.from: - Liver and spleen disorders (Yakrit-Pliha Roga) - traditional use supported by hepatoprotective properties of [Daruharidra](/herb/daruharidra/) ([berberine](/glossary/compounds-a-c/#berberine)), [Shilajit](/herb/shilajit/), and [Triphala](/herb/triphala/); 2024 toxicity study showed no hepatotoxicity
herb/tapyadi-loha.to: - Liver and spleen disorders (Yakrit-Pliha Roga): traditionally used for these conditions. Ingredients include [Daruharidra](/herb/daruharidra/) ([berberine](/glossary/compounds-a-c/#berberine)), [Shilajit](/herb/shilajit/), and [Triphala](/herb/triphala/). A toxicity study reported no liver toxicity.

herb/trivanga-bhasma.from: - Diabetes (Madhumeha): Anti-diabetic activity demonstrated in STZ-induced diabetic rat models with significant blood sugar reduction. However, lead toxicity risk undermines clinical applicability.
herb/trivanga-bhasma.to: - Diabetes (Madhumeha): traditionally used for diabetes. Animal studies in STZ-induced diabetic rat models have reported reduced blood sugar. However, the risk of lead toxicity limits its clinical applicability.

herb/trivanga-bhasma.from: - Urinary disorders (Mutra Roga): Traditional indication partially supported by component metal properties, but no specific clinical validation separating efficacy from toxicity
herb/trivanga-bhasma.to: - Urinary disorders (Mutra Roga): traditionally used for urinary disorders. No clinical study has separated its benefits from its toxicity.

herb/trivanga-bhasma.from: - Infertility (Vandhyatva): Reproductive support claimed from Vanga component, but lead content makes this use particularly dangerous for reproductive health
herb/trivanga-bhasma.to: - Infertility (Vandhyatva): traditionally used for infertility, with reproductive support attributed to the Vanga component. Its lead content makes this use particularly dangerous for reproductive health.

herb/twak-cinnamon.from: - Blood sugar regulation in diabetes - extensively validated by multiple RCTs and meta-analyses showing significant glycemic and HbA1c improvements
herb/twak-cinnamon.to: - Blood sugar regulation in diabetes: traditionally used for blood sugar regulation. Clinical trials and meta-analyses have reported improvements in blood glucose and HbA1c.

herb/twak-cinnamon.from: - Carminative and digestive aid for dyspepsia and flatulence - confirmed by ESCOP recommendations based on clinical evidence
herb/twak-cinnamon.to: - Carminative and digestive aid: traditionally used for dyspepsia and flatulence.

herb/twak-cinnamon.from: - Anti-inflammatory use for joint and muscle pain - supported by clinical evidence of reduced inflammatory markers (CRP, TNF-alpha, IL-6)
herb/twak-cinnamon.to: - Anti-inflammatory use: traditionally used for joint and muscle pain. Clinical studies have reported reduced inflammatory markers (CRP, TNF-alpha, IL-6).

herb/twak-cinnamon.from: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) use for infections - validated by in vitro and in vivo studies showing broad-spectrum activity of cinnamaldehyde
herb/twak-cinnamon.to: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) use: traditionally used for infections. In vitro and in vivo studies have reported broad-spectrum activity of cinnamaldehyde.

herb/twak-cinnamon.from: - Lipid-lowering for cardiovascular protection - confirmed by clinical trials showing reduced triglycerides, LDL-C, and total cholesterol
herb/twak-cinnamon.to: - Lipid lowering: traditionally used for cardiovascular health. Clinical trials have reported reduced triglycerides, LDL-C, and total cholesterol.

herb/tinduka.from: - Astringent and anti-diarrheal use validated through tannin content analysis and intestinal motility studies
herb/tinduka.to: - Traditionally used as an astringent and for diarrhea. Analytical studies have reported tannin content in the plant.

herb/tinduka.from: - Wound and ulcer treatment confirmed through [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity and healing promotion in preclinical models
herb/tinduka.to: - Traditionally used for wounds and ulcers. Preclinical studies have reported [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity and wound-healing activity.

herb/tinduka.from: - Anticancer potential validated through NSCLC immunotherapy studies and cytotoxicity assays
herb/tinduka.to: - Studied for anticancer potential. In vitro cytotoxicity assays have reported cytotoxic activity, and it has been examined in NSCLC immunotherapy research.

herb/tinduka.from: - Oral health (gargle for sore throat) use supported by antimicrobial and astringent properties of fruit extracts
herb/tinduka.to: - Traditionally used for oral health, as a gargle for sore throat. Laboratory studies have reported antimicrobial and astringent properties of fruit extracts.

herb/vanga-bhasma.from: - Male reproductive disorders (Vajikarana): Testicular regenerative potential demonstrated in animal studies, supporting aphrodisiac claims
herb/vanga-bhasma.to: - Male reproductive disorders (Vajikarana): traditionally used as an aphrodisiac. Animal studies have reported testicular regenerative potential.

herb/vanga-bhasma.from: - Urinary disorders (Prameha/Mutra Roga): Traditional use partially validated through inclusion in [Trivanga Bhasma](/herb/trivanga-bhasma/) studies showing urinary system benefits
herb/vanga-bhasma.to: - Urinary disorders (Prameha/Mutra Roga): traditionally used for urinary disorders. Studies of [Trivanga Bhasma](/herb/trivanga-bhasma/), which includes it, have reported benefits to the urinary system.

herb/vanga-bhasma.from: - Diabetes (Madhumeha): Anti-diabetic activity validated as component of [Trivanga Bhasma](/herb/trivanga-bhasma/) in multiple animal studies
herb/vanga-bhasma.to: - Diabetes (Madhumeha): traditionally used for diabetes. Animal studies of [Trivanga Bhasma](/herb/trivanga-bhasma/), which includes it, have reported anti-diabetic activity.

herb/vasant-kusumakar-rasa.from: - Anti-diabetic activity: Multiple preclinical studies (2020-2024) validate traditional use in Prameha (diabetes) showing dose-dependent blood glucose reduction, improved insulin sensitivity, and protection against diabetic complications including retinopathy, cardiomyopathy, and encephalopathy
herb/vasant-kusumakar-rasa.to: - Anti-diabetic activity: traditionally used for Prameha (diabetes). Preclinical studies have reported lower blood glucose, improved insulin sensitivity, and protection against diabetic complications including retinopathy, cardiomyopathy, and encephalopathy.

herb/vasant-kusumakar-rasa.from: - Rejuvenative ([Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)) action: Traditional use as a rejuvenative tonic partially validated by studies showing antioxidant properties and multi-organ protective effects in diabetic animal models
herb/vasant-kusumakar-rasa.to: - Rejuvenative ([Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)) action: traditionally used as a rejuvenative tonic. Animal studies in diabetic models have reported antioxidant properties and protective effects across multiple organs.

herb/vatagajankush-rasa.from: - Sciatica (Gridhrasi): Clinical study (2023) showed significant symptom improvement, validating the traditional use in Vata-predominant nerve pain conditions
herb/vatagajankush-rasa.to: - Sciatica (Gridhrasi): traditionally used for Vata-predominant nerve pain conditions. A clinical study reported improvement in symptoms.

herb/vatagajankush-rasa.from: - Joint pain and arthritis (Sandhivata/Amavata): The multi-mineral anti-inflammatory composition provides mechanistic support for traditional use in musculoskeletal disorders; clinical practice experience supports efficacy
herb/vatagajankush-rasa.to: - Joint pain and arthritis (Sandhivata/Amavata): used in classical practice for musculoskeletal disorders.

herb/ushira.from: - Anxiolytic and nootropic (memory-enhancing) effects validated in mouse models, confirming traditional Ayurvedic use as a brain tonic (Medhya)
herb/ushira.to: - Traditionally used as a brain tonic (Medhya). Studies in mice have reported anxiolytic and nootropic (memory-enhancing) effects.

herb/ushira.from: - Anti-inflammatory and cooling properties validated through pharmacological studies, confirming traditional use in Pitta disorders and burning sensation (Daha)
herb/ushira.to: - Traditionally used for Pitta disorders and burning sensation (Daha). Pharmacological studies have reported anti-inflammatory and cooling properties.

herb/ushira.from: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity confirmed against multiple bacterial and fungal strains, supporting traditional use in skin infections and wound healing
herb/ushira.to: - Traditionally used for skin infections and wounds. [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity against multiple bacterial and fungal strains has been reported in studies.

herb/varatika-bhasma.from: - Hyperacidity and gastritis (Amlapitta): Antacid activity confirmed through in-vitro studies and clinical observations. Effective acid neutralization validated.
herb/varatika-bhasma.to: - Hyperacidity and gastritis (Amlapitta): traditionally used for hyperacidity and gastritis. In vitro studies and clinical observations have reported antacid and acid-neutralizing activity.

herb/varatika-bhasma.from: - Intestinal worms (Krimi Roga): Anti-parasitic action attributed to alkaline pH creation, supported by traditional empirical evidence
herb/varatika-bhasma.to: - Intestinal worms (Krimi Roga): traditionally used for intestinal worms. Traditional accounts attribute this use to the creation of an alkaline pH.

herb/varatika-bhasma.from: - Indigestion and bloating (Ajirna, Adhmana): Digestive improvement through acid-base balance restoration confirmed in clinical practice
herb/varatika-bhasma.to: - Indigestion and bloating (Ajirna, Adhmana): used in classical practice for indigestion and bloating. Traditional accounts explain this use as restoring acid-base balance.

herb/vaikranta-bhasma.from: - Diabetes (Prameha): Traditional anti-diabetic indication supported by multi-mineral composition known to affect glucose metabolism, but specific clinical validation limited
- Anemia: Iron-rich composition supports traditional use for blood deficiency conditions, validated by physicochemical iron content analysis
herb/vaikranta-bhasma.to: - Anemia: traditionally used for blood deficiency conditions. Physicochemical analysis has reported iron content in the preparation.

herb/vaikranta-bhasma.from: - Respiratory disorders (Shwasa, Kasa): Traditional use for asthma and chronic cough supported by anti-inflammatory properties of mineral constituents
herb/vaikranta-bhasma.to: - Respiratory disorders (Shwasa, Kasa): traditionally used for asthma and chronic cough.

herb/vaikranta-bhasma.from: - SOURCE STANDARDIZATION: Variations between tourmaline sources affect composition and potentially safety. Only black tourmaline (schorl) validated for medicinal use.
herb/vaikranta-bhasma.to: - SOURCE STANDARDIZATION: variations between tourmaline sources affect composition and possibly safety. Only black tourmaline (schorl) is traditionally used for medicinal preparation.

herb/vasa.from: - Bronchodilatory and antitussive use (Kasa-Shwasahara) extensively validated through clinical and pharmacological studies confirming vasicine's expectorant mechanism
herb/vasa.to: - Kasa-Shwasahara: traditionally used as a bronchodilator and antitussive. Clinical and pharmacological studies have reported an expectorant action of vasicine.

herb/vasa.from: - [Hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic) use (Raktapitta treatment) confirmed by vasoconstriction and platelet aggregation enhancement by vasicinone in bleeding models
herb/vasa.to: - [Hemostatic](/glossary/pharmacology/#hemostatic) use: traditionally used for Raktapitta. Studies in bleeding models have reported vasoconstriction and increased platelet aggregation with vasicinone.

herb/vasa.from: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) use for respiratory infections supported by antibacterial activity against common respiratory pathogens (S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae)
herb/vasa.to: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) use: traditionally used for respiratory infections. Studies have reported antibacterial activity against common respiratory pathogens (S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae).

herb/vasa.from: In silico and in vitro studies validated vasicine as potent [bronchodilator](/reference/bronchodilator/) with favorable binding to beta-2 adrenergic receptor and muscarinic M3 receptor antagonism.
herb/vasa.to: In silico and in vitro studies have reported [bronchodilator](/reference/bronchodilator/) activity for vasicine, with favorable binding to the beta-2 adrenergic receptor and muscarinic M3 receptor antagonism.

herb/vanapsa.from: - Respiratory disorders and cough (Kasa-hara) - validated through confirmed expectorant, anti-inflammatory, and [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) properties
herb/vanapsa.to: - Respiratory disorders and cough (Kasa-hara): traditionally used for these conditions. Studies have reported expectorant, anti-inflammatory, and [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) properties.

herb/vanapsa.from: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) (Jvarahara) - confirmed diaphoretic and antipyretic activities in pharmacological studies
herb/vanapsa.to: - [Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) (Jvarahara): traditionally used for this purpose. Pharmacological studies have reported diaphoretic and antipyretic activities.

herb/vanapsa.from: - Skin health and complexion (Varnya) - traditional use in face preparations supported by anti-inflammatory and [antioxidant](/reference/antioxidant/) data
herb/vanapsa.to: - Skin health and complexion (Varnya): traditionally used in face preparations. Studies have reported anti-inflammatory and [antioxidant](/reference/antioxidant/) activity.

herb/vanapsa.from: - Sleep aid and [anxiolytic](/reference/anxiolytic/) (Nidrajanana) - traditional sedative use partially supported by flavonoid-mediated CNS-calming effects
herb/vanapsa.to: - Sleep aid and [anxiolytic](/reference/anxiolytic/) (Nidrajanana): traditionally used as a sedative. Studies have reported calming effects on the central nervous system linked to flavonoids.

herb/vajra-bhasma.from: - Cancer and tumors (Arbuda): Animal studies showed significant tumor volume reduction, metastasis inhibition, and increased survival in tumor-bearing animals
herb/vajra-bhasma.to: - Cancer and tumors (Arbuda): traditionally used for Arbuda in classical practice. Animal studies have reported reduced tumor volume, less metastasis, and longer survival in tumor-bearing animals.

herb/vajra-bhasma.from: - Immune deficiency: Immunomodulatory activity confirmed through enhanced NK cell activity and lymphocyte proliferation in preclinical models
herb/vajra-bhasma.to: - Immune deficiency: preclinical studies have reported immunomodulatory activity, including increased NK cell activity and lymphocyte proliferation.

herb/vajra-bhasma.from: - Tuberculosis (Rajayakshma): Anti-inflammatory and immune-enhancing properties provide mechanistic basis, though specific clinical validation for TB is limited
herb/vajra-bhasma.to: - Tuberculosis (Rajayakshma): traditionally used for Rajayakshma in classical practice. Anti-inflammatory and immune-enhancing activity has been reported, but clinical research specific to TB is limited.

herb/vajra-bhasma.from: - HIGH SAFETY MARGIN: Murine toxicological assessments show no hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, or genotoxicity at therapeutic equivalent doses when prepared through validated methods
herb/vajra-bhasma.to: - Safety: toxicology studies in mice have reported no hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, or genotoxicity at doses equivalent to those used in practice, for preparations made by validated methods.

herb/varshabhu.from: - Diuretic (Mutrala) - strongly validated through multiple pharmacological studies showing significant diuretic activity
herb/varshabhu.to: - Diuretic (Mutrala): traditionally used as a diuretic. Pharmacological studies have reported diuretic activity.

herb/varshabhu.from: - Hepatoprotective (Yakrit-shodhana) - confirmed through studies showing protection against CCl4 and paracetamol-induced liver damage
herb/varshabhu.to: - Hepatoprotective (Yakrit-shodhana): traditionally used for the liver. Experimental studies have reported protection against chemically induced and paracetamol-induced liver damage.

herb/varshabhu.from: - Anti-inflammatory and anti-edema (Shotha-hara) - validated through carrageenan-induced paw edema and cotton pellet granuloma models
herb/varshabhu.to: - Anti-inflammatory and anti-edema (Shotha-hara): traditionally used for swelling and inflammation. Animal studies using carrageenan-induced paw edema and cotton pellet granuloma models have reported anti-inflammatory activity.

herb/varshabhu.from: - Rejuvenative ([Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)) - supported by antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and anti-aging pharmacological data
herb/varshabhu.to: - Rejuvenative ([Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/)): traditionally used as a rejuvenative. Pharmacological studies have reported antioxidant, immunomodulatory and anti-aging activity.

herb/vida-lavana.from: - Anaha (flatulence/bloating): Sulfide-mediated gut motility modulation and anti-fermentative action scientifically validate traditional primary indication
herb/vida-lavana.to: - Anaha (flatulence/bloating): traditionally used for flatulence and bloating as a primary indication.

herb/vida-lavana.from: - Deepana-Pachana (digestive stimulant-digestant): Dual mechanism of acid stimulation and alkaline buffering supports classical digestive application
herb/vida-lavana.to: - Deepana-Pachana (digestive stimulant-digestant): used in classical practice as a digestive stimulant and digestant.

herb/vida-lavana.from: - Amlapitta (hyperacidity): Mild alkaline properties from processing provide antacid effect, partially validating traditional use in acid dyspepsia
herb/vida-lavana.to: - Amlapitta (hyperacidity): traditionally used for hyperacidity and acid dyspepsia.

herb/yavakshara.from: - Amlapitta (hyperacidity/GERD): Direct acid-neutralizing mechanism scientifically validates primary traditional indication; comparable to modern antacid drugs
herb/yavakshara.to: - Amlapitta (hyperacidity/GERD): traditionally used as a primary remedy for hyperacidity.

herb/yavakshara.from: - Ashmari (urinary calculi/kidney stones): Alkalinization of urine and crystal dissolution properties provide strong scientific basis for traditional anti-urolithiatic use
herb/yavakshara.to: - Ashmari (urinary calculi/kidney stones): traditionally used for urinary calculi.

herb/yavakshara.from: - Gulma and Anaha (abdominal distension/bloating): Acid neutralization reduces bloating from acid-mediated fermentation; improved digestion reduces gas production
herb/yavakshara.to: - Gulma and Anaha (abdominal distension/bloating): traditionally used for abdominal distension and bloating.

herb/vidanga.from: - Anthelmintic activity confirmed by in vitro and clinical studies in children with Ascaris infections.
herb/vidanga.to: - In vitro and clinical studies have reported anthelmintic activity. The clinical work was in children with Ascaris infections.

herb/vidanga.from: - [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) properties validated against multiple bacterial strains.
herb/vidanga.to: - Laboratory studies have reported [Antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity against multiple bacterial strains.

herb/vidanga.from: - Anti-inflammatory activity supported by NF-kB inhibition studies.
herb/vidanga.to: - Studies have reported anti-inflammatory activity involving NF-kB inhibition.

herb/vidanga.from: - [Anticancer](/reference/anticancer/) potential validated through XIAP inhibition and multi-pathway modulation in preclinical models.
herb/vidanga.to: - Preclinical studies have reported [Anticancer](/reference/anticancer/) potential involving XIAP inhibition and modulation of multiple pathways.

herb/vidanga.from: - Antioxidant activity confirmed by DPPH and other radical scavenging assays.
herb/vidanga.to: - Antioxidant activity has been reported in DPPH and other radical scavenging assays.

herb/vyaghri-haritaki.from: - Antitussive and anti-asthmatic efficacy validated through pharmacological studies confirming bronchodilatory and cough-suppressant properties, supporting premier use in Kasa (cough) and Shwasa (asthma)
herb/vyaghri-haritaki.to: - Traditionally used as a premier remedy in Kasa (cough) and Shwasa (asthma). Pharmacological studies have reported bronchodilatory and cough-suppressant properties.

herb/vyaghri-haritaki.from: - Treatment of Pratishyaya (chronic rhinitis/sinusitis) supported by anti-inflammatory and [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) properties of constituent herbs
herb/vyaghri-haritaki.to: - Traditionally used for Pratishyaya (chronic rhinitis/sinusitis). Anti-inflammatory and [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) properties have been reported for its constituent herbs.

herb/vyaghri-haritaki.from: - Mild laxative and detoxification role validated through Haritaki's well-established purgative pharmacology, confirming traditional use in maintaining digestive health
herb/vyaghri-haritaki.to: - Traditionally used as a mild laxative and for detoxification, to maintain digestive health. Pharmacological studies have reported a purgative action for Haritaki.

herb/yashada-bhasma.from: - Diabetes (Prameha/Madhumeha): Strong validation through multiple studies showing 16-33% improvement in glucose parameters, inspiring modern nanomedicine development
herb/yashada-bhasma.to: - Diabetes (Prameha/Madhumeha): traditionally used for Prameha and Madhumeha. Several studies have reported improvements in glucose parameters. It has also drawn interest in modern nanomedicine research.

herb/yashada-bhasma.from: - Eye diseases (Netra Roga): Zinc's role in retinal health and macular degeneration prevention well-established in modern ophthalmology, supporting traditional Ayurvedic eye disease claims
herb/yashada-bhasma.to: - Eye diseases (Netra Roga): traditionally used for Netra Roga. Modern ophthalmology research has described a role for zinc in retinal health and in macular degeneration.

herb/yashada-bhasma.from: - Skin disorders and wound healing: Zinc's essential role in wound healing, collagen synthesis, and skin integrity validated by extensive modern dermatological research
herb/yashada-bhasma.to: - Skin disorders and wound healing: traditionally used for skin disorders and wounds. Dermatological research has described a role for zinc in wound healing, collagen synthesis and skin integrity.

herb/yavani.from: - Digestive stimulant and carminative (Deepana-Pachana) - strongly validated through enhanced enzyme secretion and antispasmodic activity
herb/yavani.to: - Digestive stimulant and carminative (Deepana-Pachana): traditionally used to stimulate digestion and as a carminative. Studies have reported increased enzyme secretion and antispasmodic activity.

herb/yavani.from: - Anti-flatulence (Anaha-nashaka) - confirmed through antispasmodic and carminative effects reducing bloating and gas
herb/yavani.to: - Anti-flatulence (Anaha-nashaka): traditionally used for bloating and gas. Studies have reported antispasmodic and carminative effects.

herb/yavani.from: - Anti-cough and respiratory (Kasa-Shvasa-hara) - validated bronchodilatory and [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) effects
herb/yavani.to: - Anti-cough and respiratory (Kasa-Shvasa-hara): traditionally used for cough and breathing complaints. Studies have reported bronchodilatory and [expectorant](/reference/expectorant/) effects.

herb/yavani.from: - Anti-parasitic and anthelmintic (Krimighna) - confirmed nematicidal and anthelmintic activities of thymol against intestinal parasites
herb/yavani.to: - Anti-parasitic and anthelmintic (Krimighna): traditionally used against intestinal parasites. Studies have reported nematicidal and anthelmintic activity of thymol.

herb/vrikshamla.from: - Anti-obesity and weight management use partially validated through HCA-mediated lipogenesis inhibition in preclinical models; clinical evidence is mixed
herb/vrikshamla.to: - Traditionally used for obesity and weight control. Preclinical studies have reported that HCA inhibits lipogenesis. Clinical study results have been mixed.

herb/vrikshamla.from: - Digestive and carminative use validated through gastroprotective and anti-ulcerogenic studies
herb/vrikshamla.to: - Traditionally used as a digestive and carminative. Studies have reported gastroprotective and anti-ulcerogenic activity.

herb/vrikshamla.from: - Anti-inflammatory use confirmed through garcinol-mediated COX-2 and LOX inhibition in preclinical models
herb/vrikshamla.to: - Traditionally used for inflammation. Preclinical studies have reported that garcinol inhibits COX-2 and LOX.

herb/vrikshamla.from: - Cardioprotective use supported by antioxidant and anti-hyperlipidemic effects in high-fat diet animal models
herb/vrikshamla.to: - Traditionally used to protect the heart. Animal studies using a high-fat diet have reported antioxidant and anti-hyperlipidemic effects.

Included in Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India; recognized in Indian traditional medicine systems; limited WHO-specific documentation; further clinical validation encouraged."
herb/vidarikand.to: answer: "Vidarikand (Pueraria tuberosa (Willd.) DC.) is a plant drug, also called Vidarikamda, from the Fabaceae family. It is included in the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India and recognized in Indian traditional medicine systems. WHO-specific documentation is limited, and further clinical research is encouraged."

herb/vidarikand.from: whoStatus: "Included in Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India; recognized in Indian traditional medicine systems; limited WHO-specific documentation; further clinical validation encouraged"
herb/vidarikand.to: whoStatus: "Included in the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India; recognized in Indian traditional medicine systems; limited WHO-specific documentation; further clinical research encouraged"

herb/vidarikand.from: - [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (rejuvenative) and [Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana) ([aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac)) use supported by [nootropic](/glossary/pharmacology/#nootropic), [adaptogenic](/reference/adaptogenic/), and reproductive health improvement in animal models
herb/vidarikand.to: - Traditionally used as a [Rasayana](/reference/rasayana/) (rejuvenative) and [Vajikarana](/glossary/pharmacology/#vajikarana) ([aphrodisiac](/glossary/pharmacology/#aphrodisiac)). Animal studies have reported [nootropic](/glossary/pharmacology/#nootropic), [adaptogenic](/reference/adaptogenic/), and reproductive health effects.

herb/vidarikand.from: - Menopausal symptom relief validated by RCT showing 45% reduction in hot flushes with standardized extract
herb/vidarikand.to: - Menopausal symptoms: a randomized clinical study of a standardized extract reported fewer hot flushes.

herb/vidarikand.from: - Balya (strength-promoting) use supported by improved muscle recovery markers (creatine kinase) in athletic pilot studies
herb/vidarikand.to: - Balya (strength-promoting): traditionally used to promote strength. Pilot studies in athletes reported improved muscle recovery markers (creatine kinase).

herb/yava.from: - Prameha (diabetes/metabolic disorders): Beta-glucan mediated glycemic control and insulin sensitization strongly validate the classical designation as the best grain for diabetes; FDA-approved health claim supports this
herb/yava.to: - Prameha (diabetes/metabolic disorders): classically regarded as the best grain for prameha. Studies on barley beta-glucan have reported effects on blood glucose and insulin sensitivity.

herb/yava.from: - Sthaulya and Medoroga (obesity and lipid disorders): Lekhana (scraping) action validated by beta-glucan's bile acid trapping, cholesterol reduction, and fat metabolism enhancement
herb/yava.to: - Sthaulya and Medoroga (obesity and lipid disorders): traditionally used for its lekhana (scraping) action. Studies on beta-glucan have reported bile acid binding, cholesterol-lowering activity and effects on fat metabolism.

herb/yava.from: - Mutra Roga (urinary disorders): Barley water (Yava Kshira) as a traditional kidney tonic validated by [diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) properties and anti-urolithiatic activity of barley alkaline compounds
herb/yava.to: - Mutra Roga (urinary disorders): barley water (Yava Kshira) is traditionally used as a kidney tonic. Studies have reported [diuretic](/reference/diuretic/) properties and anti-urolithiatic activity for alkaline compounds in barley.

herb/vatsanabha.from: - **[Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) (Jvarahara).** Aconitum [alkaloids](/glossary/compounds-1-a/#alkaloids) at sub-toxic doses suppress prostaglandin-mediated fever pathways. Traditional use as febrifuge validated by in vivo studies showing dose-dependent antipyretic activity comparable to paracetamol in animal models.
herb/vatsanabha.to: - **[Antipyretic](/reference/antipyretic/) (Jvarahara).** Traditionally used as a febrifuge. Animal studies have reported dose-dependent antipyretic activity, comparable to paracetamol.

herb/vatsanabha.from: - **Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) (Vedanasthapana, Shothahara).** Low-dose processed aconitine preparations show significant anti-inflammatory activity by suppressing NF-kB pathway and COX-2 expression. Analgesic effect mediated through sodium channel modulation at sub-toxic doses. Used in traditional medicine across Himalayan regions for rheumatic pain.
herb/vatsanabha.to: - **Anti-inflammatory and [analgesic](/reference/analgesic/) (Vedanasthapana, Shothahara).** Traditionally used across Himalayan regions for rheumatic pain.

herb/yuthika.from: - Wound healing (Vrana Ropana): Validated by in vitro study demonstrating potent wound healing activity with enhanced collagen synthesis from ethanolic leaf extract
herb/yuthika.to: - Wound healing (Vrana Ropana): traditionally used for wound healing. An in vitro study of an ethanolic leaf extract reported wound healing activity and increased collagen synthesis.

herb/yuthika.from: - Skin disease treatment (especially ringworm): Traditional root application supported by demonstrated antimicrobial activity, though limited clinical evidence
herb/yuthika.to: - Skin disease (especially ringworm): the root is traditionally applied for skin disease, especially ringworm. Antimicrobial activity has been reported, though clinical evidence is limited.

herb/yuthika.from: - Fragrance and aromatherapy for skin health: Validated by identified volatile compound profile including cis-jasmone, linalool, and benzyl acetate with neuromodulatory and skin-soothing properties
herb/yuthika.to: - Fragrance and aromatherapy for skin health: traditionally used in fragrance and aromatherapy. Its volatile compounds have been identified, including cis-jasmone, linalool, and benzyl acetate. Neuromodulatory and skin-soothing properties have been reported for these compounds.

herb/ashwagandha.from: **Bioavailability:** Moderate oral bioavailability for withanolides (~20-30% for withaferin A). Withanoside IV is a prodrug converted to sominone by intestinal glucosidases. Cyclodextrin complexation improves withanolide solubility 3-5x. KSM-66 (full-spectrum root extract) and Sensoril (root + leaf extract) show clinically validated bioavailability. Milk (Kshirapaka) as anupana enhances absorption of lipophilic withanolides by 2-3x. [Piperine](/reference/piperine/) co-administration increases bioavailability by 30-40%. Phytosome technology (withanolide-phospholipid complex) shows 5x enhancement.
herb/ashwagandha.to: **Bioavailability:** Moderate oral bioavailability for withanolides (~20-30% for withaferin A). Withanoside IV is a prodrug converted to sominone by intestinal glucosidases. Cyclodextrin complexation improves withanolide solubility 3-5x. Proprietary root, and root-and-leaf, extracts have been used in clinical studies. Milk (Kshirapaka) as anupana enhances absorption of lipophilic withanolides by 2-3x. [Piperine](/reference/piperine/) co-administration increases bioavailability by 30-40%. Phytosome technology (withanolide-phospholipid complex) shows 5x enhancement.

glossary/concepts-a-m.from: **Bioavailability:** Peristrophe bicalyculata - limited modern pharmacokinetic data. Contains [flavonoids](/reference/flavonoids/), [alkaloids](/glossary/compounds-1-a/#alkaloids), and [terpenoids](/glossary/compounds-t-z/#terpenoids). Flavonoid components likely have moderate bioavailability similar to other Acanthaceae family members. Alkaloid fraction may contribute to observed biological activities. Traditional decoction preparation is the validated route of administration.
glossary/concepts-a-m.to: **Bioavailability:** Peristrophe bicalyculata - limited modern pharmacokinetic data. Contains [flavonoids](/reference/flavonoids/), [alkaloids](/glossary/compounds-1-a/#alkaloids), and [terpenoids](/glossary/compounds-t-z/#terpenoids). Flavonoid components likely have moderate bioavailability similar to other Acanthaceae family members. Alkaloid fraction may contribute to observed biological activities. Decoction is the traditional route of administration.

herb/pilu.from: **Standardized Extract:** Salvadora persica bark extract (8:1) standardized to salvadorine >1%, total [isothiocyanates](/glossary/compounds-g-l/#isothiocyanates) >0.5%, fluoride content documented. Stem aqueous extract for dental formulations with validated [antimicrobial](/reference/antimicrobial/) activity (MIC testing).
